rules.title: Leader
rules.description: The warband has no fixed leader. When it is raised, mark each Hero except the Imperial Captain with a number from 1 to 5. Roll a D6 before each battle: the Hero whose number is rolled leads the warband for that battle. The Imperial Captain can never lead, so the warband may go into a battle with no leader.

rules.title: Rivalries
rules.description:
While the Dwarf leads, the Elf will not stay within 6" of him and so cannot use his Leadership, though he may join a combat the Dwarf is in.

While the Elf leads, the Dwarf will not stay within 6" of him and so cannot use his Leadership, though he may join a combat the Elf is in.

While the Wizard leads, the Barbarian will not stay within 6" of him and so cannot use his Leadership, though he may join a combat the Wizard is in.

While the Barbarian leads, the Wizard will not stay within 6" of him and so cannot use his Leadership, though he may join a combat the Barbarian is in.

While the Imperial Noble leads, none of this applies.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The warband may hire these hired swords: Dwarf Troll Slayer, Freelancer (without his horse), Warlock, Duellist, Elf Ranger, Halfling Scout, Pit Fighter, Tilean Marksman and Imperial Assassin.

specials.name: Hatred
specials.description: The Elf hates Dark Elves.

specials.name: Seeker
specials.description: If the Elf is not taken out of action during the battle, you may change one dice of the exploration sequence by +1 or -1.

specials.name: Dim-witted
specials.description: While the Barbarian leads the warband, his Leadership counts as 7 for warband members within 6" and for Rout tests.

specials.name: Never Armoured
specials.description: The Barbarian never wears armour.

specials.name: Honourable
specials.description: The Imperial Noble never attacks an opponent who is knocked down or stunned.

specials.name: Family Heirloom
specials.description:
The Family Heirloom is a sword or a pistol his family has held a long time. Roll a D6 for it when the warband is raised:

D6 | Result
1-2 | The Noble may re-roll his first failed Psychology test in a battle.
3-4 | The Noble causes fear in Orcs, Goblins and Skaven.
5-6 | The Noble may re-roll one dice in a battle.

specials.name: Hard to Kill
specials.description: A Dwarf is taken out of action only on a 6 on the Injury chart: 1-2 is knocked down, 3-5 stunned and 6 out of action.

specials.name: Hard Head
specials.description: Dwarfs ignore the special rules of clubs, maces and the like.

specials.name: Mixed Bunch
specials.description: When a Cannon Fodder gets the Lad's Got Talent result he becomes an Imperial Captain. He picks two skills from any of the Adventurers' skill tables, but not the special ones, and keeps the Cannon Fodder equipment list. The warband may never hold more than one Imperial Captain.

rules.title: May Hire
rules.description: The warband hires no hired swords. The only models it may take on are the dramatis personae Im Abav Yub and Gaz Er Unga Og.

rules.title: Indigenous
rules.description: The warband suffers no movement penalty from the weather, and halves any Initiative reduction the weather table calls for (a reduction of 2 becomes 1, a reduction of 1 becomes none). Sight, shooting and hailstorms affect them as they affect anyone else.

rules.title: No Blackpowder
rules.description: No warrior in the warband may use a blackpowder weapon, even if a skill he has would otherwise let him.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior in the warband within 6" of the Chief may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Lad's Got Talent
specials.description: When a Hunter rolls That Lad's Got Talent, the new Hero takes Shooting and Speed as his skill lists.

specials.name: Lad's Got Talent (Warrior)
specials.description: When a Warrior rolls That Lad's Got Talent, the new Hero takes Combat and Strength as his skill lists.

rules.title: Students
rules.description: No more than half of the warband may be Students.

rules.title: Solemn Duty
rules.description: The warband may not take on a hired sword or dramatis persona who can cast spells.

rules.title: Beyond Reproach
rules.description: The warband may not ally with a warband that holds members or hirelings who are Undead, possessed, daemonic, mutated or evil, and may take on no hired sword or dramatis persona who is.

rules.title: Perils of Casting
rules.description:
A wizard casting Common Magic who rolls two 1s suffers a miscast and rolls at once on the table below. No change to the dice cancels a miscast, re-rolls included, though a re-roll may cause one.

2D6 | Result
2 | The wizard is taken out of action.
3 | The wizard is stupid. Roll a D6 after the battle: on a 2 or more the effect ends.
4 | The wizard may cast no spell for the rest of the battle.
5-6 | The spell is cast on the wizard himself. Any choice it calls for is made by the player to his left.
7 | Nothing happens beyond the spell failing.
8-9 | The wizard is thrown D6" in a random direction and lands knocked down.
10-11 | The wizard may cast no spell in his next shooting phase. He may use missile weapons as normal.
12 | Pick a warband at random from those with a caster, then a caster within it at random. That caster may cast one spell of his choice for free, with no roll to cast; everything else follows the normal rules.

rules.title: The Colleges
rules.description:
A Mage picks one College of magic, which he may never abandon. Each College changes his Common Magic as follows.

Amber: the target of Buff causes fear. The wizard also knows Children of the Wild, which works as Children of the Horned Rat but summons woodland animals, using the giant rat profile. De-buff cast on an animal sets the target's Movement to 0 while it lasts.

Amethyst: Blast 2 ignores armour saves. A model taken out of action by Blast 1 cannot be raised by Necromancy. Unsaved wounds from Blast 2 and Blast 3 are drained to the caster, who may go above his starting and racial maximum Wounds until the end of the battle. Only living models are affected by Blast 2 and Blast 3.

Bright: every Blast spell counts as flaming. The target of Buff causes flaming hits in close combat. De-buff causes a Strength 0 flaming hit for each failed recovery test. A fighter of either side who hits a warded model in close combat suffers a Strength 0 flaming hit for each hit he scores.

Celestial: Buff grants re-rolls of missed hits in the close combat and shooting phases. Ward grants re-rolls of failed saves and characteristic tests. De-buff forces re-rolls of successful hits in the close combat and shooting phases. The wizard also knows Scrying, difficulty automatic, which alters one dice by +1 or -1 in the exploration phase.

Gold: Blast 1 counts as flaming. Blast 2 is Strength 3 against a target in light armour and Strength 4 against one in heavy armour; Blast 3 is Strength 4 and Strength 5 the same way; both ignore armour saves. Against a target in neither, both are Strength 1. Add +1 Strength if the target wears a helmet. The wizard may also, instead of searching for rare trade, try to make D3 units of Flash Powder, D3 units of Superior Blackpowder or one Fire Bomb, succeeding on a D6 roll of 4 or more.

Grey: the target of Buff causes fear and may make a normal move or charge at once when the spell is cast. The target of Ward may fly up to 12" in the movement phase instead of moving or charging, and counts as charging if that brings him into base contact with an enemy. The wizard may also adjust a mission roll by +1 or -1 after it is rolled; where more than one model may, the highest Leadership test chooses the order.

Jade: Blast spells are +1 Strength if the target is within 1" of a terrain feature that gives cover without being a building, or of difficult, very difficult or impassable terrain. De-buff halves the target's Movement. Buff doubles the target's Toughness and halves his Movement and Initiative. Ward heals the model to full on the turn it is first cast. After serious injuries are rolled, one result of 36 or less is ignored on a D6 roll of 3 or more.

Light: Blast spells are +1 Strength against Undead, daemonic and possessed models. A living model hit by Blast 1 must also pass an Initiative test or be dazzled, counting as Weapon Skill 1 in its next close combat phase. Blast 2 and Blast 3 cause one flaming hit. Ward heals the model 1 wound and stands him up on the turn it is first cast, with no close combat penalty for standing up. Buff makes every model within 8" of the target immune to fear.

Flaming hits: a model that suffers an unsaved flaming hit is set on fire on a D6 roll of 5 or more. It takes a Strength 4 hit in each recovery phase; if it survives, roll a D6, and on a 4 or more the fire goes out. Any unengaged friendly model in contact with it that earns experience may roll as well, and a 4 or more from any of them puts the fire out. A burning model flees in a random direction under the normal rules for fleeing.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior in the warband within 6" of the Arch-Mage may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Learned
specials.description: The Arch-Mage starts with one Common Magic spell of your choice and one Common Magic spell chosen at random.

specials.name: Very Talented
specials.description: A Student who rolls That Lad's Got Talent becomes a Mage. Pick two skill lists for him as normal; he also takes the warband's special skills. In place of rolling on the hero's advance table, pick a College of magic for him and a Common Magic spell of your choice. A Mage is recruited no other way, has no hire cost and buys from the Wizard equipment list.

specials.name: Trained to a Pattern
specials.description: A Soldier takes only the lines of the Warrior list marked for him. A Soldier promoted to a Hero who learns Weapons Training or Weapons Expert may be equipped as those skills allow.

rules.title: Isolationists
rules.description: The Amazons are constantly battling against the predations of the Lizardmen and greedy treasure-seeking Norse. Amazon culture reflects their dislike and distrust of outsiders and in battle they are particularly savage. Amazons get to re-roll any attack rolls that miss in the first round of combat against Lizardmen and Norse.

rules.title: Sacrifice
rules.description: The Amazons are quick to sacrifice any captive to their gods. The Amazons follow the rules for Possessed in the Rulebook when it comes to captives. lf an Amazon Warband captures a Lizardman, they may sacrifice him as normal, plus get a free Skins and Charms.

rules.title: Norse Enmity
rules.description: When facing a Norse Warband an Amazon Warband will fight to the death. The Amazons can re-roll their first failed Rout against the Norse. Remember you can't re-roll a failed re-roll. In addition, Amazons can never choose to voluntarily rout when facing a Norse warband unless their Warband Leader has been taken Out of Action.

rules.title: Not one of us
rules.description: Due to the Amazons' isolationism and suspicions about other races they never side with anyone else. For this reason, the Amazons may not have any Hired Swords or Dramatis Personae unless they are Amazons themselves.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any models in the warband within 6" of the Priestess may use her Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: One with the Jungle
specials.description: A Jaguar has lived her life in the deepest parts and can move through jungle terrain without penalty.

rules.title: Sacrifice
rules.description: The Amazons are quick to sacrifice any captive to their gods. The Amazons follow the rules for Possessed in the Rulebook when it comes to captives.

rules.title: Not one of us
rules.description: Due to the Amazons’ isolationism and suspicions about other races they never side with anyone else. For this reason, the Amazons may not have any Hired Swords or Dramatis Personae unless they are actually Amazons themselves.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any models in the warband within 6" of the Priestess may use her Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Stealthy
specials.description: A Scout may deploy twice the distance onto the battlefield than other warriors and may start the battle Hiding.

rules.title: Hate Undead
rules.description: The men of Araby have suffered heavily at the hands (or should that be claws!) of the Tomb King’s armies in the Land of the Dead. Therefore, Araby Nomad Heroes hate all Undead.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: The Sheikh is the leader of the Warband and any Tomb Raiders within 6" may use his Leadership characteristic for any Leadership tests.

specials.name: Desert Trader
specials.description: Add +1 to your search for Equipping/Trading result. Note that you only get +1 even if you have two Bedouins.

specials.name: Life of Slavery
specials.description: A Slave may gain experience, but if he rolls Lad’s got Talent, the leader executes the Slave, and he is removed from the roster. The rest of the group may then re-roll their advance.

rules.title: Slavers
rules.description: A captured Hero or Henchman who joins the warband willingly becomes one of the Crew; one who joins unwillingly becomes a Slave, and does not follow the Swabbie rules. After rolling for captures in the post-battle sequence, the warband may sell any Slaves, old or newly taken, for 2D6 gold crowns each. Taking slaves may carry the warband over 15 models and over five Slaves for a time, as long as the extra models are sold or dismissed before the cargo is sold.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Rais may use his Leadership for any Leadership test.

specials.name: Fine Craftmenship
specials.description: Once per turn you may re-roll any dice roll the Merchant makes. If he is not taken out of action, he rolls two exploration dice and keeps either one as the result.

specials.name: Not Pirates
specials.description: A Janissary may not use the leader's Leadership for a test. A Janissary who becomes a Hero may not learn a Pirate skill and may not become the warband's leader.

specials.name: Life of Slavery
specials.description: A Slave gains experience, but if he rolls That Lad's Got Talent the leader executes him: remove him from the roster. The rest of his group then re-roll the advance, re-rolling any further That Lad's Got Talent result this advance.

rules.title: Northern Barbarians
rules.description: Every Hero in the warband hates human warriors of the Empire and of Bretonnia.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Sheik may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Guide
specials.description: Add +1 to the warband's roll for equipping and trading. Two Bedouins still give +1 only.

specials.name: Executed
specials.description: A Slave gains experience, but the leader executes him if he rolls That Lad's Got Talent.

rules.title: Known thieves
rules.description: Several of the warband's members are wanted thieves. A captured thief may be sold for 1D6 gold crowns plus his experience. Roll a D6 once he is sold: on a 1-3 one of his hands is chopped off; on a 4-5 he is burned with hot irons and branded on the forehead, which counts as a deep chest wound, so he loses 1 Toughness and is at -3 on his rolls to find items; on a 6 he is executed.

rules.title: Knowing the trade routes
rules.description: Add +1 to the warband's rolls to find items.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Guild Master may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Known thief
specials.description: The Guild Master counts as a known thief.

specials.name: Known thief
specials.description: The Guild Master counts as a known thief.

specials.name: Begging
specials.description: Whenever the warband rolls for what it finds after a battle in a city or at an oasis with a caravan, each Beggar may beg. Roll a D6 for him: on a 2-6 he is given D3 gold crowns, and on a 1 he is beaten and misses the next battle.

name: Assassin Squad, Knives from the Dark
source: Assassin Squad, Knives from the Dark

rules.title: Look Behind You!
rules.description: A model trying to spot a hidden member of the warband does so at -1 Initiative, to a minimum of 1. This does not cover the warband's hired swords.

rules.title: The Boss
rules.description: The warband's leader must cause fear where that is possible. When a leader is replaced, pick from the heroes who are horribly scarred or fearsome; if none is, pick as normal, and the new leader must take the Fearsome skill with his next skill advance, which rules out a hero with no Strength skills.

specials.name: Leader
specials.type: Warband - Assassin Squad, Knives from the Dark
specials.description: Any warrior in the warband within 6" of the Shadowblade may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Vanish Into the Shadows
specials.type: Warband - Assassin Squad, Knives from the Dark
specials.description: At the start of a close combat round the Shadowblade may declare that he leaves the battle at the end of that round. He is out of the game from then on, with everything that follows from it. This is not being taken out of action, and he may do it while knocked down.

specials.name: Shadow Infiltration
specials.type: Warband - Assassin Squad, Knives from the Dark
specials.description: As the Infiltration skill, except that he need only be set up beyond the range at which he could be spotted while hidden. He is also immune to all alone tests.

specials.name: Camouflage
specials.type: Warband - Assassin Squad, Knives from the Dark
specials.description: A Sniper may shoot while hidden. He is detected only if he hits his target and a D6 roll of 3 or more follows.

specials.name: Dagger Specialist
specials.type: Warband - Assassin Squad, Knives from the Dark
specials.description: A missed attack made with a dagger on the turn he charges may be re-rolled. The second result stands.

name: Averlander Mercenaries
source: Town Cryer #10, revised in Mordheim Annual 2002

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Captain may use his Leadership characteristic when taking Leadership tests.

specials.name: Set Traps
specials.description: Bergjaeger are expert trappers and hunters and these skills can be put to great use in the ruins of Mordheim. A Bergjaeger may set a trap if he spends a turn doing nothing else (he may not set traps if he’s just recovered from being Knocked Down). Place a marker in base contact with the Bergjager. When a model, friend or foe, moves within 2" of the marker he risks setting off the trap – roll a D6. On a score of 3+ he has triggered the trap and suffers a S4 hit (note that the Bergjager won’t trigger his own traps). If the trap did not wound the model or it didn’t trigger, the ‘victim’ may finish his move otherwise he is placed knocked Down or Stunned 2" from the marker. Regardless whether the trap was triggered or not, the marker is removed.

specials.name: Promotion
specials.description: A Halfling that is promoted to hero through the “The lad’s got talent” advance may not choose Strength skills as one of his two skill lists. Halflings are not known for their great strength!

rules.title: Strictures
rules.description: A stringent regime of meditation is used by monks. Their faith is supported by a notion that the skin of one's body is armour in itself. Dragon Monks and Warrior Monks never wear any kind of armour.

rules.title: Distaste for Poison
rules.description: The use of poisons and various drugs is a speciality for dishonorable warriors who would stoop to such ends. Dragon Monks and Warrior Monks frown on this and may never use any kind of poison or venom.

rules.title: Outsiders
rules.description: Foreigners are generally considered unwelcome by the border guards of Cathay. The Battle Monks warband may never hire any sort of Hired Sword or Dramatis Personae unless specifically stated with the Hired sword/Dramatis Personae.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6“ of the Emissary may use his Leadership when taking Ld tests.

specials.name: Decree
specials.description: When the Emissary dies, a new one must be hired as soon as possible. Until you have done so, no other warriors and/or equipment may be bought. The new Emissary will then reclaim Leadership of the warband.

specials.name: Unarmed Combat
specials.description: Monks suffer no penalties whatsoever for fighting unarmed and they receive +1 Attack when doing so.

specials.name: Art of Silent Death
specials.description: Dragon Monks have become masters of the Cathayan art of open-hand fighting. In hand-to-hand combat, if fighting unarmed, they will cause a critical hit on a roll 'to wound' of 5-6 instead of a 6. If the Dragon Monk wields a quarter staff, only the unarmed attacks will cause a critical hit on 5+.

specials.name: Unarmed Combat
specials.description: Monks suffer no penalties whatsoever for fighting unarmed and they receive +1 Attack when doing so.

fighters.name: Raging Peasant
fighters.fixed_kit: A peasant is usually equipped with a pitchfork, torch, or other simple tool. Treat them as fighting unarmed but without any penalties.

specials.name: Weapons/Armour
specials.description: A peasant is usually equipped with a pitchfork, torch, or other simple tool. Treat them as fighting unarmed but without any penalties.

specials.name: Simple folk
specials.description: Peasants never gain Experience.

specials.name: Mob
specials.description: Peasants become threatening in large numbers. A Peasant gets +1 Ld for each other allied Peasant model within 3". Due to their rage, they do not benefit from the leader rule.

specials.name: Ignored
specials.description: Peasants that are out of action do not count toward the number of out-of-action models for the purpose of Rout tests.

specials.name: Downtrodden
specials.description: When a Peasant is wounded, do not roll for injury. The model is immediately taken out of action.

rules.title: Animals
rules.description: Beastmen are fearsome creatures of Chaos that do not interact with other races other than in war. A Beastmen warband may never hire any Hired Swords unless specifically stated with the Hired Sword.

lists.name: Beastmen Equipment List
lists.note: The following lists are used by Beastman warbands to pick their weapons:

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any Warrior within 6" of the Beastman Chieftain may use his Leadership characteristic when taking Leadership tests.

specials.name: Drunken
specials.description: Centigor are inclined to drink vast quantities of noxious beer and looted wine and spirits before battle, working themselves up into a drunken frenzy. Roll 1D6 at the start of each turn. On a roll of 1, they must test for stupidity that turn. On a roll of 2-5 nothing happens and on the roll of a 6 they become subject to frenzy for that turn. Whilst subject to either stupidity or frenzy, they are immune to all other forms of psychology.

specials.name: Woodland Dwelling
specials.description: Centigors are creatures of the deep, dark forests. They suffer no movement penalties for moving through wooded areas.

specials.name: Trample
specials.description: As well as their weapons, Centigors use their hooves and sheer size to crush their enemies. This counts as an additional attack, which does not benefit from weapon bonuses or penalties...

specials.name: Lowest of the Low
specials.description: Ungor are on the lowest rung of Beastmen society and regardless of how much Experience they accrue they will never acquire a position of authority. If an Ungor rolls ‘That lad’s got talent’ it must be re-rolled.

fighters.name: Warhounds of Chaos
fighters.fixed_kit: None! Apart from their fangs and nasty tempers the Chaos Hounds don’t have weapons and can fight without any penalties.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Chaos Hounds are animals and never gain Experience.

specials.name: Bloodgreed
specials.description: If a Minotaur puts all of its enemies out of action in hand-to-hand combat, it becomes frenzied on a D6 roll of 4+.

specials.name: Animal
specials.description: A Minotaur is far more bestial than its Beastmen brethren and, although it may gain Experience, it may never become a Hero.

rules.title: Hard to Kill
rules.description: Like their uncorrupted brethren, Chaos Dwarfs are tough, resilient individuals who can only be taken out of action on a roll of 6 instead of 5-6 when rolling on the Injury chart. Treat a roll of 1-2 as knocked down, 3-5 as stunned, and 6 as out of action.

rules.title: Hard Head
rules.description: Chaos Dwarfs ignore the special rules for clubs, maces, etc. They too are not easy to knock out!

rules.title: Armour
rules.description: Chaos Dwarfs never suffer movement penalties for wearing armour.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: A Chaos Dwarf warband may hire the following Hired Swords: Ogre Bodyguard, Pit Fighter, Warlock, Imperial Assassin, and Hobgoblin Scout. They may hire any Hired Sword described as all may hire, or allowed by Orc warbands and Chaos warbands. They may never hire Elves of any sort!

lists.name: Chaos Dwarf Equipment List
lists.note: Starting warbands receive special prices on the Mechanical suit and the Engine of Chaos. These special prices represent the lower rarity of these items in the Dark Lands. When attempting to manufacture these items in Mordheim or anywhere else outside Zharr-Naggrund, Chaos Dwarfs pay the full prices, and must roll to acquire them as normal.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6“ of the Sorcerer may use his Leadership when taking Ld tests.

specials.name: Nasty Reputation
specials.description: Gaolers are known for their brutality. The dreaded sight of them and the very thought of being captured causes fear in Humans.

specials.name: Drudgery
specials.description: Informers have had their will broken by their masters. Informers may never become Heroes. Re-roll all results of ‘The lad’s got talent’ for them.

rules.title: Let the goons do the work
rules.description: Black Orcs rely on themselves to do the killing and do not ride mounts of any kind. Only normal Orcs may ride a boar or other such mount.

rules.title: Da Boss is Dead!
rules.description: If the Boss should be killed a Black Orc will always assume leadership of the warband before any other type, irrespective of relative experience. The replacement will automatically acquire the "Oi Behave!" skill.

rules.title: Animosity
rules.description:
Orcs and Goblins enjoy nothing more than a good scrap, unfortunately they’re not always very discerning about who they scrap with! To represent this, at the start of the Orc player’s turn, roll a D6 for each Henchman who is either an Orc or a Goblin. A roll of 1 means that the warrior has taken offense to something one of his mates has done or said. Do not roll for models that are engaged in hand-to-hand combat (they’re already scrappin’!). To find out just how offended the model is, roll another D6 and consult the following chart to see what happens:

D6 | Result
1 | “I ’Erd Dat!”
The warrior decides that the nearest friendly Orc or Goblin Henchman has insulted his lineage or personal hygiene and must pay the price!
If there is a friendly Orc or Goblin Henchman or Hired Sword within charge reach (if there are multiple targets within reach, choose the one nearest to the mad model), the offended warrior will immediately charge and fight a round of hand-to-hand combat against the source of his ire. At the end of this round of combat, the models will immediately move 1" apart and no longer count as being in close combat (unless one of them fails another Animosity test and rolls this result again).
If there are no friendly Orc or Goblin Henchmen or Hired Swords within charge reach, and the warrior is armed with a missile weapon, he immediately takes a shot at the nearest friendly Orc or Goblin Henchman or Hired Sword. If none of the above applies, or if the nearest friendly model is an Orc Hero, the warrior behaves as if a 2-5 had been rolled on this chart. In any case, the warrior in question may take no other action this turn, though he may defend himself if attacked in hand-to-hand combat.
2-5 | “Wud Yoo Say?”
The warrior is fairly certain he heard an offensive sound from the nearest friendly Orc or Goblin, but he’s not quite sure. He spends the turn hurling insults at his mate.
He may do nothing else this turn, though he may defend himself if attacked in hand-to-hand combat.
6 | “I’ll Show Yer!”
The warrior imagines that his mates are laughing about him behind his back and calling him silly names. To show them up he decides that he’ll be the first one to the scrap!
This model must move as quickly as possible towards the nearest enemy model, charging into combat if possible. If there are no enemy models within sight, the Orc or Goblin warrior may make a normal move immediately. This move is in addition to his regular move in the Movement phase, so he may therefore move twice in a single turn if you wish.
If the extra move takes the Orc or Goblin warrior within charge reach of an enemy model, the warrior must charge into close combat during his regular movement.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Boss may use his Leadership characteristic when taking Leadership tests.

specials.name: Black Orc
specials.description: Model starts with a natural 6+ Armour Black Orc Save. This save may be combined with other equipment to improve it.

specials.name: Oi Behave!
specials.description:
If any Henchman fails his Animosity test within 6” of the Boss, the player may opt to have the boss stamp his authority (and clenched fist) on the situation.

The misbehaving Henchman will receive an automatic hit at the strength of the Orc player’s choosing. If the Henchman is still on his feet after his slap, he may add a number equal to the strength of the slap to his subsequent roll to determine the effects of Animosity.

E.g. The player decides that the Boss will hit a misbehaving Henchman with a S2 slap. If the slap fails to Knock Down, Stun or Out of Action the Henchman, then he adds +2 to the Animosity Effect roll.

specials.name: Black Orc (Black Orc)
specials.description: Model starts with a natural 6+ Armour Black Orc Save. This save may be combined with other equipment to improve it.

specials.name: Black Orc Blood
specials.description: One Young’un may be upgraded to a Black Orc Young’un for 10gc. This upgrade allows him to take the ‘Proven Warrior’ skill upgrade, thus making him a fully-fledged Black Orc Warrior.

specials.name: Animosity
specials.description: At the start of every turn, every Orc Boy must take a Ld Test for Animosity

specials.name: Animosity (Orc Shoota)
specials.description: At the start of every turn, every Shoota must take a Ld Test for Animosity.

specials.name: Uncommon
specials.description: A warband may not hire more Shootaz than they have Boyz. If a boy dies and the Shootaz outnumber the Boyz, the next hire must be a boy so that the balance is restored.

specials.name: Unstable
specials.description: These Orcs are not quite all there. They do not suffer from Animosity, but instead have a host of their own issues to deal with.

specials.name: Crazy
specials.description: Nuttaz always pass any Leadership-based Tests they have to take. A side effect of this is that their minds are too far-gone and they may never learn Academic Skills should they become a Hero on an Advance Roll.

specials.name: Savage (Orc Nutta)
specials.description: Nuttaz must always run or charge their maximum distance towards the nearest opponent they can see. Friendly models do not block line of sight. Additionally they fight with an extra attack whilst in combat. This does not appear on their profile nor does it count towards the racial maximum. If no enemy is visible they are moved under the player’s control. They can never use any form of armour or ranged weapons. Nuttaz are also too unstable for other Boyz and can never have the Leader ability or use their Ld stat for rout tests, excepting them as being the only models left on the board.

fighters.name: Troll
fighters.fixed_kit: Trolls do not require weapons to fight but often carry a big club. In any event, Trolls can never be given weapons or armour.

specials.name: Regeneration (Black Orcs' Troll)
specials.description: Trolls have a unique physiology that allows them to regenerate wounds. Whenever an enemy successfully inflicts a wound on a Troll roll a D6, on a result of 4 or more the wound is ignored and the Troll is unhurt. Trolls may not regenerate wounds caused by fire or fire-based magic. Trolls never roll for Injury after a battle, unless they were taken Out of Action by a Flaming weapon or spell. Then they roll after the battle as a normal Henchman.

specials.name: Dumb Monster
specials.description: A Troll is far too stupid to ever learn any new skills. Trolls do not gain experience.

specials.name: Always Hungry
specials.description: A Troll requires an upkeep cost. This upkeep represents the copious amounts of food that must be fed to the Troll in order to keep him loyal to the warband. The warband must pay 20 gold crowns after every game in order to keep the Troll. If a warband lacks the gold to pay the upkeep, the Boss has the option to let him count as 2 members, letting the Troll cost only 5 crowns. However this does effectively drop your maximum warband size down to 11 models.

specials.name: Vomit Attack
specials.description: Instead of his normal attacks, a Troll can regurgitate its highly corrosive digestive juices on an unfortunate hand-to-hand combat opponent. This is a single attack that automatically hits with a Strength of 5 and ignores armour saves.

rules.title: Grave Guards
rules.description: A warband may never have more Grave Guards than Skeleton Warriors.

rules.title: Bloodline Abilities
rules.description: The Vampire may take one or more Bloodline abilities when he is created, the first at its price and every later one at double. Each time he gains a new skill he may take a Bloodline ability instead of the skill, at double cost.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Vampire may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Summoner
specials.description: The Vampire summoned every undead warrior of the warband. While he is out of action, roll a Leadership test each round for every undead model in the warband: a model that fails goes out of action too.

specials.name: Killing Blow
specials.description: A natural 6 on the roll to hit wounds automatically. The blow may not be parried, but armour and other saves are allowed.

specials.name: No Brain
specials.description: Skeleton Warriors gain no experience.

specials.name: Killing Blow
specials.description: A natural 6 on the roll to hit wounds automatically. The blow may not be parried, but armour and other saves are allowed.

fighters.name: Hell Hound
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Hell Hounds are animals and use no weapons or armour.

specials.name: Animal
specials.description: Hell Hounds are animals and gain no experience.

special.name: Red Fury
special.description: The Vampire gains +1 Attack.

special.name: Killing Blow
special.description: A natural 6 on the roll to hit wounds automatically. The blow may not be parried, but armour and other saves are allowed.

special.name: Blood Lust
special.description: The Vampire is subject to frenzy.

special.name: Master Strike
special.description: The Vampire causes a critical hit on a 5 or 6.

special.name: Curse Of The Undead
special.description: If the Vampire goes out of action, after the battle he heals all of his wounds on a D6 roll of 5+, and then does not roll on the serious injury table.

special.name: Strength of the Dragon
special.description: The Vampire gains +1 Strength.

special.name: Gift of Abhorash
special.description: The warband's maximum number of warriors rises by one, for good.

rules.title: Look Out Behind You!
rules.description: A model trying to spot a hidden member of the warband, hired swords aside, suffers -1 Initiative.

rules.title: Men of Low Character
rules.description: The warband may hire no warrior with knightly, noble or law-enforcing ties: for now the Elf Ranger and the Freelancer.

rules.title: The Boss
rules.description: The warband's leader must cause fear where it can be arranged. When a new leader is needed, choose among the heroes who cause fear; if none does, choose as usual, and that hero must take the Fearsome skill with his next skill advance. A hero with no Strength skills can never do so.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Scarface may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Old Connections
specials.description: The Fallen Noble adds +1 to rarity rolls.

rules.title: Swabbies
rules.description: The warband's Swabbies are human, and are captured rather than hired, under the Sartosa campaign rules.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The warband hires Hired Swords and buys other items as a human Mercenary warband does. A warband holding both Dwarfs and Elves pays 20 gold crowns more in upkeep.

rules.title: Swivel Guns are Rare, Matey!
rules.description: The warband may not start a campaign game with a Swivel Gun on its roster. In a one-off game it may buy one for 2D6 gold crowns more.

rules.title: Duellists
rules.description: When a Hero shoots with a Pistol, its first 6" count as short range; with a Duelling Pistol, its first 10" count as short range. With the Eagle Eye skill, the 6" that skill adds count as long range.

rules.title: Succession
rules.description: If the Captain is killed, one of the Mates takes his place, as a Champion does in a Mercenary warband.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any pirate within 6" of the Captain may use his Leadership for any Leadership test.

specials.name: Swivel Guns is Dangerous, Matey!
specials.description: A Gunner carrying the Swivel Gun always counts as an individual and may never be joined by anyone else. Since the warband may hold only one Swivel Gun, the Gunner carrying it is either newly hired or split off from his group, keeping the experience and skills he had.

fighters.name: Boatswain
fighters.fixed_kit: A Rope & Hook, which he may never sell or give away.

specials.name: Expert Riggers
specials.description: A Boatswain may re-roll a failed Initiative test for leaping over a gap, jumping down or making a diving charge, and the test for climbing up or down with a rope.

specials.name: Not Hired
specials.description: Swabbies are not hired: they are captured, under the Sartosa campaign rules.

specials.name: Never Gain Experience
specials.description: Swabbies never gain experience.

specials.name: Rabble
specials.description: Swabbies need not be armed alike: each may carry different equipment, but only from the Swabbie Equipment list. A Swabbie may never use magic or cast a spell.

specials.name: 'Blimey, they got away!'
specials.description: If the warband routs, any Swabbie who has already left the table in an earlier turn escapes for good: remove him from the roster as if he had been killed.

specials.name: 'Don't mind them mates, they ain't true pirates!'
specials.description: Swabbies who are running away or have been taken out of action do not count towards the warband's rout test.

rules.title: Chivalry
rules.description: No Knight may ever use any missile weapon at all, with the exception of Holy Water. Likewise, they will never use any drug or poison, nor learn any spells (prayers are allowed).

rules.title: Lord’s Boon
rules.description: Every Knight, either at warband formation or upon later recruitment, is likely to start with some sort of boon from the baron, marquis, or similar lord he serves. Each Knight may, upon purchase, start with ONE of the following items, which is bought at half cost: a Warhorse, Light Armour, OR Heavy Armour. This item may not be traded, given to another warrior, or sold. The warrior may set it aside and choose not to use it, but no Bretonnian warrior would dare use a boon item that belonged to another Knight, even after the warrior’s death. If the Knight dies, his "Lord’s Boon" item is removed from the warband, having been buried with him or returned to his benefactor.

rules.title: Virtue of Purity
rules.description: Knights with the Virtue of Purity may never voluntarily break from combat, unless he is knocked down. He is immune to All Alone and any other mundane effect that would cause him to leave combat. Magical spells and effects that would cause him to flee (ex. Dread of Aramar) affect him as normal.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Questing Knight may use his Leadership characteristic when taking Leadership tests.

specials.name: Knight
specials.description: The Questing Knight has the following rules from above apply to him; Chivalry, Lord’s Boon and Virtue of Purity.

specials.name: Vow of Poverty
specials.description: May not take a Lance.

specials.name: Prayercaster
specials.description: The Damsel starts with one prayer from the Lady's Prayers list, and can learn additional prayers as outlined in the Magic section.

specials.name: Knight
specials.description: The Questing Knight has the following rules from above apply to him; Chivalry, Lord’s Boon and Virtue of Purity.

specials.name: Vain
specials.description: The Knight may not wear a helmet, as it reduces their chances of being noticed by pretty ladies.

specials.name: Impetuous
specials.description:
During each Movement Phase, after declaring charges, a Knight Errant that is not in combat and did not charge this turn must charge an opposing standing warrior (not knocked down or stunned) that is within range if they are able.

Likewise, a Knight Errant that declared a charge against a knocked down or stunned opponent will be compelled to charge a viable standing opponent instead. If you wish, you may choose to have the Knight take a leadership test (they may use their Leader's Leadership if they are within range); if the test is passed, they may move as normal or charge their original target.

When making a compelled charge, the Knight Errant automatically passes all fear tests or any other psychology tests that would prevent them from charging.

specials.name: Knighthood
specials.description:
When a Squire rolls "The Lad's Got Talent", you may choose one of two options when promoting him to a hero: to have him remain a Squire, or to have him become a Knight Errant. (Note: in this manner, you may have more than three Knights Errant in your Warband).

If you choose to keep him a Squire, he may choose two skill lists from following lists: Combat, Academic, Strength, or Speed. He retains his normal Squire equipment tables.

If you choose to make him a Knight Errant, he immediately gains the following rules/bonuses instead of receiving an immediate advancement: ‘Knight’, ‘Vain’ and ‘Impetuous’. The new knight may learn Special Skills, in addition to two other skill sets, but must immediately switch his equipment to Knight Equipment list. The new knight may never use missile weapons.

specials.name: Low Caste
specials.description: Battle Pilgrims are peasants, and while they are not stupid, there is a glass ceiling to what they can attain in Bretonnian society. Low Caste henchmen learn experience and advance as normal, but reroll any results of "The Lad's Got Talent", and may never become heroes.

specials.name: Hatred
specials.description: The model hates every enemy model.

specials.name: Stubborn
specials.description: Battle Pilgrims reroll all failed Leadership rolls once, accepting the second result.

specials.name: Holy Relics
specials.description: Battle Pilgrims may be given a Holy Relic, regardless of the fact that henchman are not normally allowed to take Miscellaneous items. If a Battle Pilgrim owns a Holy Relic, he gains the ability Frenzy (Reminder: when frenzied, he is immune to Hatred.) It is possible to give a Holy Relic to Battle Pilgrim that is a part of a larger henchman group. If you do not have enough Holy Relics for every member of the group, the Pilgrim with the relic will break off and form his own individual henchman group.

specials.name: Low Caste
specials.description: Battle Pilgrims are peasants, and while they are not stupid, there is a glass ceiling to what they can attain in Bretonnian society. Low Caste henchmen learn experience and advance as normal, but reroll any results of "The Lad's Got Talent", and may never become heroes.

rules.title: Knight Virtues
rules.description:
A model with Virtuous who gains a skill may roll 3D6 on this table instead of choosing one; he re-rolls a virtue he already has. Virtues never apply to a mount, and don't stack with other skills that give a like bonus.

3D6 | Virtue
3-4 | Virtue of Noble Disdain
5 | Virtue of Heroism
6 | Virtue of Stoicism
7 | Virtue of the Penitent
8 | Virtue of the Ideal
9 | Virtue of the Impetuous Knight
10 | Virtue of Audacity
11 | Virtue of Purity
12 | Virtue of Duty
13 | Virtue of the Joust
14 | Virtue of Confidence
15 | Virtue of Knightly Temper
16 | Virtue of Discipline
17-18 | Virtue of Empathy

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Grail Knight may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Knight's Vow
specials.description: The knight may never use a ranged weapon, is immune to All Alone tests and never breaks from combat.

specials.name: Loyal Steed
specials.description: The Grail Knight starts with a free warhorse (M8 WS3 BS- S3 T- W1 I- A1, no Ld given) that he can never dismount. It makes no injury rolls of its own, can't be traded or sold, never gains experience or abilities, and is lost if he gains a Pegasus. He moves at the warhorse's Movement.

specials.name: Lord's Boon
specials.description: When recruited the Grail Knight gains, free, either one set of barding, light armour and holy shield, or heavy armour. These can't be traded or sold and stay his until he dies. If he loses one, any later item of that type costs him twice its usual price.

specials.name: Blessing of the Lady
specials.description: An enemy model that wants to shoot at the Grail Knight must first pass a Leadership test; if it fails it can't shoot at him.

specials.name: Virtuous
specials.description: When the Grail Knight gains a skill he may roll on the Knight Virtues table instead of choosing a skill, re-rolling a virtue he already has.

specials.name: Honored Dead
specials.description: A Grail Knight who dies after a battle becomes a Grail Reliquae: replace his profile with the Reliquae's and he becomes a henchman. If the warband already has a Grail Reliquae, the new one gains +1 Strength. No new Grail Knight may be recruited to replace him.

specials.name: Knight's Vow
specials.description: The knight may never use a ranged weapon, is immune to All Alone tests and never breaks from combat.

specials.name: Lord's Boon (Knight of the Realm)
specials.description: Each Knight of the Realm may start with one free warhorse, suit of light armour and holy shield, or heavy armour. These can't be traded or sold and stay his until he dies. If he loses one, any later item of that type costs him twice its usual price.

specials.name: Virtuous
specials.description: When the Grail Knight gains a skill he may roll on the Knight Virtues table instead of choosing a skill, re-rolling a virtue he already has.

specials.name: Skilled Rider
specials.description: Knights of the Realm know how to ride a warhorse.

specials.name: Fanatics
specials.description: At the start of every battle the model hates the opposing warband.

specials.name: Commoner
specials.description: This model can never become a Hero: re-roll a "That Lad's Got Talent" result.

specials.name: Scouts
specials.description: Each Hunter may be set up up to 1D6" further out than the warband's deployment zone.

specials.name: Commoner
specials.description: This model can never become a Hero: re-roll a "That Lad's Got Talent" result.

specials.name: Knight's Vow
specials.description: The knight may never use a ranged weapon, is immune to All Alone tests and never breaks from combat.

specials.name: Lower-Caste
specials.description: A Hedge Knight may ride a mount in battle only when both Knights of the Realm fight mounted. A Hedge Knight who becomes a Hero uses the Knight of the Realm's skill lists, rolling on the Knight Virtues table when he gains a skill.

fighters.name: Grail Reliquae
fighters.fixed_kit: None. The Grail Reliquae carries no weapons or armour and attacks with a dagger's profile.

specials.name: Grail Icon
specials.description: Friendly models within 6" of the Reliquae may re-roll a failed Leadership test. The Reliquae gains no experience and can't run.

specials.name: Icon Bearers
specials.description: Each wound the Reliquae suffers also takes 1 from its Movement, Attacks and Leadership. These losses are restored if it survives the battle.

specials.name: Fanatics
specials.description: At the start of every battle the model hates the opposing warband.

specials.name: Holy Shield
specials.description: The Reliquae has an unmodifiable 5+ save against every non-magical attack.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The warband may hire no evil hired sword, and none who uses magic or poison.

lines.shown_as: Upgrade Light Armour to Heavy armour

fighters.name: Knight Errant
fighters.fixed_kit: A suit of light armour and a shield when first recruited. He must also buy a hand-to-hand weapon from the list; a dagger will not do.

specials.name: Bretonnian Leader
specials.description: The warband has no standing leader. Each Knight Errant starts with D6+7 experience, and the one who rolls highest leads, with every rule that applies to a leader; on a tie, choose between them. The experience rolled allows no starting advances.

specials.name: Knights Virtue
specials.description: A Knight Errant never breaks or panics: he takes no All Alone test.

rules.title: Blessing of the Lady
rules.description:
Before heading into battle Bretonnian Knights kneel and pray to the Lady of the Lake, avowing to fight to the death for honour and justice.

Before playing a game of Mordheim make a Leadership test against the Leadership characteristic of the warbands leader. If the test is successful the Lady of the Lake has bestowed her blessing on the warband. The blessing takes the form of a powerful curse upon the enemies of chivalry, and in particular upon those that make use of the foul and dishonourable weapons of mass destruction. Any model in the opposing warband who wishes to fire a black powder weapon must roll a D6 and score 4+ to overcome the curse, otherwise they may not fire the weapon. The opposing player must test each time they wish to fire such a weapon.

Models armed with other shooting weapons, such as bows and crossbows, do not have to test unless they dare raise their weapons against the gallant Knights of Bretonnia. If any enemy model wishes to shoot at a Bretonnian Knight (Questing Knights and Errants only), then they must first roll a 4+ on a D6 to overcome the curse.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Questing Knight may use his Leadership characteristic when taking Leadership tests.

specials.name: Knights Virtue
specials.description: A Questing Knight is a chivalrous warrior who is superior to ordinary warriors. He will never panic and break from combat and so does not have to pass a Leadership test for being all alone.

specials.name: Knights Virtue
specials.description: A Questing Knight is a chivalrous warrior who is superior to ordinary warriors. He will never panic and break from combat and so does not have to pass a Leadership test for being all alone.

rules.title: No Skin, No Service
rules.description: Ethereal models may not enter settlements, unless a rule says they may.

rules.title: Requilary
rules.description:
Every Ethereal member of the warband starts the battle inside the Requilary. At the start of each turn, take a Leadership test on the highest Leadership the warband has (the Requilary has a Leadership of its own); for each point it is passed by, one warrior may be deployed within 6" of the Mortis Engine. Where the Mortis Engine can't be brought (underground, the pit of blood and the like), the Corpse Master carries it on his back and can't run.

If the Requilary is destroyed, the warband routs at once, and every model within D6+6" takes a Strength 5 hit; a magic user takes D3 such hits. The Cairn Wraith makes a new Requilary and misses D3 games doing it.

specials.name: Leader
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Cairn Wraith may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Ethereal
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description:
The model has an unmodifiable 4+ save against every attack, taken after the to-hit roll. It can't be used with Dodge or Step Aside, and is no use against magical attacks (spells, prayers, artefacts). A missile that misses because of the save passes through and hits the next closest target directly behind.

Terrain doesn't hinder the model, and it may take a Leadership test in the movement phase: if it passes, it may move through any terrain and over water. If it starts its next turn inside a terrain piece, it takes another Leadership test in the movement phase, and if it fails it is taken out of action at once.

Once the warband is made, every item costs an Ethereal model double. When the warband finds an item, roll a D6: on a 5+ Ethereal and other models may both use it; on a 1-4 only the others may (mark it on the roster).

specials.name: Warrior Wizard
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: The Cairn Wraith may wear armour and cast spells with no penalty.

specials.name: Death Was Merely the Beginning
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: When the Cairn Wraith rolls 11-15 (Dead) on the Serious Injury chart, he may return to the warband for his hiring cost plus twice his experience points, but only while the warband has a Requilary. If the Requilary and the Cairn Wraith are both destroyed in one round, the warband is disbanded.

specials.name: Ethereal
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description:

A missile that misses because of the save passes through and hits the next closest target directly behind.

specials.name: Ghostly Howl
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: Enemies within 6" of the Tomb Banshee have -D6 Leadership when they take fear tests.

specials.name: Ethereal
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description:
The model has an unmodifiable 4+ save against every attack, taken after the to-hit roll. It can't be used with Dodge or Step Aside, and is no use against magical attacks (spells, prayers, artefacts). Once the warband is made, every item costs an Ethereal model double. When the warband finds an item, roll a D6: on a 5+ Ethereal and other models may both use it; on a 1-4 only the others may (mark it on the roster).

specials.name: Violent Entry
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: A Malignant Spirit that charges in the turn it is summoned has +1 to hit and +1 Strength.

specials.name: Gofer
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: As the warband's only living member, the Corpse Master may visit D3+1 places in a settlement rather than 1.

specials.name: Magical Void
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: The Corpse Master has a 4+ save against enemy spells and magic weapons.

specials.name: Guardian of the Requilary
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: The Corpse Master never moves more than 6" from the Requilary of his own will.

specials.name: Spectral Ascension
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: A Revenant who rolls The Lad's Got Talent becomes Ethereal once he is a Hero.

fighters.name: Mourngul
fighters.fixed_kit: None. The Mourngul fights with its claws and fangs.

specials.name: No Brain
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: The Mourngul gains no experience.

specials.name: Nightmare Birth
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: The Mourngul may be summoned only once a Large model has been taken out of action, and is deployed where that model fell.

specials.name: Ravening Onslaught
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: Each to-hit roll of 6 gives the Mourngul another attack, and each 6 rolled for those gives another.

specials.name: Haunter of the Dark
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: The Mourngul's Ethereal save is 3+.

fighters.name: Spirit Host
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Spirit Hosts fight with spectral claws and daggers.

specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: The Mourngul gains no experience.

specials.name: Spectral Touch
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: Each to-hit roll of 6 a Spirit Host makes inflicts 1 more wound at once; the hit itself is rolled to wound as normal.

fighters.name: Poltergeist
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Poltergeists fight unarmed with no penalty.

specials.name: Incorporeal
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: A wounded Poltergeist doesn't roll for injury: it is taken out of action at once.
