A missile that misses because of the save passes through and hits the next closest target directly behind.

Terrain doesn't hinder the model, and it may take a Leadership test in the movement phase: if it passes, it may move through any terrain and over water. If it starts its next turn inside a terrain piece, it takes another Leadership test in the movement phase, and if it fails it is taken out of action at once.

Once the warband is made, every item costs an Ethereal model double. When the warband finds an item, roll a D6: on a 5+ Ethereal and other models may both use it; on a 1-4 only the others may (mark it on the roster).

specials.name: Silent Move
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: Poltergeists always stay hidden unless they charge an enemy warrior.

specials.name: Cause Ruckus
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: A Poltergeist may make a shooting attack with a range of 6" and no penalties: two shots at Strength 1.

specials.name: No Brain
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: The Mourngul gains no experience.

specials.name: Ignored
specials.type: Warband - Call of the Night Haint
specials.description: Poltergeists taken out of action don't count towards rout tests.

rules.title: Dangerous to Know
rules.description: Because of its rather diseased nature a Carnival of Chaos warband would find it very hard to keep any Hired Swords alive! Therefore, a Carnival of Chaos may never hire any type of Hired Sword.

rules.title: Tainted
rules.description: The Carnival is a similarly unclean mass of mutation and Chaos to the Possessed and so counts as such for purposes of exploration and serious injuries.

rules.title: Blessings of Nurgle
rules.description:
Those that worship at the fetid altar of the Lord of Decay suffer from terrible diseases and decay, which are known as Blessings of Nurgle.

Blessings of Nurgle may be bought for Tainted Ones only when they are recruited; you may not buy new Blessings for a model after recruitment. Any Tainted may have one or more Blessings. The first Blessing is bought at the price indicated, but second and subsequent Blessings cost double.

lists.name: Carnival of Chaos Equipment List
lists.note: The following lists are used by the Carnival of Chaos to pick their weapons:

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any models in the warband within 6" of the Master may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Nurgle’s Blessings
specials.description: Tainted Ones must start the game with one or more Blessings of Nurgle. See the Blessings of Nurgle that follow.

fighters.name: Plague Bearer
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Plague Bearers have huge filth encrusted claws, which they use to tear and slash at their foes. They therefore neither need nor use weapons and cannot wear armour.

specials.name: Daemonic
specials.description: Plague Bearers are Daemons of the lord of disease, Nurgle, and are not made of living flesh but the eternal and unchanging forces of Chaos. Therefore they never gain Experience.

specials.name: Immune to Poison (Plague Bearers)
specials.description: Plague Bearers are the Daemonic embodiment of disease and pestilence. They are totally immune to all poisons and diseases.

specials.name: Immune to Psychology (Plague Bearers)
specials.description: Plague Bearers are Daemons and do not know the concept of fear. They automatically pass any Leadership-based test they are required to take.

specials.name: Daemonic Aura
specials.description: Due to the magical, intangible nature of Daemons they have a special Armour save of 5+. This is modified by the Strength of the attack as normal and is completely negated by magic weapons and spells. Plague Bearers’ attacks are considered as magical also.

specials.name: Daemonic Instability
specials.description: Plague Bearers are bound to the world by Dark Sorcery that is highly volatile and unstable. If taken out of action a Plague Bearer is banished and effectively destroyed on a D6 roll of 1-3 (do not roll for injury). In addition, if the warband routs then every Plague Bearer in the warband must take an immediate Leadership test. If this test is failed, then the Plague Bearer counts as destroyed.

fighters.name: Nurgling
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Nurglings do not use weapons or wear armour.

specials.name: Swarm
specials.description: You may summon as many Nurglings as you wish (ie. you may have more than five Nurglings in a Henchman group).

specials.name: Daemonic (Nurgling)
specials.description: Nurglings are Daemons of the diseased Lord Nurgle and are not made of living flesh but the eternal and unchanging forces of Chaos. Therefore they never gain Experience.

specials.name: Immune to Poison (Nurglings)
specials.description: Nurglings are the Daemonic embodiment of disease and pestilence. They are totally immune to all poisons and diseases.

specials.name: Immune to Psychology (Nurglings)
specials.description: Nurglings are Daemons and do not know the concept of fear. They automatically pass any Leadership-based test they are required to take.

specials.name: Daemonic Aura (Nurgling)
specials.description: Due to the magical, intangible nature of Daemons they have a special Armour save of 5+. This is modified by the Strength of the attack as normal and is completely negated by magic weapons and spells. Nurglings’ attacks are also considered as magical.

specials.name: Daemonic Instability
specials.description: Plague Bearers are bound to the world by Dark Sorcery that is highly volatile and unstable. If taken out of action a Plague Bearer is banished and effectively destroyed on a D6 roll of 1-3 (do not roll for injury). In addition, if the warband routs then every Plague Bearer in the warband must take an immediate Leadership test. If this test is failed, then the Plague Bearer counts as destroyed.

fighters.name: Plague Cart
fighters.fixed_kit: None. The Plague Cart’s Guardian does not use or need weapons but suffers no penalties for fighting unarmed. Therefore it cannot use weapons and cannot wear armour.

specials.name: Plague Cart
specials.description:
The Daemonic nature of the Plague Cart fills both the Daemons and mortals of the Carnival of Chaos with vigour. The maximum number of warriors allowed in the warband is increased by +2.

In addition, the Daemonic Instability of the Daemons within the warband is slightly offset. Plague Bearers and Nurglings may re-roll Leadership tests for Instability and may +1 to their Injury tests if taken out of action.

specials.name: Guardian
specials.description: The Guardian comes as part of the Plague Cart. In fact, more often than not he is physically bonded to the cart in some twisted nightmare of flesh and wood. He may therefore never dismount from the cart or leave under any circumstances. In addition, as he is part of the Cart he cannot be injured unless the Cart is destroyed in which case so is he. The Guardian is considered a Daemonic creature and so never gains any Experience. Attacks from the Guardian cause Nurgle’s Rot (see below).

specials.name: Immune to Psychology (Plague Cart)
specials.description: The Plague Cart and Guardian are considered Daemonic and don’t know the concept of fear. The Plague Cart automatically passes any Leadership-based test it is required to take.

rules.title: Water Caravan
rules.description: The warband must include one Riverboat or River Barge. In a campaign with no rivers it takes a Wagon and two horses instead, and the Tinker's Rigger becomes Handyman, so that he repairs the wagon.

rules.title: Lucky White Heather
rules.description:
Instead of searching for a rare item after a battle, one Hero may try to con or rob a Hero of another warband. Roll a D6:

D6 | Result
1 | He pushes his luck and is lynched: roll on the Serious Injury chart for him.
2-5 | The other warband must buy a fake lucky charm for D6 gold crowns.
6 | He steals an item: choose one belonging to one of the other warband's Heroes.

rules.title: Shadowy Traditions
rules.description:
Instead of searching for a rare item after a battle, the Petru may ask the Old Father to receive one of his family: on a passed Leadership test, one of the warband's other Heroes visits the Old Father in the post-battle sequence; if the test fails, the Petru misses the next battle.

The visiting Hero must be human, and neither the leader nor a spellcaster; one with mutations has -1 to the roll. Roll a D6 on the Father-in-Darkness chart:

D6 | Result
1-3 | Unworthy Son: the Old Father drains him. Remove him from the roster.
4 | Fortunate Son: nothing happens.
5 | Favourite Son: he becomes a Blood-swain, with +1 Initiative and +1 Attack. A Blood-swain who visits again adds +1 to the roll.
6 | Son-in-darkness: he becomes a Surrogate Vampire, with +1 Movement, +1 Toughness, +1 Wound, +1 Initiative and +1 Attack (a Blood-swain's increases don't add to these). He treats a stunned result on the Injury chart as knocked down, causes fear, is immune to poison and is subject to Red Thirst.

rules.title: Red Thirst
rules.description: Roll a D6 for each Surrogate Vampire at the start of each turn: on a 1 he must test for stupidity that turn; on a 2-5 nothing happens; on a 6 he is subject to frenzy that turn.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Domnu may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Prize-fighter
specials.description: The Domnu suffers no penalty for fighting unarmed, and has +1 Attack when he does.

specials.name: Bear Hug
specials.description: If the Domnu hits the same enemy with both his unarmed attacks in a round of combat, he may make one Bear Hug attack instead of resolving them: each player rolls a D6 and adds his warrior's Strength. If the Domnu's total is higher or equal, the enemy takes one automatic wound with no armour save; if the enemy's is higher, he breaks the hold and takes no damage.

specials.name: Necromancy
specials.description: Instead of a new skill, the Petru may roll a new spell at random from Necromancy.

specials.name: Petru's Potions
specials.description:
Before a battle, one Hero of the warband may drink one of the Petru's potions. Roll a D6:

D6 | Result
1 | Debilitating: -1 Toughness for the whole of the next battle, until he rolls a 6 on a D6 in a recovery phase.
2-3 | Strength: +1 Strength until he rolls a 1 on a D6 in a recovery phase.
4-5 | Resilience: +1 Toughness until he rolls a 1 on a D6 in a recovery phase.
6 | Fortitude: +1 Wound for the whole battle; once lost, it can't be restored.

specials.name: Grifter
specials.description: As a merchant does, the Tinker lets the warband arrange trading deals with other warbands.

specials.name: Rigger
specials.description: While the warband's boat or barge is stationary and hasn't moved in the last turn, the Tinker in contact with it may repair one damaged location (a paddle, a mast). He does nothing else that turn, and the vessel may not move. No repair while an enemy model is in contact with the Tinker or the vessel.

specials.name: Spry
specials.description: A Truant may run or charge while climbing.

specials.name: Taunt
specials.description: In the shooting phase, instead of shooting, a Truant may taunt one enemy he can see, with line of sight as for shooting. The enemy takes a Leadership test: if he fails, he must spend his next movement phase trying to reach close combat with the Truant.

specials.name: Dead Eye Shot
specials.description: A Dead-eye ignores to-hit modifiers for cover when he shoots or throws his weapon.

specials.name: Target Practice
specials.description: A Dead-eye may fire one missile attack when he is charged, at -1 to hit for standing and shooting.

specials.name: Weapons Expert
specials.description: A Dead-eye may use any missile weapon he comes across, not only those of the warband's lists.

specials.name: Charismatic
specials.description: A model of the opposite sex (Sisters of Sigmar, Amazons, Kislev Rangers and the like) must pass a Leadership test to charge a Fugitive.

rules.title: Entertain the Masses
rules.description: In the exploration phase the warband may entertain the people living in the ruins instead of exploring. It then rolls an extra 2D6 for the wyrdstone shards it finds, and counts no doubles, triples or other results on the exploration tables.

rules.title: Superstitious
rules.description: The warband must always decline the chance to loot the dead.

rules.title: Lure of the Road
rules.description: Where an exploration result would let an Undead warband add zombies, or another warband sell people as slaves, the warband may add those people as Impressionable Youths instead.

rules.title: Apprenticeship
rules.description: A Youth promoted by That Lad's Got Talent may be named the apprentice of one Performer. If that Performer dies the Youth gains his special rules in his place, even if that takes the warband past its limit for that specialization. A promoted Youth is no longer subject to Dream Chasers.

rules.title: Hard Luck of the Road
rules.description: To hire a new Performer the Ringmaster must pass a Leadership test, at -1 for each Performer he has lost in battle and a further -1 for each Performer after the first he is hiring at the same time.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior in the warband within 6" of the Ringmaster may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Performer Skill
specials.description: For 20 gc more the Ringmaster may take one of the Performer specializations himself. He then counts towards the warband's limit for that specialization, and starts with 4 experience more.

specials.name: Specialist
specials.description:
Each Performer picks one specialization when he joins, within the warband's limits: 0-2 Beast Tamer, 0-2 Acrobat, 0-1 Exotic Mystery of the East, 0-1 Freak, 0-1 Marksman, 0-1 Magician.

Beast Tamer: the warband may hold 2 more Trained Animals, and a Trained Animal within 6" of him does not test for Ferocity.

Acrobat: he starts with the Dodge skill.

Exotic Mystery of the East: he never uses a weapon and is always treated as carrying a pair of clubs. He may be given no equipment.

Freak: he may buy a mutation from the Cult of the Possessed mutation list.

Marksman: he starts with Knife-Fighter or Trick Shooter.

Magician: he is a spell caster, as a Warlock is.

A Marksman takes Combat, Shooting and Speed as his skill lists; a Freak and an Exotic Mystery of the East take Combat and Strength; every other Performer takes Combat, Academic and Speed.

specials.name: Beefy
specials.description: A Strongman's maximum Strength is 5.

specials.name: Dream Chasers
specials.description: The warband may never hold more Impressionable Youths than its other hirelings together. If losses leave the hirelings outnumbered, enough Youths leave the warband to put that right.

specials.name: Goofy Clothes
specials.description: A Clown's costume gives him a 6+ armour save that the Strength of a hit never modifies. He loses it while he carries or wears anything else that gives an armour save.

fighters.name: Trained Animal
fighters.fixed_kit: None. A Trained Animal fights with claws and fangs.

specials.name: Animal
specials.description: A Trained Animal is an animal and gains no experience.

specials.name: Ferocity
specials.description: While it is out of range of its trainer and not in close combat a Trained Animal must test for stupidity. Where a failed test would have it stand still, it charges the nearest model instead, friend or foe.

specials.name: Oddity
specials.description: For 60 gc more when it is bought, one Trained Animal in the warband may be an Oddity: it gains +1 Wound and +1 Toughness, and is subject to stupidity in place of Ferocity.

specials.name: Tamer Limits
specials.description: The warband may hold 2 Trained Animals for each Beast Tamer Performer.

rules.title: Laws of Construction
rules.description:
A Law is not a spell, so protection against spells does not stop it, and it may be used while wearing armour, as a prayer may. A Clockworker who knows Laws rolls for one on a D6:

D6 | Law | Difficulty
1 | Offense | 7
2 | Motion | 6
3 | Defense | 7
4 | Sacrifice | 9
5 | Protection | 7
6 | Rampage | 10

lists.name: Constructs Equipment List
lists.note: A 1-slot line fills one of the construct's equipment slots and a 2-slot line two; armour goes in its armour slot.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Master of Clocks may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Laws of Construction
specials.description: The Master of Clocks starts with one Law of Construction.

specials.name: Promotion
specials.description: If the Master of Clocks dies or leaves the expedition, the new leader may learn Laws of Construction on later skill advances.

specials.name: Armour
specials.description: A Dwarf never suffers a movement penalty for wearing armour.

specials.name: Hard to Kill
specials.description: On the Injury chart, treat a roll of 1-2 as knocked down, 3-5 as stunned and 6 as out of action.

specials.name: Hard Head
specials.description: A Dwarf ignores the special rules for maces, clubs and the like.

specials.name: Smithery
specials.description: Instead of searching for rare items, the engineer may fit a single construct with any weapon he can get. A two-handed or missile weapon takes two slots, any other weapon one.

specials.name: Moonstone refinery
specials.description: Instead of searching for rare items, the Metallurgist may split one moonstone into D6 orichalcum tokens.

specials.name: Hellish tincture
specials.description: Once per game the Metallurgist may throw this tincture as blessed water is thrown, and it sets its target on fire. On a roll of 1 to hit, he is set on fire instead.

specials.name: Crude
specials.description: When a Handyman rolls That Lad's Got Talent, the new Hero takes Combat and Strength skills as his two skill lists.

specials.name: Need Orders
specials.description: At the beginning of your turn roll a D6 for each construct with no friendly Hero within 6", unless it is in close combat. On a 1-2 it may neither move nor shoot this turn.

specials.name: Brainless
specials.description: A construct gains no experience and can only be improved physically.

specials.name: In-built equipment
specials.description: A weapon or piece of armour given to a construct can never be taken off it again. A construct has equipment slots instead of the usual maximum number of weapons: to give it equipment with no slot free, enough equipment must first be abandoned. A Clockwork soldier has two equipment slots and one armour slot.

specials.name: Solitary maintenance
specials.description: Each Clockwork soldier forms a Henchmen group of his own.

specials.name: Need Orders
specials.description: At the beginning of your turn roll a D6 for each construct with no friendly Hero within 6", unless it is in close combat. On a 1-2 it may neither move nor shoot this turn.

specials.name: Brainless
specials.description: A construct gains no experience and can only be improved physically.

specials.name: In-built equipment (Clockwork fiend)
specials.description: A weapon or piece of armour given to a construct can never be taken off it again. A construct has equipment slots instead of the usual maximum number of weapons: to give it equipment with no slot free, enough equipment must first be abandoned. A Clockwork fiend has four equipment slots and one armour slot.

specials.name: Lumbering behemoth
specials.description: A Moonstone infusion on a Clockwork fiend costs twice as many orichalcum tokens for each characteristic raised.

rules.title: Corruption of the Mind and Flesh
rules.description: Whenever an enemy model, be it Hero or a Henchman of the opponents of the Warband or one of their own models dies, the Warband may opt to perform an obscene ritual to attach a part of the dying warrior into one of the Slaaneshi Beastmen, Cultist or the Slaaneshi Hounds: arm, leg, head or strips of muscle, for example. You can take one stat of the fallen warrior and replace it with the same stat of the Beastman, Cultist or Hound. We encourage players to convert the model to represent the corrupted creature with appropriate new body parts. This ritual costs 1 Wyrdstone, and 1 Hero cannot search for Rare items at the market while performing the ritual.

rules.title: Mutations
rules.description:
Any Hero may buy one of the following Mutations when you recruit them (see Cults of Possessed Rules for Mutations):
- Extra arm
- Tentacle
- Great Claw

lists.name: Wretches Equipment List
lists.note: This list is for Thralls only.

specials.name: Agony and Ecstasy
specials.type: Warband - Court of the Profane Pleasures
specials.description: The Whipmaster who is armed with a Hedonist Whip may decide to use one of its attacks to scourge one friendly model within 3". This attack automatically hits and has +1 on its rolls to wound. Roll for any injuries as standard. As a reward for such a pious act of devotion, Slaanesh rewards the Whipmaster with a surge of ecstasy that makes the Whipmaster all but invulnerable. The Whipmaster doubles its Toughness. Take a Leadership test at the start of each new turn of the Slaaneshi player. On a failure, this effect ends, though it can be re-activated.

specials.name: Pain and Pleasure
specials.type: Warband - Court of the Profane Pleasures
specials.description: Whenever the Whipmaster suffers an unsaved wound, they will be subject to the rules of Frenzy until the end of their next turn — this Frenzy is not negated by being Knocked Down or Stunned.

specials.name: Strange Allure
specials.type: Warband - Court of the Profane Pleasures
specials.description: An enemy wishing to attack a Danseuse in melee combat or with a missile attack must pass a Leadership test to do so before making its attacks. On a failure, the model must re-roll any successful hits.

specials.name: Pound of Flesh
specials.type: Warband - Court of the Profane Pleasures
specials.description: Before the battle, you may decide to give one of the Wretches to the Flesh Merchant to carry as a “meat shield” as part of the Merchant’s Equipment. When the Flesh Merchant suffers a wound for any reason, you may elect to let the slave take the hit instead. In this case the Slave is taken Out of Action and removed from the game. The Wretch can make its normal Attacks in melee if used as a Meat Shield. The model does not have a base of its own, and cannot be targeted by enemy attacks. If the Merchant dies, the Wretch is lost with it.

specials.name: Cruel Fate
specials.type: Warband - Court of the Profane Pleasures
specials.description: Any captives the warband gains through combat results or exploration can be turned into Wretches at no cost. This is achieved via lobotomy, torture and other acts of depravity.

specials.name: Flesh Reserve
specials.type: Warband - Court of the Profane Pleasures
specials.description: Before the battle, you may decide to give one of the Wretches to the Priest to carry as a “sacrificial pawn” as part of the Priest’s Equipment. When the Priest fails to cast a spell, they can choose to sacrifice the Wretch to re-roll the spell roll. The Wretch can make its normal Attacks in melee until it’s alive. The model does not have a base of its own and cannot be targeted by enemy attacks. If the Priest dies, the Wretch is lost with it.

specials.name: Fluctuating Form
specials.type: Warband - Court of the Profane Pleasures
specials.description: At the beginning of the battle, and every turn in the Recovery phase, if not engaged in close combat, you may choose whether the Devout manifests in male or female aspect. If you choose male, the Devout gains +1 WS, S, A, and T. If you choose female aspect, you gain +1 BS, +2 I, +2 Ld and +2 M.

specials.name: Animal
specials.type: Warband - Court of the Profane Pleasures
specials.description: Chaos Hounds are animals and never gain any experience.

specials.name: Slaves to Darkness
specials.type: Warband - Court of the Profane Pleasures
specials.description: Wretches are Immune to all psychology and All Alone tests if within 6" of a friendly Hero. Wretches can’t become Heroes. If you roll The Lad’s Got Talent result on the chart, and then roll it again, the model receives a Serious Injury as if it were a Hero (roll it immediately).

rules.title: Mutations
rules.description:
Those who dwell in Mordheim soon develop horrible mutations, and the Cult of the Possessed seem to be especially susceptible. In addition, Mordheim attracts mutants from all over the Empire, who are always quick to join the Chaos covens. Most mutations are simply inconvenient or hideous, but some make their bearers extremely dangerous in combat.

Mutations may be bought for a Mutant or a Possessed warrior only when they are recruited; you may not buy new mutations for a model after recruitment. Any Mutant or Possessed may have one or more mutations. The first mutation is bought at the price indicated, but second and subsequent mutations bought for the same model cost double.

lists.name: Possessed Equipment
lists.note: The following lists are used by Possessed warbands to pick their equipment.

lists.name: Darksouls Equipment List
lists.note: This list is for Darksouls and Beastmen only.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any models in the warband within 6" of the Magister may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Magic User
specials.description: The Magister has the ability to use magic and casts spells like any other magicians, and the Magister starts with one spells generated at random from the Chaos Rituals In addition the Magister may learn a new Spell instead of a new skill.

fighters.name: The Possessed
fighters.fixed_kit: None. The Possessed never use weapons or armour.

specials.name: Mutations
specials.description: Possessed may start the game with one or more mutations each. See the Mutations list for costs.

specials.name: Mutations (Mutants)
specials.description: Mutants must start the game with one or more mutations each. See the Mutations list for the cost.

specials.name: Crazed
specials.description: Darksouls have been driven insane by daemonic possession and know no fear. They automatically pass any Leadership tests they are required to take.

rules.title: Dwarf special rules
rules.description: Every special rule of a Dwarf warband applies.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any Dwarf within 6" of the Dwarf Leader may use his Leadership for any Leadership test.

specials.name: Items of devotion
specials.description: The Priest starts with one vial of Blessed Water.

specials.name: Sworn to die
specials.description: A Slayer may never wear armour and never carries a missile weapon.

specials.name: Zombie rules
specials.description: Every Zombie rule applies to a Shadow-self.

specials.name: Ghoul rules
specials.description: Every Ghoul rule applies to a Dwarf Ghoul.

rules.title: Specialists
rules.description:
The Captain may ask for one Specialist of the Black Ark to join a raid, one per battle. A Specialist is hired for nothing, does not count towards the maximum warband size, gains no experience and must carry exactly the equipment listed for him.

In the battle he counts as an ordinary member of the warband (rout tests, the Captain's Leadership and the like) and adds 10 to the warband rating. He explores with the warband if he survived, and afterwards returns to the Black Ark and leaves it. The Captain may not ask for the same Specialist two battles in a row.

After the battle the warband pays half of its earnings in gold crowns, rounding up, in tax, and his replacement cost on top if he came to harm. A warband that cannot pay at once spends no gold crowns in later battles until the debt is cleared, and may use no Specialist while it is in debt.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Captain may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Hardened
specials.description: The Captain is immune to fear.

specials.name: Slaver
specials.description: A captured result the Captain's warband rolls may only be dealt with by selling the captive into slavery.

specials.name: Elite
specials.description: Shades never roll for The Lad's Got Talent: they will not give up their trade to become heroes.

rules.title: Kindred Hatred
rules.description: The Dark Elves have been fighting the High Elves for many centuries. The wars between these two races have been very long and bloody affairs. Dark Elves Hate any High Elf warriors including High Elf Hired Swords.

rules.title: Excellent Sight
rules.description: Elves have eyesight unmatched by mere humans. All the Elves in a Dark Elves Warband can spot Hidden enemies from twice as far away as other warriors (i.e. twice their Initiative in inches).

rules.title: Black Powder Weapons
rules.description: Dark Elves may never use black powder weapons as they find them too crude, noisy and unreliable.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any models in the warband within 6" of the High Born may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Cold One Beasthound
specials.description: The Beastmaster may be accompanied by up to two Cold One Beasthounds, these are bought as henchmen and follow all rules for listed for them.

specials.name: Melee Specialists
specials.description: Fellblades live by a strict code of close quarter fighting. Fellblades may not use missile weapons of any sort.

specials.name: Natural Stealth
specials.description: The first thing that Dark Elf Scouts master is the art of moving without being seen or heard. If a Dark Elf is Hiding, enemy models suffer -1 to their Initiative value for determining if they can detect him.

fighters.name: Cold One Beasthound
fighters.fixed_kit: Cold One Beasthounds are animals and do not need any weapons save their claws and massive jaws.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Cold One Beasthounds are animals and all animal rules apply to them, they never gain experience.

specials.name: Beastmaster
specials.description: Cold One Beasthounds are nasty viscous brutes that are barely kept under control. If the Beastmaster dies the beasts will immediately escape from the warband and they are removed from the warband roster. If the Beastmaster is unable to participate in a battle, then neither will the beasts.

specials.name: Stupidity (Cold One Beasthounds)
specials.description: Cold One Beasthounds may use the basic Leadership of the Beastmaster if they are within 6" of him. They may never use the Leadership of the warband leader, nor may they benefit from the Beastmaster’s increased Leadership if he is within 6" of the leader.

specials.name: Scaly Skin (Cold One Beasthounds)
specials.description: Cold One Beasthounds have tough scaly skin, and are considered to have a 6+ armour save. This save cannot be modified beyond 6 due to strength modifiers but any result of ‘no save’ on the Critical Hit chart will negate the unmodified 6+ save.

rules.title: Squires
rules.description: A warband may never have more Squires than Questing Knights.

rules.title: Men-at-Arms
rules.description: A warband may have no more than 4 Men-at-Arms for each Questing Knight.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Prophet may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Corrupting Influence
specials.description: After each battle every untainted Questing Knight of the warband tests for corruption, as the Questing Knight's Corruption rule says. Should the Prophet die, a corrupt Knight leads the warband before an untainted one, and gains this rule when he does.

specials.name: His Master's Gift
specials.description:
When the Prophet gains a skill he may roll 2D6 on the Gifts of Tzeentch table instead.

2D6 | Gift
2-3 | The Master's Foresight: he may re-roll one dice in each battle, but not in the post-battle sequence. Add +1 to his next roll on this table, once only.
4 | Unfit!: he loses 1 Weapon Skill for good, and fights on.
5 | Twisted Fate: for the next D6 turns, if he goes out of action and his injury roll is anything but Dead, he rolls again at once and takes the second result as well.
6-8 | Silence: nothing happens.
9 | Tzeentch's Temperament: before each battle roll a D6. On an even number he has -1 Initiative and -1 Weapon Skill, on an odd number +1 Initiative and +1 Weapon Skill.
10 | Energy Surge: one characteristic chosen at random rises by 1, to a maximum of 10. It may pass his racial maximum, and no characteristic may be raised this way twice.
11 | Mutation: roll a random mutation and pay its price. If it cannot be paid he has the mutation for the next battle only.
12 | Chaos Armour: a 3+ armour save, including a shield, with no Movement penalty, and he may cast spells while wearing it. Any armour he wore fuses to him. It may never be passed to another warrior and may not be removed.

specials.name: Knights Virtue
specials.description: An untainted Questing Knight never breaks from combat and takes no All Alone test. He loses this when he becomes corrupt.

specials.name: Corruption
specials.description: After each battle an untainted Questing Knight takes a Leadership test, with +1 to the roll if he took any model out of action that game. If he passes he stays untainted. If he fails he becomes corrupt and rolls at once on the Gifts of Tzeentch table. On a double 1 he instead leaves the warband with his Squire: remove both from the roster.

specials.name: His Master's Gift (Questing Knight)
specials.description: Once he is corrupt, when the Knight gains a skill he may roll 2D6 on the Gifts of Tzeentch table instead, as the Prophet's His Master's Gift rule sets it out.

specials.name: Oath of Servitude
specials.description: Choose which Questing Knight a new Squire serves; a Knight may have only one Squire at a time. If his Knight becomes corrupt, so does the Squire.

specials.name: In His Lord's Footsteps
specials.description: When his Knight dies the Squire becomes a Questing Knight. He takes any armour his master carried, buys from the Maldred's Disciples list, counts towards the warband's two Questing Knights, may have a Squire of his own, and follows the Questing Knight's rules and skill lists.

specials.name: Sell-sword
specials.description: Before the warband's first game a Mercenary Guard may be equipped from the Mercenaries warband's equipment list. After that he buys only from the Squires and Men-at-Arms lists.

rules.title: Chosen of Morr
rules.description: When the warband is made, the Priest of Morr rolls a D6: on a 4+ the warband may hire the Dreamer. Otherwise the Priest rejects him and leads the warband himself; after its next battle the warband may try again, paying the Dreamer's cost as normal. A genuine Dreamer is the leader until he dies, when the Priest leads again. Once a genuine Dreamer has died, the warband may never hire another.

rules.title: No Fear of the Dead
rules.description: Warriors of the warband feel no fear when fighting vampires, necromancers and their undead.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The warband may hire any hired sword a Human Mercenary, Witch Hunters or Sisters of Sigmar warband may, but none of a necromantic or chaotic nature.

rules.title: Alliances
rules.description: In multiplayer games the warband may never ally with a warband of a necromantic or chaotic nature (Undead, Possessed, Skaven, Beastmen, Dark Elves and the like).

rules.title: Hate Undead
rules.description: Every Hero of the warband hates all vampires, necromancers and undead.

rules.title: New Skills
rules.description: A Hero who gains a new skill on an advance chooses from the rulebook's skill lists under the same restrictions as Witch Hunters and Sisters of Sigmar.

specials.name: Leader Without a Dreamer
specials.description: While the warband has no genuine Dreamer, the Priest of Morr leads it (Chosen of Morr): warriors within 6" of him may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Funerary Rites
specials.description: The Priest of Morr is no wizard, but chooses a Funerary Rite, using the rules for magic. Instead of a skill from the Academic or Speed lists, an advance may roll a new rite from the Funerary Rites.

specials.name: Loner
specials.description: The Priest of Morr never takes All Alone tests.

specials.name: Dagger and Scythe
specials.description: The Priest of Morr may carry only a dagger and a scythe as weapons, and may never wear armour.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Dreamer may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Guiding Dream
specials.description:
At the start of each battle the Dreamer rolls a D6 on the Guiding Dream table:

D6 | Vision
1 | Disturbing Vision: the Dreamer has -1" Movement.
2-3 | Vision of Truth: choose one of the opponent's Heroes; the Dreamer has +1 to hit him.
4-5 | Empowering Vision: choose one of the opponent's Heroes; the Dreamer has +1 Strength when fighting him.
6 | Infuriating Vision: choose one of the opponent's Heroes; the Dreamer is frenzied against him.

specials.name: Silent Guardian
specials.description: While a Black Guard is hidden, enemies must pass an Initiative test to spot him. He never suffers movement penalties for wearing armour.

specials.name: Warhorse
specials.description: With the optional mounted rules or the Blazing Saddles rules, a Black Guard may ride a Warhorse (M8 WS3 BS0 S3 T3 W1 I3 A1 Ld5), paying its cost; his save is then 4+ while mounted.

specials.name: Estalian Technique
specials.description: The Andanti may parry with his rapier and his main gauche if he rolls under his Weapon Skill and no higher than his opponent's highest roll to hit, as the normal parry rules.

specials.name: Andanti Knowledge
specials.description: The Andanti has +1 to hit in close combat against a vampire.

specials.name: Expert Halberdier
specials.description: A Death's Head may fight with his halberd in one hand and a shield in the other.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The warband may hire the hired swords an Undead warband may hire.

rules.title: Wet Powder
rules.description: A blackpowder weapon of the warband never hits on better than a 4 or more, whatever its Ballistic Skill, Weapon Skill and modifiers, shooting or in close combat.

rules.title: Drowned
rules.description: Water of any depth is difficult ground for the warband, rather than very difficult or impassable.

rules.title: No Armour
rules.description: The warband wears no armour: a model may appear to wear pieces of it, but they have no effect in play.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior in the warband within 6" of the Captain may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Necromancer
specials.description: The Surgeon is a spell caster and starts with one spell from the Necromancy list. Where that list says zombies, read Bloated.

specials.name: Rigging Gear
specials.description: Each Topsman comes with a Rope & Hook.

fighters.name: Bloated
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Bloated use no weapons or equipment and suffer no penalty for being unarmed.

specials.name: No Brain
specials.description: Bloated never gain experience.

specials.name: No Skill
specials.description: Bloated use no equipment. They may carry what they held in life, but it counts as no more than a bludgeon; they suffer no penalty for being unarmed.

fighters.name: Jolly Boat
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Neither the boat, its Helmsman nor the Bloated pulling it use weapons or equipment, and they suffer no penalty for being unarmed.

specials.name: Corpse Cart
specials.description: While the warband holds the Jolly Boat its maximum number of warriors is 3 higher, 15 in all, counting the Jolly Boat as one.

specials.name: Helmsman
specials.description: The Helmsman comes with the boat and is bonded to it. He may never leave it, and cannot be injured unless the Jolly Boat is destroyed, in which case he is destroyed with it.

specials.name: Bloated
specials.description: The two to four Bloated that drag the boat are pinned to its hull and may never leave it. They may not run, but may charge normally.

specials.name: No Brain (Jolly Boat)
specials.description: Neither the boat, its Helmsman nor the Bloated pulling it gain experience.

specials.name: Sail the Damned Seas
specials.description: The Jolly Boat may not go up stairs or ladders, but may be dragged over obstacles such as walls and barriers. It counts as a large target for shooting. Where a scenario has loot to carry, it counts as up to four models for carrying chests, shards, corpses and prisoners.

specials.name: Cursèd Eternal
specials.description: If the Jolly Boat is taken out of action, the boat, its Helmsman and the Bloated pulling it suffer it together. Leave the wreck on the table as an obstacle to hide behind and clamber over. After the battle it is lost from the warband only on a roll of 1, rather than the henchman's usual 1 or 2; on a 2 or more it fights in the next battle as normal.

rules.title: Kindred Hatred
rules.description: Dark Elves hate every High Elf warrior, High Elf hired swords included.

rules.title: Fey Acuity
rules.description: In the exploration phase, add +1 to the number of wyrdstone pieces or artefacts the warband finds, as long as at least one Hero searched.

rules.title: Disdain
rules.description: Dark Elves may never use black powder weapons.

rules.title: Slavers
rules.description: When the warband finds prisoners (a roll of 333 in the exploration phase), it may use the Skaven's rules for them.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The warband may hire only these hired swords: Pit Fighter, Ogre Bodyguard, Warlock, Imperial Assassin, Tilean Marksman, Highwayman, Duelist, Witch, Emissary of Chaos, Human Scout, Old Prospector, Dark Elf Assassin, Pathfinder, Nomad Scout, Thief and Shade Scout.

rules.title: Promoted Henchmen
rules.description: A henchman who becomes a Hero still buys from his henchman list, never the Druchii Heroes list.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Noble may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Armoured Casting
specials.description: The Sorceress may wear armour from her list, but can't cast spells while she wears it.

specials.name: Slavehounds
specials.description: Up to three Slavehounds may accompany the Beastmaster. They are bought as henchmen.

specials.name: Sea Dragon Cloaks
specials.description: Corsairs may wear Sea Dragon Cloaks though they are not Heroes.

specials.name: Natural Stealth
specials.description: While a Shade is hidden, enemy models use half their Initiative to see whether they spot it.

specials.name: Maibd Poison
specials.description: A warband with Witch Elves may buy Black Lotus as a Common item at 5 gc a dose. Lotus bought this way is for Witch Elves only, must be used in the next battle, and can't be sold or traded.

fighters.name: Slavehound
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Slavehounds are animals and need no weapons.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Slavehounds are animals and never gain experience. The warband may have them only if it has a Beastmaster.

specials.name: Beastmaster
specials.description: While the Beastmaster is within 6" and not knocked down, stunned or out of action, a Slavehound may take any Leadership test on his Leadership instead of its own; it can never use the leader's. If the Beastmaster can't fight in a battle, nor can the Slavehounds, and with no Beastmaster they stay in camp.

specials.name: Pack Work
specials.description: When a Slavehound knows where an enemy model is (it sees it, or has found it hidden), the Beastmaster and every other Slavehound of the warband may declare a charge against that model even without seeing it, with no Initiative roll.

rules.title: Hard to Kill
rules.description: On the injury chart a Dwarf of the warband is knocked down on a 1 or 2, stunned on a 3, 4 or 5, and taken out of action only on a 6.

rules.title: Hard Head
rules.description: A Dwarf of the warband ignores the special rules for maces, clubs and the like.

rules.title: Armour
rules.description: A Dwarf of the warband never suffers a movement penalty for wearing armour.

rules.title: Hate Orcs and Goblins
rules.description: Every Dwarf of the warband hates Orcs and Goblins.

rules.title: Grudgebearers
rules.description: The warband may never take on an Elven hired sword or dramatis persona of any kind.

rules.title: Incomparable Miners
rules.description: Add +1 to the number of wyrdstone shards the warband finds at the end of a battle.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior in the warband within 6" of the Thane may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Rune Wizard
specials.description: The Runesmith is no wizard and does not follow the rules for wizards, but he casts runes as spells.

specials.name: My Lord, Watch It!
specials.description: When the Thane is charged, the Oath Guard may intercept from within 4" instead of 2".

specials.name: The Oath Is Broken
specials.description: If the Thane dies the Oath Guard becomes a Slayer and gains the Deathwish rule. He may never again carry or use a missile weapon or any armour, and he learns from the Slayer special skills. He may never become the leader, and no new Oath Guard may be hired. Every skill he has already learnt he keeps.

rules.title: Hard to Kill
rules.description: Dwarfs are taken out of action only on a 6 on the Injury chart: 1-2 is knocked down, 3-5 stunned and 6 out of action.

rules.title: Hard Head
rules.description: Dwarfs ignore the special rules of clubs, maces and the like.

rules.title: Armour
rules.description: Dwarfs never suffer movement penalties for wearing armour.

rules.title: Hate Orcs and Goblins
rules.description: All Dwarfs hate Orcs and Goblins.

rules.title: Grudgebearers
rules.description: The warband may never include an Elven Hired Sword or Dramatis Persona of any kind.

rules.title: Shame
rules.description:
A Dwarf Hero taken out of action in either of the ways below is so shamed that he becomes a Trollslayer. He loses any special ability, Leader among them, but keeps his skills; he is immune to psychology, and he may learn the Troll Slayer special skills from the rulebook. Except for the leader, his place may be taken by another Dwarf at the next recruiting phase; if the leader becomes a Trollslayer, choose another leader as if he had died.

Taken out of action in the Dwarf player's first or second turn.

Taken out of action in single combat by an opponent with Weapon Skill 2 or Strength 2, or by an animal.

rules.title: Miners
rules.description: Up to 3 man-sized models (no ogres and the like) may be placed anywhere on the table at the end of the first turn, no closer than 8" to any enemy model.

rules.title: Engineers
rules.description: While a Dwarf Weaponsmith or a Master Craftsman is in the warband, every missile weapon of the warband has 6" added to its range.

rules.title: Brewers
rules.description:
A Dwarf Brewer brings a barrel of his finest brew to each battle, and the leader lets D3 of his Heroes drink before the battle. Only Dwarfs may drink it. Name the models who drink, then roll a D6 for each:

D6 | Brew
1-2 | XXXXXX: the warrior is immune to fear for the rest of the battle.
3-4 | Troll Brew: the warrior is subject to frenzy for the rest of the battle.
5-6 | Special Brew: the warrior's Weapon Skill and Strength are each +1 for the rest of the battle. This may take him above his racial maximum, but never above 10.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any model in the warband within 6" of the Dwarf Master Craftsman may use his Leadership instead of his own.

rules.title: Don’t Trust ‘Em
rules.description:
While Ranger Warbands are free to ally with other Dwarf warbands in multi-player games, their point of view is so different that they do not trust them fully. Members of a Dwarf Rangers warband are never considered ‘friendly models’ to other dwarfs and vice versa.

This means that members of one warband WILL stop members of the other from Marching, they won’t keep each other from taking all alone tests, etc. They don’t count as enemy models and may split any treasure found at the end of the game as normal, but the two bands are not friends, make no mistake!

All Dwarfs are subject to the following special rules:

rules.title: Hard to Kill
rules.description: Dwarfs are tough, resilient individuals who can only be taken out of action on a roll of 6 instead of 5-6 when rolling on the Injury chart. Treat a roll of 1-2 as knocked down, 3-5 as stunned, and 6 as out of action.

rules.title: Hard Head
rules.description: Dwarfs ignore the special rules for maces, clubs, etc. They are not easy to knock out!

rules.title: Armour
rules.description: Dwarfs never suffer movement penalties for wearing armour.

rules.title: Hate Orcs and Goblins
rules.description: All Dwarfs hate Orcs and Goblins. See the psychology section of the Mordheim rules for details on the effects of hatred.

rules.title: Grudgebearers
rules.description: Dwarfs hold an ancient grudge against Elves from the days when the two races fought for supremacy in the Old World. A Dwarf warband may never include any kind of Elven Hired Sword or Dramatis Personae.

rules.title: Incomparable Miners
rules.description: Dwarfs spend much of their lives underground searching for precious minerals, and they are the best in the world at this kind of work. In the city of Mordheim they apply similar skills to the search for wyrdstone. When checking for wyrdstone at the end of a game, add +1 to the number of pieces found for a Dwarf warband.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any models in the warband within 6" of the Dwarf Runesmith may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Inscribe Runes
specials.description: A Runesmith knows one minor rune (see list at the end of this warband list), determined randomly when the warband is first created. He may inscribe the rune on an item carried by one of the warriors of his warband, and (if successful, see below) the item will gain a bonus from the rune for that game. When a Runesmith advances and rolls a skill on the Hero Advance table, he may choose to learn a new rune instead of learning a skill (exactly like a spellcaster advancing and learning a new spell).

specials.name: Extra Set of Hands
specials.description: An Apprentice Runesmith helps his master fashion runic items, doing all the boring grunge-work that makes his master more efficient in his efforts. An Apprentice Runesmith in the warband allows a Master Runesmith to inscribe on two items before each game, instead of only one.

specials.name: Deathwish
specials.description: Troll Slayers seek an honourable death in combat. They are completely immune to all psychology and never need to test if fighting alone.

specials.name: Stubborn
specials.description:
Dwarf Longbeards have seen just about everything in their long careers and they know it. They are used to fighting by themselves against impossible odds and it hasn’t killed them yet. On top of all this they are just generally more set in their ways than other Dwarfs and they’re not about to let a bunch of weedy goblins drive them off!

A Dwarf Longbeard may reroll any failed Leadership test he is required to take. Remember that you can never reroll a reroll, so the result of this second roll must always be accepted.

rules.title: Deathwish
rules.description: Unless his own rules say otherwise, every Slayer is immune to all psychology, Hatred, Frenzy and Stupidity included, and never tests for fighting alone.

rules.title: No Armour, No Toys!
rules.description: Slayers may never use armour of any kind, nor a cloak that gives a constant save bonus (Lucky Charms are allowed). They may use no missile weapons but thrown ones, and may never learn magic.

rules.title: Hard to Kill
rules.description: Dwarfs go out of action only on a 6 on the Injury chart: 1-2 is knocked down, 3-5 stunned and 6 out of action.

rules.title: Hard Head
rules.description: Dwarfs ignore the special rules of maces, clubs and the like.

rules.title: Grudgebearers
rules.description: The warband may never include an Elven hired sword or dramatis persona.

rules.title: Damnable Luck
rules.description: After the battle, once every injury has been rolled, you may re-roll one Death result for a single Slayer Hero or henchman. The second result stands.

rules.title: Only in Victory
rules.description: Slayer Heroes gain exploration dice only if the warband won the scenario, was allied with the winner, or tied; never when it was defeated or routed. This doesn't apply to the Rememberer.

rules.title: Record of Valor
rules.description: When a Slayer Hero is taken out of action while the Rememberer is on the table, the warband gets +1 exploration die after the battle. It counts only when an enemy or a hostile NPC took him out, directly or not (a warrior's attack, a fall after being shot, a hostile random event); a Slayer who goes out of action with no one else's doing (walking off a cliff, failing a jump) gives none. A Slayer brought back to the battle loses the die.

rules.title: Back-up Records
rules.description: A Bard hired sword in the warband also has Record of Valor. The two don't stack: a Slayer taken out of action gives at most one die, whoever saw it.

rules.title: Gromril Weapons
rules.description: Any weapon a Dwarf may buy may be bought as a Gromril weapon (see the rulebook) at three times its cost. That price is only for a starting warband; later Gromril weapons are bought at the rulebook's or the campaign's price.

rules.title: The Rite of Trollslaying
rules.description: When a Slayer henchman takes out of action an enemy that was Large and started the game with more than one wound, after the battle he gains enough experience for his next advance (16 if he is at the most) and counts as rolling "That Lad's Got Talent!". With six Heroes already, you may roll a henchman advance instead of replacing one.

rules.title: The Rite of Dragonslaying
rules.description: When a Slayer takes out of action a Large or gigantic scaled monster (a Hydra, Dragon, Wyvern, Sea Drake, Merwyrm, Turtigon or one of their young, among others) that has Skull of Iron or 4 or more wounds, and is an NPC or rolls a death result, he may take its hide after the battle as a free Sea Dragon Cloak, if he has none. He may wear it, though Slayers wear no armour, but can't sell or give it away, and a lost one can only be won again this way. A henchman also gains the Rite of Trollslaying, and wears the cloak even if he can't be promoted.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Giant Slayer may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Rememberer
specials.description: Once per game, a Slayer Hero within 6" of the Rememberer who is fighting a Large creature or one of Toughness 5 or more may re-roll his failed rolls to hit, once.

specials.name: Pick up the Slack
specials.description: If the Rememberer wasn't taken out of action, he may make one rarity or dramatis persona roll for each Slayer Hero taken out of action in the battle, on top of the warband's usual search.

specials.name: Not a Slayer
specials.description: The Rememberer isn't a Slayer and the Slayer rules don't apply to him. He may not learn the Slayers Only skills (Deathwish, Ferocious Charge, Monster Slayer, Berserker, Deathblow, Relentless) and may never lead the warband.

specials.name: Skittish
specials.description: As a new Slayer this model lacks Deathwish and takes psychology tests as normal. When it rolls "That Lad's Got Talent" it doesn't roll on the Hero advance table: it must learn the Deathwish skill.

specials.name: Strong Arm
specials.description: An Axe Hurler throws a thrown weapon extra inches equal to his Strength (S3: +3").

specials.name: Born Marksmen
specials.description: An Axe Hurler who rolls "That Lad's Got Talent" may always pick Shooting as one of his two skill lists, even with no Hero in the warband who has Shooting skills. Even with Weapons Training he may use no missile weapon but a thrown one.

specials.name: Skittish
specials.description: As a new Slayer this model lacks Deathwish and takes psychology tests as normal. When it rolls "That Lad's Got Talent" it doesn't roll on the Hero advance table: it must learn the Deathwish skill.

rules.title: Hard to Kill
rules.description: Dwarfs are taken out of action only on a 6 on the Injury chart: 1-2 is knocked down, 3-5 stunned and 6 out of action.

rules.title: Hard Head
rules.description: Dwarfs ignore the special rules of clubs, maces and the like.

rules.title: Armour
rules.description: Dwarfs never suffer movement penalties for wearing armour.

rules.title: Hate Orcs and Goblins
rules.description: All Dwarfs hate Orcs and Goblins.

rules.title: Grudgebearers
rules.description: The warband may never include an Elven Hired Sword or Dramatis Persona of any kind.

rules.title: Mighty Doom
rules.description: The warband takes no Rout tests until half of it has been taken out of action, and may never rout voluntarily.

rules.title: Shame
rules.description:
A Dwarf Hero who is not already a Slayer and is taken out of action in either of the ways below takes his vows and becomes a Slayer. He loses any special ability, Leader among them, but keeps his skills; he is immune to psychology, and he may learn the Troll Slayer special skills from the rulebook.

Taken out of action in the Dwarf player's first or second turn.

Taken out of action in single combat by an opponent with Weapon Skill 2 or Strength 2, or by an animal.

rules.title: No Missiles or Armour
rules.description: A Slayer may never take a missile weapon or armour. This covers the Giant Slayer, the Troll Slayers and the Slayers; the Rememberer and the Clansmen may take both.

rules.title: Scars and Tattoos
rules.description:
A Slayer Hero may have runic scars and tattoos cut and inked into his body. One is bought between games in place of his search for rare equipment, and its difficulty is its rarity roll. None may be applied twice to multiply its effect, and three rules hold:

Rule of jealousy: a scar may be used only once in each warband.

Rule of three: no model may have more than three tattoos or scars. They may be added at different times, and once added can never be removed.

Rule of pride: no combination of tattoos and scars may be used more than once in each warband.

lists.name: Mercenary Equipment List
lists.note: The Human Rememberer only.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any model in the warband within 6" of the Giant Slayer may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: No Missiles or Armour
specials.description: He may take no missile weapon and no armour.

specials.name: No Missiles or Armour
specials.description: He may take no missile weapon and no armour.

specials.name: Hard to Find
specials.description: The warband may hold only one Rememberer, a Dwarf or a Human. Roll a D6 when you decide to recruit him: 1-4 he is a Dwarf, 5-6 he is a Human. If you do not want the one you rolled, you must wait until after your next game before trying again.

specials.name: Rememberer
specials.description: Once per game, a Slayer Hero within 6" of the Rememberer who is fighting a large creature, such as a troll or an ogre, may re-roll his failed to-hit rolls, once only.

specials.name: Hard to Find
specials.description: The warband may hold only one Rememberer, a Dwarf or a Human. Roll a D6 when you decide to recruit him: 1-4 he is a Dwarf, 5-6 he is a Human. If you do not want the one you rolled, you must wait until after your next game before trying again.

specials.name: Rememberer
specials.description: Once per game, a Slayer Hero within 6" of the Rememberer who is fighting a large creature, such as a troll or an ogre, may re-roll his failed to-hit rolls, once only.

specials.name: No Missiles or Armour (Slayer)
specials.description: A Slayer may take no missile weapon and no armour.

special.name: Scar of Gromril
special.description: The wearer has a 4+ ward save against missile fire. Rarity 8.

special.name: Scar of Steel
special.description: The wearer has a 5+ ward save against missile fire. Rarity 7.

special.name: Scar of Speed
special.description: Once per battle the wearer may triple his run or charge distance. Rarity 7.

special.name: Scar of Fear
special.description: The wearer causes fear. Rarity 8.

special.name: Scar of Fury
special.description: The wearer is subject to frenzy. Rarity 7.

special.name: Tattoo of Stone
special.description: The wearer has a 6+ ward save against missile fire. Rarity 6.

special.name: Tattoo of Passage
special.description: The wearer ignores difficult terrain and moves at his normal speed. Rarity 6.

special.name: Tattoo of Hatred
special.description: The wearer hates all enemies. Rarity 8.

special.name: Tattoo of Luck
special.description: The wearer ignores the first hit in each game. Rarity 6.

name: Dwarf Treasure Hunters
source: Town Cryer #4, revised in Mordheim Annual 2002

rules.title: Hard to Kill
rules.description: Dwarfs are tough, resilient individuals who can only be taken out of action on a roll of 6 instead of 5-6 when rolling on the Injury chart. Treat a roll of 1-2 as knocked down, 3-5 as stunned, and 6 as out of action.

rules.title: Hard Head
rules.description: Dwarfs ignore the special rules for maces, clubs, etc. They are not easy to knock out!

rules.title: Armour
rules.description: Dwarfs never suffer movement penalties for wearing armour.

rules.title: Hate Orcs and Goblins
rules.description: All Dwarfs hate Orcs and Goblins. See the psychology section of the Mordheim rules for details on the effects of hatred.

rules.title: Grudgebearers
rules.description: Dwarfs hold an ancient grudge against Elves from the days when the two races fought for supremacy in the Old World. A Dwarf warband may never include any kind of Elven Hired Sword or Dramatis Personae.

rules.title: Incomparable Miners
rules.description: Dwarfs spend much of their lives underground searching for precious minerals, and they are the best in the world at this kind of work. In the city of Mordheim they apply similar skills to the search for wyrdstone. When checking for wyrdstone at the end of a game, add +1 to the number of pieces found for a Dwarf warband.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any models in the warband within 6" of the Dwarf Noble may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Expert Weaponsmith
specials.description: A Dwarf Engineer is a master of mechanical devices. By using stronger construction materials and time-tested secrets of Dwarf engineering, a Dwarf Engineer can increase the distance the warband's missile weapons can shoot. Missile weapons bought from the warband's basic equipment lists have their range increased by 3" for pistols and 6" for crossbows and handguns. Range increases only apply in battles in which the Engineer takes part (though they do apply even if he is yet to enter the battlefield or has already been taken out of action in this battle). He has no effect on the equipment of Hired Swords.

specials.name: Deathwish
specials.description: Troll Slayers seek an honourable death in combat. They are completely immune to all psychology and never need to test if fighting alone.

specials.name: Slayer Skills
specials.description: Troll Slayers may choose a skill from the Troll Slayer Skill table instead of the normal Skill tables when they gain a new skill.

specials.name: No Missile Weapons or Armour
specials.description: Slayers may never carry or use missile weapons or any form of armour.

rules.title: Hard to Kill
rules.description: When rolling on the Injury chart for a Dwarf, treat 1-2 as knocked down, 3-5 as stunned and 6 as out of action.

rules.title: Hard Head
rules.description: A Dwarf ignores the special rules for maces, clubs and the like.

rules.title: Armour
rules.description: A Dwarf suffers no movement penalty for wearing armour. A Slayer will never wear armour of any kind other than runic tattoos: armour he gains through exploration is sold at the next shop he visits for whatever it fetches.

rules.title: Hate Orcs and Goblins
rules.description: Every Dwarf hates Orcs and Goblins.

rules.title: Grudgebearers
rules.description: The warband may never include an Elven Hired Sword of any kind.

rules.title: Resistant
rules.description: A Dwarf affected by a spell gains a 6+ resistance save, and the spell has no effect on him if he passes it. Each model rolls on its own, so where a spell covers an area the models that pass are unaffected and the ones that fail are not.

rules.title: Slayers
rules.description: The warband may ignore the first two Rout tests it is required to take, and may never rout voluntarily.

rules.title: Close Combat
rules.description: Slayers never buy long-range weapons, and sell any they are given at once for whatever they fetch. Thrown weapons do not count as long-range weapons.

rules.title: Academic Skills
rules.description: A Slayer may take any Academic skill that does not deal with magic.

rules.title: Heroes
rules.description: Only four Heroes may be hired. The other two may come only from "Lad's Got Talent" rolls.

rules.title: Explore On
rules.description: Every Hero rolls for exploration even when he was taken out of action, but rolls one D3 instead of one D6. A Hero who was not taken out of action still rolls a D6. Henchmen do not roll when taken out of action.

rules.title: Shops
rules.description: Slayers may visit the Dwarf Outpost, the Runesmith and the Human Shop.

rules.title: Runic Tattoos
rules.description: Only Heroes may buy runic tattoos, and no Hero may buy the same tattoo twice. A Henchman may have only ordinary tattoos, which do nothing in the game; a Henchman who becomes a Hero may buy runic tattoos. At the start of a campaign only the Daemon Slayer and the Dragon Slayer may buy them, and each pays 5 gold crowns less than the price listed; the discount is gone on every visit after that.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any model in the warband within 8" of the Daemon Slayer may use his Leadership.

specials.name: Doomed
specials.description: A Daemon Slayer is immune to all psychology and to All Alone tests.

specials.name: Monster-killer
specials.description: A Daemon Slayer automatically wounds any model of Toughness 8 or lower on a 4+, or on less where the To Wound chart needs less.

specials.name: Respected
specials.description: The Dragon Slayer does not lead the warband, but any model in the warband within 4" of him may use his Leadership.

specials.name: Doomed
specials.description: A Daemon Slayer is immune to all psychology and to All Alone tests.

specials.name: Monster-killer (Dragon Slayer)
specials.description: A Dragon Slayer automatically wounds any model of Toughness 7 or lower on a 4+, or on less where the To Wound chart needs less.

specials.name: Doomed (Giant Slayer)
specials.description: A Giant Slayer is immune to fear and to All Alone tests.

specials.name: Monster-killer (Giant Slayer)
specials.description: A Giant Slayer automatically wounds any model of Toughness 6 or lower on a 4+, or on less where the To Wound chart needs less.

specials.name: Doomed (Goblin Slayer)
specials.description: A Goblin Slayer is immune to All Alone tests.

specials.name: Monster-killer (Goblin Slayer)
specials.description: A Goblin Slayer automatically wounds any model of Toughness 5 or lower on a 4+, or on less where the To Wound chart needs less.

specials.name: Doomed (Skaven Slayer)
specials.description: A Skaven Slayer is immune to all psychology and to All Alone tests while he is frenzied, and immune to fear while he is not.

specials.name: Monster-killer (Troll Slayer)
specials.description: A Troll Slayer automatically wounds any model of Toughness 5 or lower on a 4+, or on less where the To Wound chart needs less.

specials.name: Doomed (Troll Slayer)
specials.description: A Troll Slayer is immune to fear and to All Alone tests.

specials.name: Monster-killer (Squig Slayer)
specials.description: A Squig Slayer automatically wounds any model of Toughness 5 or lower on a 4+, or on less where the To Wound chart needs less. This applies to his thrown weapons too.

specials.name: Doomed (Squig Slayer)
specials.description: A Squig Slayer is immune to fear and to All Alone tests.

specials.name: Throwing
specials.description: A Squig Slayer armed with two thrown weapons may throw each of them in the Shooting phase, shooting twice in the turn.

special.name: Stok Gloves
special.description: He may re-roll one attack that failed to hit, and the second roll stands. This works with any close combat weapon.

special.name: Ok Band
special.description: He always strikes before his enemy in close combat, but with one attack only unless he would have struck first anyway. It does nothing for a double-handed weapon, which always strikes last.

special.name: Klad Swirls
special.description: He gains a 6+ armour save, which may not be modified.

special.name: Uzkul Signs
special.description: He causes fear and is immune to fear himself.

special.name: Zharr Marks
special.description: All his attacks count as burning and do double wounds against anything susceptible to fire, his unarmed attacks and his thrown weapons included. He never suffers the penalties for fighting unarmed, and always counts as armed with a sword that may not parry.

special.name: Skrund Bracelets
special.description: He may charge his normal Movement +D3".

special.name: Drung Stripes
special.description: He gains a 4+ resistance roll against spells of every kind. This is used in place of the warband's Resistant rule, which no longer applies to him.

special.name: Azul Spirals
special.description: He is immune to all psychology and to All Alone tests.

special.name: Hunk Symbols
special.description: Any enemy charging him takes D3" off his charge distance. If he then fails to reach him, the rules for a failed charge apply.

rules.title: Swabbies
rules.description: The warband's Swabbies are human, and are captured rather than hired, under the Sartosa campaign rules.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The warband hires Hired Swords and buys other items as a human Mercenary warband does. A warband holding both Dwarfs and Elves pays 20 gold crowns more in upkeep.

rules.title: Swivel Guns are Rare, Matey!
rules.description: The warband may not start a campaign game with a Swivel Gun on its roster. In a one-off game it may buy one for 2D6 gold crowns more.

rules.title: Succession
rules.description: If the Captain is killed, one of the Mates takes his place, as a Champion does in a Mercenary warband.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any pirate within 6" of the Captain may use his Leadership for any Leadership test.

specials.name: Swivel Guns is Dangerous, Matey!
specials.description: A Gunner carrying the Swivel Gun always counts as an individual and may never be joined by anyone else. Since the warband may hold only one Swivel Gun, the Gunner carrying it is either newly hired or split off from his group, keeping the experience and skills he had.

fighters.name: Boatswain
fighters.fixed_kit: A Rope & Hook, which he may never sell or give away.

specials.name: Expert Riggers
specials.description: A Boatswain may re-roll a failed Initiative test for leaping over a gap, jumping down or making a diving charge, and the test for climbing up or down with a rope.

specials.name: Not Hired
specials.description: Swabbies are not hired: they are captured, under the Sartosa campaign rules.

specials.name: Never Gain Experience
specials.description: Swabbies never gain experience.

specials.name: Rabble
specials.description: Swabbies need not be armed alike: each may carry different equipment, but only from the Swabbie Equipment list. A Swabbie may never use magic or cast a spell.

specials.name: 'Blimey, they got away!'
specials.description: If the warband routs, any Swabbie who has already left the table in an earlier turn escapes for good: remove him from the roster as if he had been killed.

specials.name: 'Don't mind them mates, they ain't true pirates!'
specials.description: Swabbies who are running away or have been taken out of action do not count towards the warband's rout test.

rules.title: Immune to Drugs and Poison
rules.description: Every Fen Guard warrior is immune to drugs and poison, but not to disease.

rules.title: Fear of Fire
rules.description: Active fires, enemies with torches and any flame on the battlefield cause fear in Fen Guard warriors.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The warband may hire only Elf hired swords.

rules.title: Bark Skin
rules.description: Fen Guard warriors have a 6+ armour save, added to any armour worn. Strength modifiers can't take it past 6 (weapons with the Cutting Edge rule excepted), but a 'no save' result on a Critical Hit chart removes it. Not against fire attacks.

rules.title: Hard to Rattle
rules.description: Every Fen Guard warrior counts as wearing a helmet: a 4+ save against being stunned. Not against fire attacks.

rules.title: Forest and Swamp Walk
rules.description: Fen Guard warriors move through swamp and forest terrain without penalty.

rules.title: Grown Weapons
rules.description: A Fen Guard warrior's weapons grow from him: he can't be disarmed, and keeps his weapons if captured. Weapons can't be moved from one warrior to another, and one taken from a warrior is lost. Weapons found in the campaign may only be sold.

rules.title: Regrowth
rules.description: A Fen Guard warrior with a serious injury may spend a later skill advance to regrow it, striking it from the roster.

rules.title: Natural State
rules.description: Fen Guard warriors never wear cloaks, boots or armour other than those listed on their starting profile, and never visit a post-game location in Marienburg or any other city.

rules.title: Untainted
rules.description: A warrior who gains an actual mutation rolls on the Serious Injury table (Captured and Sold to the Pits ignored), and the mutation is removed.

rules.title: Variation
rules.description: A warrior may start with one Variation when hired, and may choose a new one when he rolls a double for an advance. Variations are bought from the mutation list at the listed price, and don't count as mutations for other rules (Holy Water): Vine (Tentacle), Branch (Extra Arm), Thick Leaves (Cloud of Flies), Dense Trunk (Hulking Brute), Thorns (Spines), Spores (Blackblood), and perhaps Nesting Bird (Beak).

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Branchwych may take Leadership tests on her Leadership.

specials.name: Eternal
specials.description: The Branchwych may ignore any Serious Injury result except Killed by taking a permanent -1 to her starting Wounds; not with 1 starting Wound left. On a Killed result she instead loses D3 starting Wounds for good; at 0 or less she is killed as normal.

specials.name: Feed Upon Magic
specials.description: Between battles, by consuming D3 Treasures, the Branchwych gains a permanent +1 to her starting Wounds. Not if she searches for rare items, or was taken out of action in the last battle. Without enough Treasures they are all consumed anyway and she gains nothing.

specials.name: Advancement
specials.description: On an advance roll of +1 Wound the Branchwych may pick a new skill from her lists instead.

specials.name: Instinctual
specials.description: The Branchnymph can never be the warband's leader. Fear of Fire still applies to her.

specials.name: Hard to Kill
specials.description: A Spiteborn is taken out of action only on a 6 on the Injury chart: 1-2 knocked down, 3-5 stunned, 6 out of action. Not against fire attacks.

specials.name: Root Walk
specials.description: Dryads may run only in swamp, dirt or forest terrain; on city terrain they may only walk or charge.

specials.name: Tanglevine
specials.description: A warrior in combat with more than one Dryad loses 1 Attack for each Dryad after the first, to a minimum of 1.

specials.name: Hard to Kill
specials.description: A Spiteborn is taken out of action only on a 6 on the Injury chart: 1-2 knocked down, 3-5 stunned, 6 out of action. Not against fire attacks.

specials.name: Unarmed
specials.description: Treekin can't use weapons, and fight unarmed with no penalty.

specials.name: Redwood
specials.description: A Treekin's Bark Skin save is 4+.

specials.name: Slow Growing
specials.description: Treekin gain experience at half the normal rate.

upgrades.note: Vine (Tentacle), Branch (Extra Arm), Thick Leaves (Cloud of Flies), Dense Trunk (Hulking Brute), Thorns (Spines), Spores (Blackblood), Nesting Bird (Beak). One when hired, a new one on an advance's double.
