rules.title: Natives
rules.description: Used to poking through the underbrush, Forest Goblins suffer no movement penalties from moving through any wooded terrain.

rules.title: Animosity
rules.description:
Orcs and Goblins enjoy nothing more than a good scrap, unfortunately they’re not always very discerning about who they scrap with! To represent this, at the start of the Orc player’s turn, roll a D6 for each Henchman who is either an Orc or a Goblin. A roll of 1 means that the warrior has taken offense to something one of his mates has done or said. Do not roll for models that are engaged in hand-to-hand combat (they’re already scrappin’!). To find out just how offended the model is, roll another D6 and consult the following chart to see what happens:

Animosity Result

| D6 | Result | | :------------------------: | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | 1 | "I ’Erd Dat!"
The warrior decides that the nearest friendly Orc or Goblin Henchman has insulted his lineage or personal hygiene and must pay the price!
If there is a friendly Orc or Goblin Henchman or Hired Sword within charge reach (if there are multiple targets within reach, choose the one nearest to the mad model), the offended warrior will immediately charge and fight a round of hand-to-hand combat against the source of his ire. At the end of this round of combat, the models will immediately move 1" apart and no longer count as being in close combat (unless one of them fails another Animosity test and rolls this result again).
If there are no friendly Orc or Goblin Henchmen or Hired Swords within charge reach, and the warrior is armed with a missile weapon, he immediately takes a shot at the nearest friendly Orc or Goblin Henchman or Hired Sword. If none of the above applies, or if the nearest friendly model is an Orc Hero, the warrior behaves as if a 2-5 had been rolled on this chart. In any case, the warrior in question may take no other action this turn, though he may defend himself if attacked in hand-to-hand combat. | | 2-5 | "Wud Yoo Say?"
The warrior is fairly certain he heard an offensive sound from the nearest friendly Orc or Goblin, but he’s not quite sure. He spends the turn hurling insults at his mate.
He may do nothing else this turn, though he may defend himself if attacked in hand-to-hand combat. | | 6 | "I’ll Show Yer!"
The warrior imagines that his mates are laughing about him behind his back and calling him silly names. To show them up he decides that he’ll be the first one to the scrap!
This model must move as quickly as possible towards the nearest enemy model, charging into combat if possible. If there are no enemy models within sight, the Orc or Goblin warrior may make a normal move immediately. This move is in addition to his regular move in the Movement phase, so he may therefore move twice in a single turn if you wish.
If the extra move takes the Orc or Goblin warrior within charge reach of an enemy model, the warrior must charge into close combat during his regular movement. |

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Chieftain may use his Leadership characteristic when taking Leadership tests.

specials.name: Animosity
specials.description: Braves are subject to the rules for Animosity.

specials.name: Animosity
specials.description: Braves are subject to the rules for Animosity.

specials.name: Animosity (Red Toof Goblin)
specials.description: Red Toof Boyz are subject to the rules for Animosity.

specials.name: Berserkers (Red Toof Goblin)
specials.description: Forest Goblins of the Red Toof tribe allow themselves to be bitten by all sorts of poisonous wildlife before entering battle. The mingling venom drives them into frothing convulsions, making them extremely ferocious. Red Toof Boyz are affected by the rules for Frenzy as described in the Mordheim rulebook. In addition, if they begin their turn within charge range of an enemy, they are immune to animosity for that turn.

specials.name: Animosity
specials.description: Braves are subject to the rules for Animosity.

specials.name: Sluggas
specials.description: In the shooting phase, the Sluggas may throw thrown weapons up to three times. This may not be combined with Quick Shot if they should be promoted to hero status.

fighters.name: Gigantic Spider
fighters.fixed_kit: A Gigantic Spider never needs or uses weapons or armour.

specials.name: Poisonous
specials.description: The Gigantic Spider’s maw drips with vile poisons. When it wounds an enemy and a roll is made on the injury table, 1: knocked down, 2-4: stunned, and 5-6: Out of Action.

specials.name: Native
specials.description: Negotiating woodlands is no trouble for spiders. They move through any wooded terrain without penalty.

specials.name: Non-sentient
specials.description: Spiders are affected by the stupidity rules in the Mordheim rulebook. In addition, they never gain experience, as they are animals. Note however that they may climb as normal.

specials.name: May Ride
specials.description: The Forest Goblin Chieftain, may ride the Gigantic Spider. He gains +1 armour save, and shall move at the Gigantic Spider’s rate of 6. Shooting attacks hit the Chieftain on a die roll of 1-2, and the Gigantic Spider on a 3-6. In close combat, the opponent may choose which to hit. The Gigantic Spider no longer has to check for stupidity if it is being ridden, as the Chieftain is directing its actions.

rules.title: Camouflage
rules.description: A hidden Forest Goblin is not spotted automatically within an enemy's Initiative distance in inches: the enemy must first roll equal to or under his Initiative to spot him.

rules.title: Natives
rules.description: Forest Goblins suffer no movement penalty for moving through jungle terrain.

rules.title: Animosity
rules.description:
At the start of the Forest Goblin player's turn, roll a D6 for each hero or henchman subject to animosity. Do not roll for a model engaged in hand-to-hand combat. On a 1 he has taken offence: roll another D6 and apply the result.

D6 | Result
1 | I 'Erd Dat! If a friendly Goblin henchman or Hired Sword is within charge reach, the warrior charges the nearest one and fights one round of close combat. At the end of that round both models move 1" apart and no longer count as being in close combat, unless one of them fails another animosity test and rolls this result again. If no friendly Goblin henchman or Hired Sword is within charge reach and the warrior has a missile weapon, he shoots at the nearest one instead. If neither applies, or the nearest friendly model is a Goblin hero, treat the result as a 2-5. In any case he may take no other action this turn, though he may defend himself in hand-to-hand combat.
2-5 | Wud Yoo Say? The warrior spends the turn hurling insults at the nearest friendly Goblin. He may do nothing else this turn, though he may defend himself in hand-to-hand combat.
6 | I'll Show Yer! The warrior must move as quickly as possible towards the nearest enemy model, charging into combat if possible. If no enemy model is in sight he may make a normal move at once. This move is in addition to his move in the movement phase, so he may move twice in one turn. If the extra move takes him within charge reach of an enemy model, he must charge into close combat during his regular movement.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any model in the warband within 6" of the Chieftain may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Animosity
specials.description: A Boss is subject to animosity.

specials.name: Animosity
specials.description: A Boss is subject to animosity.

specials.name: Animosity
specials.description: A Boss is subject to animosity.

specials.description: A Boss is subject to animosity.

specials.name: Sluggas
specials.description: In the shooting phase a Slugga may throw thrown weapons up to three times. This may not be combined with Quick Shot if he is promoted to a hero.

fighters.name: Gigantic Spider
fighters.fixed_kit: None.

specials.name: Poisonous
specials.description: When a Gigantic Spider wounds an enemy, a roll on the injury table of 1 is knocked down, 2-4 is stunned and 5-6 is out of action.

specials.name: Native
specials.description: A Gigantic Spider moves through jungle terrain without penalty.

specials.name: May Ride
specials.description: If the optional rules for mounts are used, the Chieftain may ride the Gigantic Spider. He gains +1 armour save and moves at the spider's rate of 6. Shooting attacks hit the Chieftain on a D6 roll of 1-2 and the spider on a 3-6; in close combat the opponent chooses which to hit. While it is ridden the spider does not test for stupidity, as the Chieftain directs it.

specials.name: Nonsentient
specials.description: A Gigantic Spider is subject to stupidity and never gains experience. It may climb as normal.

rules.title: Swabbies
rules.description: The warband may capture models with the Swabbies rules. One who agrees joins the Crew; one who refuses becomes one of the Bloated. The warband may never have more Bloated than Crew.

rules.title: Ethereal
rules.description: The Ghost Captain and the Screaming Ghosts are Ethereal. An Ethereal model has a 4+ unmodifiable save against every attack. It may not be used with Dodge or Step Aside, and it does nothing against a magical attack: a spell, a prayer, an artefact, gromril, ithilmar or a silver bullet. In the movement phase he may take a Leadership test; if he passes it he may move through any terrain piece and over water. If he begins his next movement phase in the middle of a terrain piece or over water he must take another Leadership test, and is taken out of action at once if he fails it. Once the warband is made, every item costs an Ethereal model double. When the crew finds an item, roll a D6: on a 5+ both Ethereal and non-Ethereal models may use it, and on a 1-4 only non-Ethereal models may, which is marked on the roster.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Ghost Captain may use his Leadership for any Leadership test.

specials.name: Beauty of the Sea
specials.description: A male enemy who is not an animal must pass a Leadership test to charge a Sea Singer; if he fails it he stays where he is. A model she charges may not attack back until he passes a Leadership test at the start of the combat phase, and once he passes one he need not test again for the rest of that combat. She causes fear in female models. Her Beauty counts as a form of psychology.

specials.name: Not Undead
specials.description: The Cursed are living men and do not count as Undead.

specials.name: No Brain
specials.description: A Gibbet never gains experience.

specials.name: Iron Cage
specials.description: The iron cage around the Gibbet gives him a 5+ armour save, as heavy armour would. It may not be lost, stolen or given to another model.

specials.name: Sink
specials.description: A Gibbet sinks to the bottom of any water he moves through. The bed counts as difficult terrain, so he moves at half speed, and while sunk he is at -2 to hit and -2 to be hit in combat and by missiles. He boards a ship by the normal rules. He is immune to any water or drowning damage.

fighters.name: Bloated
fighters.fixed_kit: A Bloated needs no weapon and may make one unarmed attack at no penalty. He may instead be armed from the Bloated Equipment list, and then needs two weapons to gain an extra attack.

specials.name: No Brain
specials.description: A Gibbet never gains experience.

specials.name: Squishy
specials.description: A Bloated does not treat a stunned result as knocked down.

specials.name: Dead Man's Float
specials.description: A Bloated floats, so while in water he may move up to 4" at no penalty. He may do this as a charge, but 4" is still his most.

specials.name: Weak Magic
specials.description: If the warband routs, every Bloated who had already left the table in an earlier turn falls apart: remove him from the roster as if he had been killed.

specials.name: Plenty more with the next tide
specials.description: A Bloated taken out of action does not count towards the warband's rout test.

rules.title: Blood for blood
rules.description: A Ghutani hero who rolls 51-56 on the Serious Injuries chart counts as having rolled Bitter Enmity.

rules.title: Flagellants
rules.description: The warband may hire up to 5 Flagellants as henchmen. They pick their equipment from the Townsmen equipment list.

rules.title: A slave may lead
rules.description: A slave, or the son of a slave, may become the warband's leader.

lists.name: Townsmen Equipment List
lists.note: This list is for Townsmen only.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Emir may use his Leadership for a Leadership test.

specials.name: Field of Scholarship
specials.description:
When the Scholar joins the warband, choose the field he has studied. A Ghutani Scholar may only take Poetry or Theology.

Cartography: add or subtract 1 from the D6 when exploring.

Physiology: after all serious injuries have been worked out, one hero may re-roll his result.

Poetry: the warband's leader adds +1 to his Leadership for his first Leadership test of a scenario if the warband won its last battle. For one turn of a scenario, every friendly model within 6" has +1 Weapon Skill and +1 Attack.

Theology: the Scholar serves The One and learns Holy skills.

The Occult: the Scholar is a wizard and casts Lesser Magic.

rules.title: Animosity
rules.description: Every henchman of the warband is subject to animosity, as the Orc & Goblin warband's rules describe it.

rules.title: Fear Elves
rules.description: The warband's Goblins fear Elves. No other member of the warband is affected.

rules.title: Distasteful Company
rules.description: The warband may hire only Pit Fighters, Ogre Bodyguards and Warlocks, any Goblin hired sword, and any hired sword whose own entry says he will work for Goblins.

rules.title: Bonecrunchas
rules.description: The warband may never hold more Bonecruncha Wolves than it holds Goblins.

rules.title: Riding Skills
rules.description: Every Hero of the warband may learn riding skills. The number of mounts a campaign allows does not change.

rules.title: Speshul Nitches
rules.description: Each Big Boss and Boss may buy one Speshul Nitch when he is hired, and no more. A Shaman may buy the Beastmasta Nitch and no other.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior in the warband within 6" of the Big Boss may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Animosity
specials.description: A Goblin Warrior is subject to animosity.

specials.name: Animosity
specials.description: A Goblin Warrior is subject to animosity.

specials.name: Reckless
specials.description: A Wolfhead who starts a turn out of combat and within 12" of an enemy he can see ignores all psychology until the end of that turn, fear and animosity included, and moves as fast as he can towards that enemy, leaping to close the distance if his move is not enough. Reaching base contact counts as a charge. With more than one enemy within 12" you pick the target. He is not reckless in a turn in which he has just stood up from being knocked down.

fighters.name: Bonecruncha Wolf
fighters.fixed_kit: None. A Bonecruncha Wolf fights with fangs and claws and never uses weapons or armour.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Bonecruncha Wolves are animals and gain no experience.

specials.name: Charge
specials.description: A Bonecruncha Wolf fights with 2 Attacks instead of 1 in the turn it charges, for that round of combat only.

fighters.name: Stone Troll
fighters.fixed_kit: None. A Troll may carry a big club, but may never be given weapons or armour.

specials.name: Dumb Monsters
specials.description: A Troll gains no experience and never learns a skill.

specials.name: Always Hungry
specials.description: The warband must pay 15 gc after each battle to feed the Troll. If it cannot, the Big Boss may sacrifice three Snotlings instead. If neither is paid the Troll wanders off in search of food.

specials.name: Dispel
specials.description: When a spell targets the Stone Troll, or a template over it falls on it, roll a D6: on a 4 or more the spell or prayer is negated and affects nobody.

special.name: Lil' Warboss
special.description: Big Boss only. Every Goblin within 6" of him is free of animosity, which a Boss Pole does not add to. He may learn one special skill of the Orc Da Mob warband's list, and may buy heavy armour.

special.name: World-Class Theef
special.description: He may buy and use the special items of any greenskin warband that a Goblin can use, as the players agree. Where such an item is on his own equipment list he may buy it when the warband is raised. Nobody without this Nitch may use those items.

special.name: Wolfskin
special.description: He gains the Reckless rule, as a Wolfhead has it, and the Leap skill. He may buy a Wolfcloak, and may learn the special skill Strong 'Un.

special.name: Beastmasta
special.description: Any friendly animal within 6" of him may use his Leadership, and the warband adds +1 to its rarity rolls when looking for a Giant Wolf mount. He may learn the special skill Beast tamer, and may buy a Leather Whip.

special.name: Wolf Rida
special.description: He starts with the skill Ride Giant Wolf. He may learn the special skill Wolf Breaker, and may buy barding.

special.name: Nasty Skulker
special.description: While he is armed with daggers and nothing else, Poisoned Daggers and Sharp Daggas included, he has the Lightning Reflexes skill. He may learn Infiltration and may buy Throwing Knives. No more than three members of the warband may take this Nitch.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The warband may not hire a Bounty Hunter or a Roadwarden, nor any law-enforcer, holy man or follower of Morr.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Graver may take Leadership tests on his Leadership.

specials.name: Sawbones
specials.description: You may re-roll the Serious Injury roll of one Hero; the second roll stands. Not if the Junior Medic was taken out of action in the battle.

rules.title: Hard to Kill
rules.description: A Dwarf is taken out of action only on a 6 on the Injury chart: 1-2 is knocked down, 3-5 stunned and 6 out of action.

rules.title: Hard Head
rules.description: Dwarfs ignore the special rules of clubs, maces and the like.

rules.title: Armour
rules.description: Dwarfs never suffer movement penalties for wearing armour.

rules.title: Field Test
rules.description: The Engineer and the Apprentice Engineers may use any weapon or armour made from the Inventions, and so must a henchman promoted by The Lad's Got Talent. The Sapper wears only the armour ones.

rules.title: Death of a Leader
rules.description: If the Expelled Engineer dies, an Apprentice Engineer takes the Book of Bad Ideas and the title of Engineer: he takes the Inventor rule, and the warband may hire a new Apprentice.

rules.title: Inventions
rules.description:
The Engineer makes inventions from the blueprints in the Book of Bad Ideas (Inventor). Each needs its components, and a difficulty test passed: a roll of 2 on that test is a critical failure, and every component is lost.

Every invention is experimental: a to-hit roll of 1 with it means a roll on the Experimental Weapons chart. One that doesn't roll to hit rolls a D6 each time it is used, and on a 1 it still works but rolls on the chart.

Invention | Difficulty | Components | What it does
Master Key | 8 | Blunderbuss, Handgun | Once a game the handgun fires a small blast template. It opens doors by itself, and the template reaches on through the hole where the door was. Not against large gates.
Golden Gun | 10 | Double-barrelled Hunting Rifle, Flash Powder | Counts as a double-barrelled long rifle, with Payday: the Dwarf loads gold down the barrel, each 5 gc a +1 Strength slug (25 gc is S5), at most 30 gc at a time.
Boom Hammer | 10 | Double-handed hammer, Superior Black Powder | Strength as user +2, Strike Last. Full Steam: once per combat the Dwarf may attack at a further +2 Strength (+4 in all), and the next time he is attacked the enemy has +1 to hit.
Para-Pillow | 10 | 5 Cathayan silks, 2 Rope and Hooks | The Dwarf may leap off a tall building and glide down, as the Wings mutation describes.
Launching Vertical Assistance Rope | 7 | Pistol, Rope and Hook | He passes every climbing and diving test on a 3+.
Siege Breaker | 11 | Treasure Cart, Powder Keg, 10 Belaying Pins, Superior Black Powder, Gromril hammer | A cart that 2 crew move at half speed and 4 at full. Set against a wall or barred door, roll a D6: 1, She's Gonna Blow!: it explodes, a S4 hit on every model within 4"; 2-4, Here's Johnny!: a hole big enough to shoot through (a second such result counts as 5-6); 5-6, Party Time!: the door is destroyed, or a wall holed 1" wide, enough for models that aren't Large to pass.
Stand and Deliver | 7 | Handgun, Spear | Counts as a handgun and a spear, with Point Blank: in the first round of combat he strikes first, with a rifle shot and a spear attack.
Repeaterbuss | 10 | 4 Blunderbusses, Repeater Handgun | Fires 4 blunderbuss shots at once, each rolling for misfire.
Escape Pod | 8 | Any armour, Toughened Leathers, a sacrificial goat (for the grease) | Counts as the armour it is made from, with Greasy Escape: after a failed armour save the Dwarf may launch himself D6" out of his armour, leaving combat with no hits against him. The armour is found after the game, and the pod must be greased again (a goat).
Hug Thrower | 6 | Crossbow, Net | Range 30", Move or Fire: it launches a net at a crossbow's full range, and the enemy has -1 to his Strength tests to escape it. On a to-hit roll of 1 the net wraps around the Dwarf.
Full Metal Jacket | 12 | Handheld Mortar, Heavy Armour, Net | Range 24": a stronger hug launcher firing an armoured straitjacket, the victim at -2 Strength to escape the net. A model hit in water sinks and is out of action, aquatic or not. A Large model hit is blinded, and moves 2D6" in a random direction each turn until it frees itself.
Auto-Stand | 10 | Heavy Armour, Superior Black Powder | While he wears the armour the Dwarf has the Jump Up skill.
Back Off Armour | 12 | Heavy Armour, Powder Keg | Counts as heavy armour, with Get Off!: once a game every model in base contact takes a S3 hit and is knocked back D6". A new powder keg must be bought after each use.
Death Roller | 12 | Cart, 6 Axes, 6 Swords, Steam Engine, Armoured Plating | A cart with a steam engine's and armoured plating's rules, which causes D6 impact hits on any model in its way, at a Strength equal to the distance it moved that turn.
Goblin Hewer | 12 | 12 Axes, 6 Rope and Hooks, Bolt Thrower | Troll Slayer engineer only. An artillery weapon: range 6-26", Strength 4; Hard to Fire, Cumbersome Movement, Reload!, Aim!, Broadside Shooting and Carve 'em Up, below.

The Goblin Hewer's rules. Hard to Fire: a crew of two fires it (one if he is Large), only one of whom needs the Artillery Expert skill; the usual shooting rules apply, but no Shooting skills. Cumbersome Movement: one crewman moves it at half his Movement, two at their full Movement, never running. Reload!: it fires only after a full turn of the crew preparing it (mark it loaded), and may still need to aim. Aim!: it may not move and fire in a turn, and pivoting counts as moving, so it shoots only at a target in a straight line from its nozzle (1" leeway). Broadside Shooting: a shot at a building, or a boat of a barge's size or larger, within 10" hits automatically. Carve 'em Up: each time it fires, nominate a target and roll 2D6 for its shots, spread them evenly between the target and another model within 6" of it (friend or foe), then roll to hit and to wound for each.

rules.title: Experimental Weapons Chart
rules.description:
An invention that goes wrong rolls a D6:

D6 | Result
1 | Scrap: it is beyond repair and leaves the roster; add a club to the roster or 3 gc for the scrap.
2-4 | Badly Mangled: either add its bits to the parts pile, counting as one item used to build it, or try to repair it: on a D6 roll of 3+ it works again; on anything else it is useless and leaves the roster.
5-6 | Few Bits Missing: the Engineer has the parts to fix it, and it works as normal.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Expelled Engineer may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Inventor
specials.description: In the trading phase, instead of searching for rare items or visiting a location, the Engineer may try to make a new invention from the Book of Bad Ideas. He needs the book and the invention's components, and must pass its difficulty test.

specials.name: Make Explosives
specials.description: After a battle, instead of searching for rare items, the Sapper may make explosives: pick what and pay before he takes a Leadership test. If he passes, he makes up to two Blast Charges at 9 gc each, up to two doses of Flash Powder at 11 gc each, a Fire Bomb at 21 gc or a Cinderblast Bomb at 27 gc.

specials.name: Tunnel Rat
specials.description: The Sapper re-rolls characteristic tests underground.

specials.name: Assistant
specials.description: Each Apprentice who works on an invention after the battle adds +1 to the Expelled Engineer's roll to make it. Or an Apprentice may search for rare items in the Engineer's place, with any bonus to rarity rolls the Engineer has.

specials.name: Properly Used
specials.description: With the optional misfire rules, when a Thunderer rolls a 1 he rolls again: on a 3+ the misfire is ignored, so the shot still misses but the weapon doesn't explode.

fighters.name: Gyrocopter
fighters.fixed_kit: None. The Gyrocopter is a machine.

specials.name: Fly
specials.description: The Gyrocopter flies, as the flying rules describe.

specials.name: Transport
specials.description: The Gyrocopter starts with 1 seat for a passenger; the Tinkerer skill's customisation may add more.

specials.name: Full Steam Ahead!
specials.description: The Gyrocopter may burst forward in a straight line: roll a D6. On a 6 roll on the Engine Malfunction chart; otherwise add the roll to its move. A warrior with the Driver skill may re-roll an Engine Malfunction result, and the new result stands. A Gyrocopter with a steam engine hit with a Draft Creature result is hit in the engine, which has Toughness 6; if it is wounded, roll on the Engine Malfunction chart.

specials.name: Engine Malfunction
specials.description:
D6 | Result
1 | Kaboom!: the engine explodes. The hull takes D6 wounds, every model within 4" of the bow takes a S5 flaming hit, and the Gyrocopter, now on fire, swerves 45 degrees in a random direction and crash-lands straight down: D3 more S5 hits to the hull, and D3 S5 hits to anyone beneath.
2 | Dangerous Overpressure!: it takes 1 wound, plunges 6" forward and lands, taking damage if it hits anything.
3-4 | Emergency Vent: models within 4" of the bow take D3 S2 flaming hits, and it lands at once in the nearest free space below. It can't move next turn.
5 | Minor Leak: it lands at once in the nearest free space below, and can't move next turn.
6 | Valve Locked: it moves only 2D3" this turn, and can't turn.

specials.name: Customisation
specials.description:
A Hero with the Tinkerer skill may roll 2D6 on this chart after a battle to improve the Gyrocopter:

2D6 | Result
2 | That Didn't Go Well!: roll again (re-rolling That Didn't Go Well! and Breakthrough!), and lower that characteristic, or lose that upgrade, instead.
3 | Bomber: in its movement phase it may drop a bomb: roll an artillery dice and move a small blast template that far back along its path; every model under it takes a S4 hit. On a misfire the Gyrocopter and its steam engine take the hit instead. Each bomb is bought for 25 gc.
4 | Every Gear and Gizmo: +2 Movement.
5 | Room for Activities: +1 passenger.
6 | Stabilisers: when an Engine Malfunction or Wheel Damage result halts it or makes it land, it may first glide up to 2D6" in any direction.
7 | More Reliable: one re-roll on the Engine Malfunction table. Re-roll this result if it comes again.
8 | Steam Cloud: -1 to hit it with missile weapons. Once only: re-roll it after.
9 | Weapons Mount: it may buy any swivel-mounted artillery weapon, worked by the pilot while it is stationary or by a passenger, without taking a seat.
10 | Reinforced Hull: +4 Armour Save.
11 | Steel Propellers: +1 Wound.
12 | Breakthrough!: roll D3 more times on this chart, ignoring further Breakthrough! results.

rules.title: Impeccable Care
rules.description: Amongst one of the first things that the students are taught is to take proper care of their equipment and the right way to perform that maintenance. Once they have mastered this function, they learn to repair the same weapons should they become damaged and because of this they can buy such black powder weapons on the cheap and quickly return them to good working order. As a result they can buy these weapons at a fairly reduced price! They can ALWAYS use the reduced cost for black powder weapons listed in their starting Equipment List, and they gain an additional +2 on rare rolls to find any black powder weapons since people don’t mind selling broken guns!

rules.title: Properly Used
rules.description: The students know the proper way to use their weapons, spending many hours on the school’s shooting range. This is considered to be a good use of time between lessons and recommended by all the school’s instructors, after all if the students constantly blow themselves up with their weapons, there wouldn’t be many graduates. When using the optional Misfire rules, if a one is rolled, roll a second dice. On a 3+ the misfire is ignored (the shot still misses, but the weapon does NOT explode).

rules.title: Proud To A Fault!
rules.description: Anyone studying at the Gunnery School is very proud of this fact, as it is a great honour to be accepted. After they start using black powder weapons, students recognise the superiority of these weapons and refuse to bend their knee to the ‘lesser’ ranged weapons. The members of this warband NEVER use any non-black powder ranged weapons (this prohibition does NOT apply to hired swords or dramatis personae, as they are hired help and have not received proper Nuln training).

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any models in the warband within 12" of the Senior Gunnery Officer may use his Leadership value when using Leadership tests.

specials.name: Expert Weaponsmith
specials.description: The Instructors know every trick in the book when it comes to working with black powder weapons. While there is an Instructor in the warband all Pistol weapons receive a +3” range bonus and all other black powder weapons receive a +6” range bonus.

specials.name: Crack Shot
specials.description: Experts with pistols in close quarters; they have an uncanny ability to turn what should have missed its target into a success. When using pistols in close combat, they may re-roll any missed to-hit rolls with the pistol in the first round of combat.

rules.title: Pretty Much Human
rules.description: The warband may hire any hired sword that human mercenaries may hire.

rules.title: Too Big
rules.description: Halflings can never use a Long Bow, Elf Bow, Handgun, Long Rifle or Blunderbuss, even when an advance would let them.

rules.title: Halfling Items
rules.description: Halflings get no bonus from Halfling items, such as the Halfling Cookbook.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Halfling Elder may take Leadership tests on his Leadership.

specials.name: Master Chef
specials.description: Roll a D6: on a 5+ the warband counts as one size smaller when it sells treasure or wyrdstone.

specials.name: Infiltrator
specials.description: The Halfling Thief is set up after the enemy warband(s), anywhere on the table out of their sight and at least 12" from every enemy model. When more than one model can infiltrate, roll off to decide who places first.

specials.name: Pick Locks
specials.description: To open a locked door the Halfling Thief needs only to pass an Initiative test.

specials.name: Cutpurse
specials.description: If the Halfling Thief fought in the battle and was not taken out of action, the warband finds +1 treasure on top of its usual find.

fighters.name: Piggy
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Piggies use no weapons and fight without penalty for it.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Piggies are animals and never gain experience.

specials.name: Skills
specials.description: If the Village Ogre becomes a Hero, he picks his skills from the Combat and Strength lists only.

specials.name: Slow Witted
specials.description: The Village Ogre gains experience at half the usual rate.

specials.name: Protective
specials.description: While the warband has a Village Ogre no Ogre Bodyguard joins it, and one hired before the Village Ogre arrived leaves.

rules.title: Excellent Sight
rules.description: A High Elf spots hidden enemies from twice as far away as other warriors, that is, twice his Initiative value in inches.

rules.title: Haughty
rules.description: The warband may never include a hired sword who is not a High Elf, and may never use equipment of Dwarf origin, gromril weapons and armour included.

rules.title: Honourable
rules.description: A High Elf may never use poison or drugs of any kind.

rules.title: The Old Ways
rules.description: A High Elf may never use black powder weapons of any sort.

rules.title: Resolve
rules.description: When taking a Rout test against Dark Elves the warband counts its Leadership as 10. It may never choose to rout voluntarily against them.

fighters.name: Loremaster
fighters.fixed_kit: A sword, a dagger or a Mage Staff of Hoeth only.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any model in the warband within 6" of the Loremaster may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Seeker
specials.description: If the Ranger was not taken out of action, you may modify one Exploration dice by -1 or +1.

fighters.name: Sword Warden
fighters.fixed_kit: Anything from the High Elf equipment list; never a missile weapon.

specials.name: Sword Master Protege
specials.description: Anyone shooting at a Sword Warden armed with a sword or an Elven Greatsword, but not a double-handed sword, deducts -1 from the roll to hit. This does not apply to black powder weapons.

rules.title: Distasteful Company
rules.description: The warband may hire only Pit Fighters, Ogre Bodyguards, Hobgoblin Scouts and Warlocks, and any greenskin hired sword your group approves.

rules.title: Animosity
rules.description: Every Henchman in the warband suffers from Animosity, using Da Mob's rules for it.

rules.title: Strength in Numbers
rules.description: Each round the warband's leader gains +1 Leadership, to a maximum of 10, as long as no more than 75% of the warband has been taken out of action. At the start of any of your turns in which 25% of the warband is out of action, so that rout tests are called for, the leader loses the +1.

rules.title: Great Gits
rules.description: The warband may include up to three Great Gits in all, in any mix of Gasher Gits and Arrer Gits.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any member of the warband within 6" of the Chieftain may use his Leadership for a Psychology test.

specials.name: No Armour
specials.description: The Maghu may not wear armour.

specials.name: Poisons
specials.description: At the start of any battle the Maghu can fight in, he laces one Hero's weapon with black lotus. Write down which hero and which weapon before the battle; the choice may not be changed, and you may reveal the poisoned weapon at any time.

specials.name: Animal Link
specials.description: Whenever an animal within 6" of the Maghu takes a Leadership test, you may re-roll it once and must accept the second result. This covers a friendly animal's test, a test to control a mount and an enemy's fear test alike.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: A Bonecruncha Wolf gains no experience, and uses neither weapons nor armour.

specials.name: Charge
specials.description: A Bonecruncha Wolf fights with 2 Attacks instead of 1 in the turn it charges.

specials.name: Sneaky
specials.description: When the Git charges an opponent already engaged in combat he gains +1 Attack for the first round, and all his hand-to-hand attacks carry a -1 armour save modifier in that round. This applies only to attacks made with daggers of some kind: ordinary daggers, ithilmar daggers, Double-Dirks and the like.

rules.title: Treacherous Gits
rules.description:
At the start of each turn roll a D6 for every Henchman not already in hand-to-hand combat. On a 1, roll a D6 again:

D6 | Result
1 | He switches sides and the opposing player controls him for the rest of the battle. With more than one opponent he joins the warband with the highest rating. He still takes treachery tests, so he may end up back on his own side.
2-5 | He will not shoot or charge this turn, but may do anything else.
6 | He takes no further treachery tests for the rest of the game.

rules.title: Giant Wolves
rules.description: A Giant Wolf must be ridden into battle. Nominate a Hero or a Henchman to ride each one, and the rules for mounted models apply, except that a rider never dismounts during a battle. If the model is taken out of action roll on the Serious Injury table for both the rider and the wolf. Riders may be switched between battles. A mounted model may not enter a building in an above-ground scenario; in a tomb-raiding scenario it may be ridden, but may not run inside a tomb and charges only its normal move, which must still be declared as a charge.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any member of the warband within 6" of the Khan may use his Leadership for a Psychology test.

specials.name: Steady aim
specials.description: A Stickaz may re-roll one failed to-hit roll with a missile weapon each turn.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: A Giant Wolf gains no experience and may be given no weapons or equipment.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: Bandits have no compunction about hiring mercenaries, and may hire any Hired Swords allowed to a Human Mercenary warband.

rules.title: Powder's Expensive!
rules.description: Bandits are often too poor to purchase or upkeep expensive equipment like gunpowder weapons. The exception to this is Bandit heroes, who often see such extravagances as pistols as symbols of their status and higher wealth. The higher costs for black powder weapons in the equipment chart, and the fact that henchmen can't purchase them at all, reflect the extreme rarity of these types of weapons for Bandit warbands.

rules.title: Foragers
rules.description: Bandits are used to lean times, and know how to make their gold stretch. Because of this, they usually have fewer expenses between adventures. When determining Income for a Bandit warband, always use the next lower warband size category (a warband with 1-3 members still uses the first column however!). For example, a warband with 15 members finds 4 Treasures in the Exploration Phase. When they sell these Treasures, they use the 10-12 members column instead of the 13-15 members column, resulting in a gain of 5 gold pieces for the warband.

rules.title: Know Who To Sell To
rules.description: Bandits are used to getting rid of stolen goods, and have built up contacts for doing so. When a Bandit warband sells equipment, they get half of any random element of the equipment cost, in addition to the normal half of the item's basic cost.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Bandit Prince may use his Leadership characteristic when taking any Leadership tests.

specials.name: Concealment
specials.description: Enemy warriors often find it difficult to detect a Footpad until he strikes. If an enemy warrior wishes to charge a Footpad that he cannot see (but was not declared as Hidden), he must subtract 1 from his Initiative before making his Initiative test. Note that a roll of ‘6’ always fails when rolling to charge a Footpad that the warrior cannot see. Also, models halve their Initiative when checking the range to see if they can detect a Footpad who has been declared as Hiding.

specials.name: Swordmaster
specials.description: In order to remain alive, a Duelist picks up swordfighting techniques that few others master. The Duelist successfully parries an enemy blow on a roll equal to or over the roll to hit, not just over the roll as with normal parries. Obviously a Duelist must first be armed with a weapon or armour that allows him to Parry in order to use this rule.

specials.name: Weapon Knowledge
specials.description: A Duelist must be prepared to fight an opponent with any weapon at any time, so a working knowledge of even exotic weapons is critical for his survival. The weapons in the Bandit equipment chart merely represent the weapons a Duelist may start with. A Duelist may use any close combat or missile weapon that the warband members can get hold of.

specials.name: Convincing Manner
specials.description: Hucksters specialize in convincing strangers of their benevolent intentions. When an enemy warrior attempts to charge a member of the huckster’s warband within 12” of the huckster, the enemy must first pass a successful Leadership test. If the warrior fails the test he may not charge and remains stationary for the turn (treat as a failed charge), exactly as if he had failed a test to charge a Fear-causing enemy. Note that individuals subject to stupidity and animals are immune to this effect (they are too stupid to understand what the huckster is saying).

specials.name: Slick Operator
specials.description: In between games the player may choose to have the huckster run a con on the local inhabitants of the region. Roll a D6: On a result of 2-6, the con is successful and the warband gains 2D6 gold (the huckster keeps the rest). However, on a result of 1 the huckster’s con has backfired and he is on the run (he misses the next game and no gold is received by the warband).

specials.name: Looting the Dead
specials.description: Normally when a warrior is killed or his wounds cause him to leave the warband and he is taken off the warband’s roster, all of his equipment is lost. However, some unscrupulous individuals will stoop to robbing a dead or incapacitated warrior, thereby gaining his equipment for themselves. When rolling for warriors who were taken Out of Action at the end of a battle, the Bandit player may roll a D6 for any warriors who are to be removed from their warband’s roster. On a roll of 4+ the looter has taken all of the warrior’s equipment — it is the Bandit player’s to keep. Failure indicates that the Looter either didn’t notice the warrior going down, or he didn’t get the opportunity to rob the body. Obviously any warrior can only be looted once, but multiple Looters allow the Bandit player multiple chances that his warband members got the equipment off of each downed warrior. Note also that warriors to be looted can be from any warband participating in the game, including the Bandit warband — Bandits are certainly not above looting their own dead!

specials.name: Hardened
specials.description: Blackhearts are not as put off by the evils of the world when they come across them… in fact persons of this nature are often more uncomfortable around situations where warmth and love are in abundance! Blackhearts are immune to Fear, and never have to take All-Alone tests (they prefer to work alone anyway…).

specials.name: Trailblazers
specials.description: Poachers are experts at finding new game or safe campsites for the warband. In the game this is represented by allowing the warband to reroll one D6 for each Poacher in the Exploration phase. Poachers are not as good as Elf Rangers for scouting, but they are often darned close!

specials.name: Utterly Inept
specials.description: Gutterscum have turned to a life of crime because they lack the ability to fit into normal society. They lack both the ambition and the capacity for self-improvement. Gutterscum do not gain experience.

rules.title: Woodcraft
rules.description: Followers of Taal make their homes in the wilderness and shall only frequent towns or cities when it is compulsory for them to do so. They are expert woodsmen and their knowledge of the wilds is unrivalled by all except perhaps the Wood Elves. Horned Hunter warbands move through any difficult terrain they encounter without suffering any movement penalties.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Horned Hunter may use his Leadership value when taking Leadership tests.

specials.name: Prayers
specials.description: A Priest of Taal may use the Prayers of Taal.

specials.name: Strictures
specials.description: Priests of Taal may never wear heavy armour.

specials.name: Infiltrator
specials.description:
A warrior with this skill is always placed on the battlefield after the opposing warband and can be placed anywhere on the table as long as it is out of sight of the opposing warband and more than 12" away from any enemy model.

If both players have models which infiltrate, roll a D6 for each, and the lowest roll sets up first.

specials.name: Strictures (Initiate)
specials.description: Taal’s Initiates may never wear armour.

specials.name: Drunk
specials.description: The militia are blasted out of their tiny minds on Rotfire moonshine and cheap ale. As such, they automatically pass all Leadership-based tests they are required to take.

specials.name: Strictures (Zealot)
specials.description: Zealots may never wear armour.

fighters.name: Warhound
fighters.fixed_kit: Jaws and brutality! Warhounds never use or need weapons and armour.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Warhounds are animals and thus do not gain experience.

rules.title: Chain of Command
rules.description: If the warband's leader is taken out of action, work out a new temporary leader at once, as if the leader had been killed for good. He is in charge and has the Leader ability until the end of the game or until he too is taken out of action, when the warband works out another.

rules.title: Personal Guard
rules.description: Every Hero and Henchman of a House Guard intercepts a charge at a friendly Hero within 3" instead of the usual 2". In the Assassination scenario they may ignore the attacker's evasive rule when their protege is the target.

rules.title: Dueling Pride
rules.description: A Fierezza Hero may re-roll failed hits in the first round of combat when he fights an enemy Hero.

rules.title: Sharp Aim
rules.description: Every warrior of House Halcon ignores the long range modifier when he fires a missile weapon.

rules.title: Armour
rules.description: A Baluardo Hero suffers no movement penalty for wearing armour.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Commander may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Relay orders
specials.description: While the Adjutant may use his leader's Leadership, any warrior within 6" of the Adjutant may use the leader's Leadership instead of his own. The Adjutant may take the Battle Tongue skill to raise that range to 12".

specials.name: Pikewall
specials.description: A Pikeman who is charged while wielding a weapon that strikes first may re-roll his failed hits.

fighters.name: Warhound
fighters.fixed_kit: Jaws. A Warhound never uses weapons or armour.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: A Warhound is an animal and gains no experience.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The Imperial Outriders may only be accompanied by mounted Hired Swords. This includes the Freelance Knight from the Mordheim Rulebook and the Roadwarden from the Empire In Flames supplement. The Highwayman keeps himself a safe distance from any official representatives of the Empire and so may not be hired.

lists.name: Imperial Outriders equipment list
lists.note: The following lists are used by Imperial Outrider warbands to pick their weapons:

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6” of the Knight may use his Leadership characteristic when taking a Leadership test.

rules.title: Swabbies/Skinners
rules.description: The warband may try to enlist captured crew as normal. One who agrees joins the Plunderers. One who refuses does not become a Swabbie: the warband gains 1D3 Toughened Leathers free instead.

rules.title: Magic? Bah!
rules.description: No one in the warband may learn magic, and the warband may not hire a Hired Sword or Dramatis Persona who uses magic. It may keep and use any magical item it finds that it could use normally. Apart from spellcasters, it may hire any Hired Sword or Dramatis Persona a Possessed warband may hire.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Dread Captain may use his Leadership for any Leadership test.

specials.name: Massive Swing
specials.description: A Quartermaster may carry one two-handed weapon, a halberd or a double-handed weapon for instance, in one hand. In his other hand he may carry an additional single-handed weapon.

specials.name: Immune to Psychology (Madbrains)
specials.description: A Madbrain passes any Leadership test he is required to take. He may not be promoted to leader.

specials.name: Reckless
specials.description: A Madbrain adds +1 to every injury roll he makes in hand-to-hand combat, and every opponent in hand-to-hand combat adds +1 to injury rolls made against him.

fighters.name: Flayerkin
fighters.fixed_kit: Steel hooks. A Flayerkin takes only armour from the Madbrain Equipment list.

specials.name: Hooks
specials.description: A Flayerkin has a sharp steel hook at the end of each wrist. He gains one extra attack, as if armed with a second weapon, and attacks with the hooks take neither penalty nor bonus. He may use no other weapon.

specials.name: Climbing
specials.description: A Flayerkin always counts as carrying a Rope & Hook.

specials.name: Chain Spine
specials.description: While a Flayerkin is at the top of an elevation and within 1" of the edge, every friendly model directly below him at the bottom counts as carrying a Rope & Hook when climbing up, and any friendly model within 1" of him at the top of an elevation may use that Rope & Hook when climbing down. He still gives this while knocked down, stunned or taken out of action; in the last case, remove the model and leave a marker where he stood.

specials.name: Mindless
specials.description: A Flayerkin never gains experience.

name: Kislevites
source: Town Cryer #16, revised in Mordheim Annual 2002

rules.title: May Hire
rules.description: A Kislevite warband is allowed the same selection of Hired Swords as Human Mercenary warbands.

rules.title: Ancient Enemies
rules.description: Kislevite warbands may never ally with any type of Chaos warband. This restriction pertains to the following warbands: Possessed, Beastmen, Carnival of Chaos, Skaven, Dark Elf, Chaos Dwarf, and any other warbands the players judge to be sufficiently 'Chaotic'.

lists.name: Kislev Warrior Equipment List
lists.note: The following lists are used by Kislevite warbands to pick their weapons:

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Druzhina Captain may use his Leadership characteristic when taking any Leadership tests.

specials.name: Inheritance
specials.description: When the Kislevite warband is first created, the Druzhina Captain is allowed to purchase one item from the Kislevite Warrior equipment list at half the normal cost. This item represents a treasured family heirloom that has been passed down through the generations. Losing an ancestral item is considered very disrespectful and if the item is ever lost (e.g. from a Robbed result on the Serious Injury chart), the Captain MUST replace it with a finely-made substitute as quickly as possible or risk being haunted by the angry spirits of his ancestors. To replace an ancestral item, the Captain must purchase the same item of equipment at 150% of its normal price. This higher cost represents the fine detail and valuable materials used in the item’s manufacture. Until the item is replaced, the Captain suffers a -1 penalty to all tests and rolls to hit.

specials.name: Bear Handler
specials.description: A Kislevite Warband that includes a Bear Tamer is allowed to purchase a Bear as a henchman. This bear has been trained to follow the Tamer’s commands, and so will automatically pass its stupidity tests when within 6" of the Bear Tamer (even if the Tamer has been Knocked Down or Stunned).

specials.name: Hate Chaos
specials.description: Years of bitter struggle against the forces of Chaos have left their mark on the Cossack people. Cossacks are subject to hatred against all forces of Chaos (e.g. members of any warband the players would apply the Ancient Enemies special rule to).

specials.name: Gun-Rest
specials.description: A Streltsi warrior armed with both halberd and handgun may use the halberd as a gun-rest. The warrior receives a +1 on his ‘to hit’ roll with the handgun, as long as he did not move that turn (this applies even if the warrior has a skill that allows him to move and shoot with his handgun – he must not move if he is to rest the gun).

fighters.name: Trained Bear
fighters.fixed_kit: None, other than their claws and teeth!

specials.name: Trained
specials.description: A bear doesn’t care about the warband’s mission or enmity for other warbands – it’s just following the orders of its trainer. Sometimes it gets bored waiting for orders; for this reason Trained Bears are subject to the rules for Stupidity. If given ‘special attention’ by its trainer, it will mind a bit better, so a bear is not required to take these Stupidity tests if the warband’s Bear Tamer is within 6". In fact this is the only member of the warband the bear will listen to; a Trained Bear will never use the warband leader’s Leadership for any tests it is required to take. It may use the Bear Tamer’s leadership if within 6" of him however. Note that the warband cannot control the bear without a Bear Tamer. The Trained Bear may not be used in any game in which the warband's Bear Tamer does not take part (and this means that if the warband does not include a Bear Tamer at all, the warband must keep the bear staked back at camp until they hire a new one!).

specials.name: Bear Hug
specials.description: If the Bear hits the same enemy warrior with both of his attacks in the same round of combat, the player may choose to make a single ‘Bear Hug’ attack instead of resolving the attacks normally. If this option is chosen, each player must roll a D6 and add his model’s Strength to the roll. If the Bear’s total is higher or the totals are equal, the opposing warrior takes a single automatic wound with no armour save allowed. If the enemy warrior’s total is higher, the warrior has broken the Bear’s hold and suffers no damage from the attack.

specials.name: Fiercely Loyal
specials.description: Such dedication is built into the relationship between Bear Tamer and bear that if his trainer is injured, a bear will often stand over the body to protect it, or even drag the trainer’s body to safety. As long as his bear is not taken Out of Action during a game, a Bear Tamer ignores the following results on the Serious Injuries table: ‘Sold to the Pits’, ‘Robbed’, and ‘Captured’ (and ignore equivalent results in settings such as Lustria that have their own special Serious Injury table). If any of these results are rolled for the Bear Tamer, treat the result as a ‘Full Recovery’ instead.

specials.name: Animal
specials.description: Trained Bears are animals and do not gain experience.

rules.title: Peasant Labour
rules.description: The Questing Knight and Knights Errant always pay the starting warband's prices for horses and armour. Squires and the peasantry pay the full price, so armour and horses bought for a Knight may never be passed to them when the warband reallocates its equipment.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: Bretonnians count as Humans and may hire any hired sword Humans may, except those who use black powder, magic or poison. Runes are allowed.

rules.title: Lady's Blessing
rules.description: Before each game, take a Leadership test on the leader's Leadership. If it is passed, every enemy model must roll a 4+ on a D6 each time it wants to fire a black powder weapon, or it may not fire it; and any enemy model must roll a 4+ before it shoots at the Questing Knight or a Knight Errant, whatever its weapon.

rules.title: Squires
rules.description: The warband may never have more Squires than Knights.

specials.name: Leader
specials.type: Warband - Knights of the Bitter Moors
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Questing Knight may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Knights Virtue
specials.type: Warband - Knights of the Bitter Moors
specials.description: A Knight never panics and breaks from combat, so he takes no Leadership test for being all alone.

specials.name: Ride
specials.type: Warband - Knights of the Bitter Moors
specials.description: A Knight has the Ride skill for a horse or a warhorse (Blazing Saddles). He comes with his mount in his cost: a warhorse for the leader, a horse otherwise.

specials.name: Righteous Charge
specials.type: Warband - Knights of the Bitter Moors
specials.description: When the Questing Knight charges mounted with at least one other model within 2" of him, every friendly mounted warrior charging within 4", the Questing Knight too, has +1 to hit, causes fear and is immune to psychology for the first round of combat.

specials.name: Ride
specials.type: Warband - Knights of the Bitter Moors
specials.description: A Knight has the Ride skill for a horse or a warhorse (Blazing Saddles). He comes with his mount in his cost: a warhorse for the leader, a horse otherwise.

specials.name: Knights Virtue
specials.type: Warband - Knights of the Bitter Moors
specials.description: A Knight never panics and breaks from combat, so he takes no Leadership test for being all alone.

specials.name: Knighted
specials.type: Warband - Knights of the Bitter Moors
specials.description: A Squire who reaches 20 experience has finished his apprenticeship and becomes a Knight Errant, with all that comes with it: the Knights' skill lists and equipment list, Knights Virtue and Ride: Warhorse.

specials.name: Mounted or Nothin'
specials.type: Warband - Knights of the Bitter Moors
specials.description: Mounted Yeomen come with riding horses, in their cost, and the skill Ride: Horse. If a Yeoman's horse is killed, it must be bought again before the group fights again.

specials.name: Smarts
specials.type: Warband - Knights of the Bitter Moors
specials.description: The Field Trebuchet and the Mounted Yeomen never take the field in the same game: one or the other.

rules.title: Foreign or Khemrian
rules.description: A Lahmian warband begins either as a newly returned foreign warband or as a native Khemrian one. A foreign warband takes Blood Slaves and Black Hounds, and its Beloved equips from the Mercenary list, but only when the warband is raised; after that every warrior and every piece of equipment lost is replaced from the Khemrian side, so the warband becomes Khemrian over time. A Khemrian warband takes Wights and Jackals, and its Beloved equips from the Arabyan Nomad list when the warband is raised. A Lahmian warband played anywhere but Khemri uses the foreign side for everything, recruiting and re-equipping included.

rules.title: No more than five Heroes
rules.description: The warband may never hold more than 5 Heroes.

rules.title: Vampire warbands without vampires
rules.description: The warband may not recruit a new vampire while it holds a Blood Sister. If the Lahmia is slain the Blood Sister may become a vampire in the post-battle experience phase; until she does, the surviving human Henchman with the highest Leadership leads the warband, and with a tie the one with the most experience. With no Blood Sister the warband is led the same way and a new vampire may be recruited after the next battle. If after a battle the warband holds neither a vampire nor a necromancer, every skeleton and wight is lost as the magic sustaining them fails.

rules.title: Habituation
rules.description: A human member of a Lahmian warband is immune to fear caused by the skeletons, wights and vampires of his own warband. Any other kind of undead causes fear as normal.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the vampire may use her Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Local Knowledge
specials.description: Khemrian warbands only. A Khemrian Lahmian warband with a vampire may re-roll one dice in the exploration phase. This applies only in the Khemri setting.

specials.name: Devoted
specials.description: If the vampire is knocked down or stunned in close combat the Beloved becomes frenzied and at once takes the most direct route to her aid, attacking any model within 2" of either side of a straight line to her. If the vampire is taken out of action the Beloved hates the model that did it and tries to kill it at the earliest opportunity. He stays frenzied until that enemy is slain.

specials.name: Hardened
specials.description: A Blood Sister is immune to fear and never tests for being all alone.

specials.name: Demi-Vampires
specials.description: If the warband's Lahmia is killed the Blood Sister may take her place. At her next advance she becomes a vampire on a 4+ on a D6, and that counts instead of the advance. She keeps her skills and experience, the rules for undead apply to her at once and her maximum characteristics become a vampire's. If she fails, roll again at her next advance and at every one after it. Once a Blood Sister has become a vampire a new Blood Sister may be recruited after the next game.

specials.name: Devoted (Thrall)
specials.description: If the vampire is knocked down or stunned in close combat the Thrall becomes frenzied and at once takes the most direct route to her aid, attacking any model within 2" of either side of a straight line to her. If the vampire is taken out of action he hates the model that did it and tries to kill it at the earliest opportunity.

specials.name: Favoured
specials.description: If the vampire's Beloved is killed she may grant one Thrall the Blood Kiss at his next advance, which counts instead of that advance. His Leadership rises to 8 if it is not already, and he takes the Beloved's place on the roster. A new Thrall may be recruited after the warband's next battle.

specials.name: No Brain
specials.description: A skeleton gains no experience.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: A Black Hound gains no experience and carries no weapons or armour.

specials.name: Wight weapons
specials.description: A wight's weapons are enchanted to drain the living, so his rolls to wound cause a critical hit on a 5+.

specials.name: Pack Attack
specials.description: If two or more jackals attack the same model, every jackal attacking it gains one extra attack.

rules.title: Scaly Skin
rules.description: All Lizardmen have a natural save thanks to their thick scales. Saurus have a 5+ save and Skinks have a 6+. This save cannot be modified beyond 6 due to Strength modifiers but any result of ‘no save’ on the Critical Hit chart will negate this 6+ save. Light Armour adds +1 to the save, as does the addition of a shield.

rules.title: Armour
rules.description: Armour is rare amongst the Lizardmen and the cost of light armour is always 50 gc, even if you are buying it from Equipment chart.

rules.title: Bite Attack
rules.description: Saurus have a powerful bite attack, this bite attack uses the Saurus’ own Strength to wound and receive no penalty for not using a weapon. The Bite attack always strikes last, regardless of who charged or which weapon is used. The Bite even attacks after Double-Handed Weapons.

rules.title: Cold Blooded
rules.description: All Lizardmen are slow to react to psychology, they may roll 3D6 and select the lowest two dice when taking a psychology test or Rout test. A Lizardmen Warband may never use the Leadership of Saurus or Kroxigor when taking a rout test.

rules.title: Aquatic
rules.description: Skinks may move through water terrain with no penalty, and count as being in cover whilst they are in the water.

rules.title: Jungle born
rules.description: All Skinks can move through jungle terrain without penalty.

rules.title: Saurus Rarity
rules.description: The Slann Mage-Priests would never include more Saurus braves in a Warband than Skink braves and thus you can never have more Saurus braves than Skink braves in the Warband.

rules.title: Poisoned Weapons
rules.description:
Skinks are experts at extracting and refining poisons from poisonous frogs, spiders and snakes. Skink Heroes may buy Dark Venom at a cost of 20 pts and Black Lotus at a cost of 10 pts, both of these items are treated as a common item however the poison may only be used on missile weapons. Only Saurus warriors may buy Dark Venom or Black Lotus and use it on their close combat weapons, and they have to buy it as normal from the Trading chart.

Skink henchmen may buy low-strength Reptile Venom for their missile weapons at a cost of 5 pts per weapon. This poison is a common item. This adds +1 to the Strength of the weapon but does not grant the -1 save modifier. The poison only lasts for one battle and remember that all the henchmen in a group must be armed in the same manner.

rules.title: Sacred markings
rules.description: Many Skink and Saurus warriors are born with distinct markings or mutations. They are regarded as being blessed by the gods and often rise to become leaders. A Hero may only have a single Sacred Marking and these may only be bought when you recruit the Hero, not in the middle of a campaign.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description:
The Skink Priest is the leader of the Warband and any Lizardmen within 6" may use his Leadership characteristic for any Leadership tests.

If the Skink Priest is killed you may recruit a new Skink Priest but you must play at least one game without the leader to give him time to join up.

fighters.name: Kroxigor
fighters.fixed_kit: The Kroxigor is equipped with a halberd.

specials.name: Scaly Skin (Kroxigor)
specials.description: Kroxigor has a natural save of 4+.

specials.name: Aquatic
specials.description: Kroxigor may move through water with no penalty, and count as being in cover whilst in water.

specials.name: Animal
specials.description: Kroxigor are slow-witted creatures that never learn from their mistakes. The Kroxigor doesn’t gain experience.

special.name: Oversized Jaws
special.description: The Hero may make his bite attack with +1 Strength. (Saurus Only)

special.name: Poison Glands
special.description: He may choose to make any number of attacks with his teeth instead of his weapons; these attacks are treated just like a Saurus bite attack. These attacks at +1 save modifier, regardless of the Strength of the Skinks, in addition add +1 to the roll on the Injury table as well. (Skinks only)

special.name: Mark of the Old Ones
special.description: The Hero may change one of his failed dice rolls into a successful one; this mark may only be used once per battle and only on actions that the Hero is making himself. You may use this mark on a failed Rout test if you wish.

rules.title: Scaly Skin
rules.description: A Saurus has a 5+ armour save and a Skink a 6+ from his scales. Strength modifiers may not take the save beyond 6, and any "no save" result on the injury chart negates the 6+. Light armour adds +1 to the save, as does a shield.

rules.title: Armour
rules.description: Light armour always costs the warband 50 gold crowns, from the equipment list and from the trading chart alike.

rules.title: Bite Attack
rules.description: A Saurus has a bite attack that wounds with his own Strength and takes no penalty for being unarmed. The bite always strikes last, whoever charged and whatever weapon is used, and strikes after a double-handed weapon.

rules.title: Cold Blooded
rules.description: When taking a psychology test or a Rout test a Lizardman rolls 3D6 and takes the lowest two dice. The warband may never use the Leadership of a Saurus or a Kroxigor for a Rout test.

rules.title: Aquatic
rules.description: A Skink moves through water terrain with no penalty and counts as being in cover while he is in the water.

rules.title: Jungle Born
rules.description: A Skink moves through jungle terrain with no penalty.

rules.title: Saurus Rarity
rules.description: The warband may never hold more Saurus Braves than Skink Braves.

rules.title: Saurus Skill Prohibitions
rules.description: A Saurus may never gain Academic skills and may never use missile weapons.

rules.title: Poisoned Weapons
rules.description: A Skink Hero may buy Dark Venom for 20 gold crowns and Black Lotus for 10 gold crowns, both as common items, and may use them only on missile weapons. A Saurus may buy Dark Venom or Black Lotus for his close combat weapons at the trading chart's price and rarity. A Skink Henchman may buy Reptile Venom for a missile weapon for 5 gold crowns as a common item: it adds +1 to the weapon's Strength, grants no save modifier, and lasts for one battle. Every henchman in a group must be armed the same way.

rules.title: Sacred Markings
rules.description: A Hero may have a single Sacred Marking, and it may only be bought when he is recruited.

lines.note: Skink Heroes only, missile weapons only
Skink Heroes only, missile weapons only
Skink Henchmen only, missile weapons only

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any Lizardman within 6" of the Skink Priest may use his Leadership for any Leadership test. If the Skink Priest is killed you may recruit a new one, but you must play at least one game without a leader first.

fighters.name: Kroxigor
fighters.fixed_kit: A halberd.

specials.name: Aquatic
specials.description: A Kroxigor moves through water with no penalty and counts as being in cover while he is in the water.

specials.name: Animal
specials.description: A Kroxigor never gains experience.

special.name: Oversized Jaws
special.description: Saurus only. The Hero makes his bite attack at +1 Strength.

special.name: Poison Glands
special.description: Skinks only. The Hero may attack with his teeth instead of his weapons. These attacks are resolved as a Saurus bite attack but at a +1 save modifier whatever his Strength, and add +1 to the roll on the injury table.

special.name: Mark of the Old Ones
special.description: The Hero may turn one of his failed dice rolls into a successful one. This may be used once per battle and only on an action he makes himself, a failed Rout test included.

rules.title: Mutations
rules.description: A Fimir Hero may start the campaign with one mutation from the Corrupted Characters chapter, paying its price.

rules.title: From the Mist
rules.description: Fimir see and move normally through any fog, magical mist included.

rules.title: Mystic Mist
rules.description: The warband starts each battle wreathed in mist, cast with its talismans: Mystic Mist, difficulty 7. While it holds, missile attacks at the mist-wreathed Fimir have a further -1 to hit, and Young Nobles and Shearls aren't subject to stupidity. Once cast it lasts until the start of the shooting phase in the player's next turn.

rules.title: Cold-blooded
rules.description: Fimir roll 3D6 for Leadership tests and discard the highest dice.

rules.title: Aquatic
rules.description: Fimir move through water terrain with no penalty, and count as in cover while they are in the water.

rules.title: Swamp Striders
rules.description: Fimir move through swamp and marshland terrain with no penalty.

rules.title: Scaly Skin
rules.description: Fimir have a 6+ armour save, 5+ for Fimir Warriors. Strength modifiers can't take it past 6, but a 'no save' result on a Critical Hit chart removes it. Light armour adds +1 to it, and other armour adds too.

rules.title: Cyclopean Fiends
rules.description: A Hero re-rolls a Blinded in One Eye result on the Serious Injury chart. If it comes again, he is blinded for good.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The warband may hire only a Slaver, Highwayman, Swashbuckler, Bog Hunter or Whaler.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Draich may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Mind Focus
specials.description: When the Draich uses a spell or prayer he may re-roll one dice of the difficulty roll.

specials.name: Craven
specials.description: The model is subject to fear unless it is protected by Mystic Mist.

specials.name: Craven
specials.description: The model is subject to fear unless it is protected by Mystic Mist.

specials.name: Craven
specials.description: The model is subject to fear unless it is protected by Mystic Mist.

specials.name: Monstrous
specials.description: On the henchmen's Injury chart a Fimir Warrior dies only on a 1; a 2-6 leaves him unhurt. He counts as 2 models towards the warband's maximum.
