Trolls may not regenerate wounds caused by fire or fire-based magic. Trolls never roll for Injury after a battle.

specials.name: Dumb Monster
specials.description: A Troll is far too stupid to ever learn any new skills. Trolls do not gain experience.

specials.name: Always Hungry
specials.description: A Troll requires an upkeep cost. This upkeep represents the copious amounts of food that must be fed to the Troll in order to keep him loyal to the warband. The warband must pay 15 gold crowns after every game in order to keep the Troll. If the warband lacks the gold to pay the upkeep, the Boss has the option of sacrificing two Goblin Warriors or Cave Squigs to the Troll in lieu of buying food (Trolls eat nearly anything). If this fee is not paid (either in gold or in warband members) the Troll gets hungry and wanders off in search of food.

specials.name: Vomit Attack
specials.description: Instead of his normal attacks, a Troll can regurgitate its highly corrosive digestive juices on an unfortunate hand-to-hand combat opponent. This is a single attack that automatically hits with a Strength of 5 and ignores armour saves.

rules.title: May Hire
rules.description: The warband may hire the same hired swords as a Human Mercenary warband.

rules.title: Strategic Minded
rules.description: The warband may choose to rout after one casualty fewer than normal.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Hatamoto may use his Leadership when taking any Leadership test.

fighters.name: Vim-To Mage
fighters.fixed_kit: A walking staff (a club) and a dagger only; he may never have any other equipment.

specials.name: Tenants of the Order
specials.description: The Vim-To Mage may have only a walking staff (a club) and a dagger, never any other equipment.

specials.name: Infiltration
specials.description: The Shinobi is set up after the opposing warband, anywhere on the table out of its sight and more than 12" from every enemy model. If both sides have infiltrators, each rolls a D6 and the lowest sets up first.

specials.name: Loner
specials.description: The Shinobi may never become the warband's leader.

specials.name: Wall of Steel
specials.description: An Ashigaru may wield a spear in both hands; it then gains the Parry rule.

specials.name: Wardens of the Castle
specials.description: An Onnabushi inside a building or ruin causes fear. Agree which terrain counts as buildings or ruins before the battle.

rules.title: Seafaring
rules.description: The Norse are seafaring people and spend much of their time rowing boats. To represent this, all Norse warriors get +2 to Strength when they row a boat.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any Warrior within 6“ of the Jarl may use his Leadership instead of his own when taking Ld tests.

specials.name: Bestial
specials.description: Wulfen are ravenous beasts and therefore immune to psychology. Also despite being greatly revered by their barbarian kinsmen, Wulfen are too feral and uncontrolled to become the leader of the warband.

fighters.name: Wolf
fighters.fixed_kit: Wolves have very sharp fangs. They never use or need weapons and armour.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Wolves are animals and thus do not gain experience.

specials.name: Pack Leader
specials.description: Wolves are feral animals that only respond to the strongest in their pack – the Wulfen. In the event that no Wulfen is included in the warband due to a death or an injury, the wolves cannot be used until the creature is replaced.

rules.title: Greenskins
rules.description: Gnoblars count as Greenskins. They don't suffer Animosity; Gnoblar henchmen Bicker instead.

rules.title: Ideas Above Their Station
rules.description: If the Ogre Hunter is killed, the Gnoblar with the highest Leadership becomes the leader (on a tie, the one with the most experience). A new Ogre Hunter may be bought, and he becomes the leader.

rules.title: Distasteful Company
rules.description: The warband may hire only a Hobgoblin Scout, a Gnoblar Botcher or a Ninja Gnoblar. While it has no Ogre Hunter it may also hire an Ogre Bodyguard and an Ogre Slaver; if it hires an Ogre Hunter again, every other Ogre leaves.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Ogre Hunter may use his Leadership when taking Leadership tests.

specials.name: Huuuuge
specials.description: The Ogre Hunter ignores All Alone tests. He can never have ithilmar, gromril or heavy armour. He adds 20 to the warband rating, plus his experience, instead of 5.

specials.name: Slow Witted
specials.description: The Ogre Hunter needs twice the usual experience for each advance.

specials.name: Don't Fight with Eating Knives
specials.description: The Ogre Hunter has no free dagger and never fights with one. With no other weapon he fights unarmed, as many attacks as his Attacks, with no -1 Strength penalty; the enemy still has +1 to his armour save. He can't add an unarmed attack to another weapon's.

specials.name: Lazy
specials.description: While any Gnoblar Hero is able to search for wyrdstone or rare items, the Ogre Hunter rolls no exploration die and doesn't search. He explores and searches only when no other Gnoblar Hero can (for example, all were taken out of action).

specials.name: Central Figure
specials.description: If the Ogre Hunter is taken out of action, the warband is at once at its Rout level, whatever its casualties.

specials.name: Sabre Trainer
specials.description: The Ogre Hunter has the Sabre Trainer skill: when a Sabretusk Cub that started the turn within 6" of him rolls a 1 for Untamed, you may move it 3D6" towards any model within 12" of it that it can see, instead of the nearest.

specials.name: Veteran Tracker
specials.description: When hired, a Trapper takes one of these special skills: Infiltration (one Trapper at most), Set Traps, Netter or Scent Hound.

specials.name: Bait
specials.description: When a model declares a charge against the Sabre-Baiter, he may at once move D6" directly away from the charger, which fails its charge if he ends out of its reach. Once a turn, and only if he isn't knocked down, stunned or in hand-to-hand combat. Against a charging Sabretusk he moves 2D6" instead and may move around models in his way, so the Sabretusk may end up charging another model.

specials.name: Bicker
specials.description: At the end of your Recovery phase roll a D6 for each Gnoblar henchman not in combat: on a 1 he only hurls insults at the nearest Gnoblar, and may not move, shoot or cast spells this turn. A Gnoblar who gains That Lad's Got Talent loses Bicker.

specials.name: Bicker
specials.description: At the end of your Recovery phase roll a D6 for each Gnoblar henchman not in combat: on a 1 he only hurls insults at the nearest Gnoblar, and may not move, shoot or cast spells this turn. A Gnoblar who gains That Lad's Got Talent loses Bicker.

specials.name: Scrap Slinger
specials.description: A Flinger may throw 3 pieces of Sharp Stuff a turn instead of 1. Not with Knife Thrower, and not with throwing knives.

fighters.name: Sabretusk Cub
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Sabretusks fight with tusks and claws.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Sabretusks are animals and never gain experience.

specials.name: Untamed
specials.description: Sabretusks don't Bicker. At the start of each turn roll a D6 for each Sabretusk not in combat: on a 1, instead of moving normally, it moves 3D6" towards the nearest model that isn't a Sabretusk, which counts as a charge. If it charges a model of your warband, move it 1" away after the combat.

specials.name: Charge
specials.description: A Sabretusk has 2 Attacks instead of 1 in a turn it charges.

specials.name: Tough Hide
specials.description: Sabretusks have a natural 5+ armour save.

name: Orc Mob
source: Town Cryer #6, revised in Mordheim Annual 2002

rules.title: Distasteful Company
rules.description: Many Hired Swords refuse to work for Orcs, as they know that Orcs are just as likely to eat them as fight alongside them. Orcs may only hire the following Hired Swords: Pit Fighters, Ogre Bodyguards or Warlocks.

rules.title: Animosity
rules.description:
Orcs and Goblins enjoy nothing more than a good scrap, unfortunately they’re not always very discerning about who they scrap with! To represent this, at the start of the Orc player’s turn, roll a D6 for each Henchman who is either an Orc or a Goblin. A roll of 1 means that the warrior has taken offense to something one of his mates has done or said. Do not roll for models that are engaged in hand-to-hand combat (they’re already scrappin’!). To find out just how offended the model is, roll another D6 and consult the following chart to see what happens:

Animosity Result

D6 | Result
1 | “I ’Erd Dat!”
The warrior decides that the nearest friendly Orc or Goblin Henchman has insulted his lineage or personal hygiene and must pay the price!
If there is a friendly Orc or Goblin Henchman or Hired Sword within charge reach (if there are multiple targets within reach, choose the one nearest to the mad model), the offended warrior will immediately charge and fight a round of hand-to-hand combat against the source of his ire. At the end of this round of combat, the models will immediately move 1" apart and no longer count as being in close combat (unless one of them fails another Animosity test and rolls this result again).
If there are no friendly Orc or Goblin Henchmen or Hired Swords within charge reach, and the warrior is armed with a missile weapon, he immediately takes a shot at the nearest friendly Orc or Goblin Henchman or Hired Sword. If none of the above applies, or if the nearest friendly model is an Orc Hero, the warrior behaves as if a 2-5 had been rolled on this chart. In any case, the warrior in question may take no other action this turn, though he may defend himself if attacked in hand-to-hand combat.
2-5 | “Wud Yoo Say?”
The warrior is fairly certain he heard an offensive sound from the nearest friendly Orc or Goblin, but he’s not quite sure. He spends the turn hurling insults at his mate.
He may do nothing else this turn, though he may defend himself if attacked in hand-to-hand combat.
6 | “I’ll Show Yer!”
The warrior imagines that his mates are laughing about him behind his back and calling him silly names. To show them up he decides that he’ll be the first one to the scrap!
This model must move as quickly as possible towards the nearest enemy model, charging into combat if possible. If there are no enemy models within sight, the Orc or Goblin warrior may make a normal move immediately. This move is in addition to his regular move in the Movement phase, so he may therefore move twice in a single turn if you wish.
If the extra move takes the Orc or Goblin warrior within charge reach of an enemy model, the warrior must charge into close combat during his regular movement.

rules.title: Pressganging
rules.description: The warband may pressgang models it captures by the normal rules. One who agrees loses his race and profile and joins the crew as an Orc Boy. One who refuses becomes a Goblin Swabbie, keeps his race and profile, and gains Never Gain Experience, Rabble, "Blimey, they got away!" and "Don't mind them mates, they ain't true pirates!".

rules.title: Talismans galore
rules.description: Every Orc and Goblin in the warband has a 6+ armour save, which may not be reduced below 6+ and may not be ignored, even by a critical hit. They may never use armour other than a shield, and may never parry.

rules.title: Fear fire
rules.description: Every member of a Savage Orc warband fears any model with a flaming attack, carrying a lit item (a lantern, a torch, a brazier) or any flame item. A caster who works a fiery spell in sight of a member of the warband, or who keeps up a fire-based spell, causes fear for the whole game.

rules.title: Primitive
rules.description: The warband may never use an advanced weapon, and may never take the Weapons Master or Weapons Expert skills. Its members may not use a Halfling Cookbook, a Mordheim Map, a Tome of Magic or a Lantern.

rules.title: Wild Animosity
rules.description:
Wild Animosity replaces the Orcs' Animosity. At the start of the turn, roll a D6 for every standing warrior in the warband who is not in combat, the troll included unless he failed his stupidity test, and the heroes included. Every warrior rolls, not only those who roll a 1.

D6 | Result
1 | Squabble. A henchman must charge the nearest friendly model at once, hero or henchman, and fight one round of combat; after it neither may do anything else this turn, though both fight back if attacked. With no friendly model in charge range he uses a missile weapon, if he has one, against the nearest friendly model, and otherwise does nothing. A Forest Goblin will never attack a hero this way. A hero attacks no one, but may still do nothing else.
2-5 | Uggg. The model behaves normally.
6 | Waaaagh! The model makes a full move at once towards the nearest enemy model, charging it if it can. In its next movement phase it must charge if an enemy is within charge range. These charges ignore fear and any other psychology that would stop the Savage Orc charging.

lists.name: Orc Equipment List
lists.note: The following lists are used by Orc Mob warbands to pick their equipment.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Orc Boss may use his Leadership characteristic when taking Leadership tests.

specials.name: No Armour
specials.description: An Orc Shaman may never wear armour.

specials.name: Animosity
specials.description: Orc Boyz are subject to the rules for Animosity (see Special Rules for details).

specials.name: Animosity (Goblin Warrior)
specials.description: Goblin Warriors are subject to the rules for Animosity (see Special Rules for details). Note: A Goblin Warrior who fails his Animosity test and rolls a 1 for the result will never charge an Orc Henchman, though he will still use any missile weapons to attack as normal. Goblins are far too afraid of Orcs to challenge them individually.

specials.name: Not Orcs
specials.description: Orcs don’t expect much from non-Orcs, and are therefore not unsettled if Goblins or Cave Squigs break or get cut down in battle. In fact, they expect as much from these weaklings! Therefore, when testing to see if an Orc Warband needs to take a Rout test, each Goblin Warrior or Cave Squig taken out of action only counts as half a model. Therefore, a band of 5 Orcs and 10 Goblins (15 models) would only have to take a test if 4 models fell (4 Orcs or 8 Goblins, or some combination thereof ).

specials.name: Runts
specials.description: Goblins may gain experience but if they happen to roll ‘That Lad’s got talent’ they are immediately killed by their Orc overlords for becoming too ‘mouthy’ (remove the Gobbo from the roster).

fighters.name: Cave Squig
fighters.fixed_kit: Big gob and brutality! Cave Squigs never use or need weapons or armour.

specials.name: Movement
specials.description: Cave Squigs do not have a set Movement characteristic but move with an ungainly bouncing stride. To represent this, when moving Squigs, roll 2D6 for the distance they move. Squigs never run and never declare charges. Instead, they are allowed to contact enemy models with their normal 2D6" movement. If this happens, they count as charging for the following round of close combat, just as if they had declared a charge.

specials.name: Minderz
specials.description: Each Cave Squig must always remain within 6" of a Goblin Warrior, who keeps the creature in line. If a Cave Squig finds itself without a Goblin within 6" at the start of its Movement phase, it will go wild. From that point on, move the Squig 2D6" in a random direction during each of its Movement phases. If its movement takes it into contact with another model (friend or foe), it will engage the model in hand-to-hand combat as normal. The Cave Squig is out of the Orc & Goblin player’s control until the end of the game.

specials.name: Not Orcs
specials.description: Orcs don’t expect much from non-Orcs, and are therefore not unsettled if Goblins or Cave Squigs break or get cut down in battle. In fact, they expect as much from these weaklings! Therefore, when testing to see if an Orc Warband needs to take a Rout test, each Goblin Warrior or Cave Squig taken out of action only counts as half a model. Therefore, a band of 5 Orcs and 10 Goblins (15 models) would only have to take a test if 4 models fell (4 Orcs or 8 Goblins, or some combination thereof ).

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Cave Squigs are animals of a sort and so do not gain experience.

fighters.name: Troll
fighters.fixed_kit: Trolls do not require weapons to fight but often carry a big club. In any event, Trolls can never be given weapons or armour.

specials.name: Regeneration (Troll)
specials.description: Trolls have a unique physiology that allow them to regenerate wounds. Whenever an enemy successfully inflicts a wound on a Troll roll a D6, on a result of 4 or more the wound is ignored and the Troll is unhurt. Trolls may not regenerate wounds caused by fire or fire-based magic. Trolls never roll for Injury after a battle.

specials.name: Dumb Monster
specials.description: A Troll is far too stupid to ever learn any new skills. Trolls do not gain experience.

specials.name: Always Hungry
specials.description: A Troll requires an upkeep cost. This upkeep represents the copious amounts of food that must be fed to the Troll in order to keep him loyal to the warband. The warband must pay 15 gold crowns after every game in order to keep the Troll. If the warband lacks the gold to pay the upkeep, the Boss has the option of sacrificing two Goblin Warriors or Cave Squigs to the Troll in lieu of buying food (Trolls eat nearly anything). If this fee is not paid (either in gold or in warband members) the Troll gets hungry and wanders off in search of food.

specials.name: Vomit Attack
specials.description: Instead of his normal attacks, a Troll can regurgitate its highly corrosive digestive juices on an unfortunate hand-to-hand combat opponent. This is a single attack that automatically hits with a Strength of 5 and ignores armour saves.

specials.name: Glass Ceiling
specials.description: A Goblin Enjuneer may never be the warband's leader.

specials.name: Booma Tweaker
specials.description: In any game the Enjuneer plays in, whenever a Booma Pistol's range is rolled and the result is not a misfire, the roll may be re-rolled once. The second result stands and may not be re-rolled, even if it is a misfire.

specials.name: Mad Bomba
specials.description: When the Enjuneer spends his rarity roll looking for a Fire Bomb, he treats it as Rare 5. This holds only when the Enjuneer himself searches.

specials.name: Under der Thumb
specials.description: A Goblin Swabbie is not subject to Animosity.

specials.name: Spendible
specials.description: The warband may shoot into a combat that holds only a Goblin Swabbie and enemy models; the shots are distributed at random.

specials.name: Never Gain Experience
specials.description: A Goblin Swabbie never gains experience.

specials.name: Rabble
specials.description: Goblin Swabbies need not be armed alike. Each may be given different equipment, but only from the Goblin Swabbie Equipment list. A Goblin Swabbie may never use magic or cast a spell of any kind, whatever his background.

specials.name: Blimey, they got away
specials.description: If the warband routs, every Goblin Swabbie who had already left the table in an earlier turn is taken to have escaped: remove him from the roster as if he had been killed.

specials.name: Don't mind them mates, they ain't true pirates
specials.description: A Goblin Swabbie who is running away or has been taken out of action does not count towards the warband's rout test.

fighters.name: Sea Squig
fighters.fixed_kit: A Sea Squig never uses or needs a weapon or armour.

specials.name: Movement (Sea Squig)
specials.description: A Sea Squig has no set Movement. On land he moves 2D6-1" each turn, and in water he swims 2D6", which water penalties do not reduce. He does not count as aquatic. He never runs and never declares a charge; instead he may reach an enemy with his normal move, and then counts as charging for that round of close combat.

specials.name: Minderz (Sea Squig)
specials.description: A Sea Squig must stay within 6" of a Goblin. He will not go wild while within 12" of a Goblin carrying a Cat O' Nine Tails, which counts as a Squig Prodder. Without a minder at the start of his movement phase he goes wild: from then on move him 2D6" in a random direction each movement phase, and he engages any model he reaches, friend or foe.

specials.name: Not Orcs (Sea Squig)
specials.description: A Goblin or a Sea Squig taken out of action counts as half a model when working out whether the warband must take a rout test.

specials.name: Animals (Sea Squig)
specials.description: A Sea Squig never gains experience.

fighters.name: Sea Troll
fighters.fixed_kit: A Sea Troll needs no weapon and may never be given a weapon or armour.

specials.name: Regeneration (Sea Troll)
specials.description: Whenever a wound is inflicted on a Sea Troll, roll a D6: on a 4 or more the wound is ignored. He may not regenerate a wound caused by fire or fire-based magic, and never rolls for injury after a battle.

specials.name: Dumb Monster (Sea Troll)
specials.description: A Sea Troll never learns a skill and never gains experience.

specials.name: Always Hungry (Sea Troll)
specials.description: The warband must pay 15 gold crowns after every game to keep a Sea Troll. If it lacks the gold, the Boss may feed him two Goblin Swabbies or Sea Squigs instead.

specials.name: Aquatic
specials.description: A Sea Troll takes no penalty for moving through water and counts as aquatic.

specials.name: Slimy
specials.description: Any model trying to hit a Sea Troll in hand-to-hand combat is at -1 to hit; a natural 6 to hit always hits.

specials.name: Not Orcs (Forest Goblin)
specials.description: A Forest Goblin or a Cave Squig taken out of action counts as half a model when working out whether the warband must take a rout test.

specials.name: Runts (Forest Goblin)
specials.description: A Forest Goblin may gain experience, but if he rolls That Lad's Got Talent his Orc overlords kill him at once: remove him from the roster.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The warband may hire the same Hired Swords and Dramatis Personae as a Mercenary warband.

rules.title: Horse and rider
rules.description: When the Paragon and the Gallant are recruited, each may buy a single horse or warhorse at half the normal price.

rules.title: A Dame without delay
rules.description: The warband must hold a Dame of the Mare. If she is lost, a new one is recruited before any other warrior.

rules.title: Blazing Saddles
rules.description: If the Blazing Saddles supplement (Town Cryer 14) is in play, the Paragon, the Gallant, the Esquiresses and the Redeemed knights all have the Ride skill, and the warband may ignore the limit of two mounts in areas of dense terrain.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any member of the warband within 6" of the Paragon may use his Leadership for a Leadership test.

specials.name: Knight's virtue
specials.description: A knight never panics and never breaks from combat, and takes no Leadership test for being all alone.

specials.name: Vow of poverty
specials.description: The Paragon may not use a Lance.

fighters.name: Dame of the Mare
fighters.fixed_kit: An ancient armour that may never be taken off, traded or stolen. It does not stop her casting and gives a 5+ save that may not be modified, but does not work against a magical attack.

specials.name: Prayers
specials.description: The Dame of the Mare prays from the Blessings of the Mare. She starts with one, chosen at random.

specials.name: Knight's virtue
specials.description: A knight never panics and never breaks from combat, and takes no Leadership test for being all alone.

specials.name: Hatred
specials.description: Pilgrims hate every enemy of the Dame of the Mare.

specials.name: Peasants
specials.description: A Pilgrim may never become a Hero: re-roll any Lad's Got Talent result.

specials.name: Knight's virtue
specials.description: A knight never panics and never breaks from combat, and takes no Leadership test for being all alone.

fighters.name: Companion filly
fighters.fixed_kit: A covering that gives a 5+ save which may not be modified, but does not work against a magical attack. The filly may take no other equipment.

specials.name: Hooves
specials.description: The filly fights with its hooves and takes no penalty for fighting unarmed.

specials.name: Horse
specials.description: The filly is an animal and never gains experience. It follows the movement rules for a mounted warrior.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The warband may take only mounted hired swords, among them the Freelance Knight, the Roadwarden and the Halfling Knight. The Roadwarden costs 10 gc less than usual to hire, so 30 gc, and 5 gc more per game to keep, so 25 gc upkeep. The Highwayman may not be hired.

rules.title: Horses
rules.description: The warband is not limited to two horses. A horse adds +3 to the warband's rating and a warhorse +5.

fighters.name: Warden
fighters.fixed_kit: A Riding Horse, which may be upgraded to a Warhorse for 40 gc more.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Warden may use his Leadership for a Leadership test.

fighters.name: Reeve
fighters.fixed_kit: A Riding Horse, which may be upgraded to a Warhorse for 40 gc more.

fighters.name: Courier
fighters.fixed_kit: A Riding Horse.

fighters.name: Chasseur
fighters.fixed_kit: A Riding Horse.

specials.name: Horse Handling
specials.description: A Groom has the Animal Handling skill from the Blazing Saddles article.

name: Ostlander Mercenaries
source: Town Cryer #11, revised in Mordheim Annual 2002

rules.title: Self-Sufficient
rules.description: The men of Ostland have no desire to give their hard-earned gold to outsiders. As a result they can never hire any Mercenaries except for Ogres (who are not an uncommon sight in Ostland).

lists.name: Ostlander Equipment List
lists.note: The following lists are used by Ostlander warbands to pick their weapons:

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Elder may use his Leadership characteristic when taking Leadership tests.

specials.name: Prayers
specials.description: A Priest of Taal may use the Prayers of Taal.

specials.name: Strictures
specials.description: Priests of Taal may never wear heavy armour.

specials.name: Drunk
specials.description: Ruffians are blasted out of their any minds on rotgut spirits and cheap ale. As such, they automatically pass all Leadership based tests they are required to take.

specials.name: No Respect
specials.description: Ruffians are objects of a strange mix of pity and abject fear for their fellows and may never become a warband leader.

specials.name: No Missile Weapons
specials.description: Ruffians never use missile weapons, as their depth perception leaves a bit to be desired, even if they gain an Advance roll which would otherwise allow them to do so.

specials.name: Skills
specials.description: An Ogre who becomes a Hero as a result of The Lad’s Got Talent may choose from the Combat and Strength skills.

specials.name: Slow Witted
specials.description: Although Ogres are capable of earning experience and bettering themselves they are not the smartest of creatures. Ogres only gain advances at half the rate of everyone else (ie, they must accrue twice as much experience as normal to get an advance).

rules.title: Bowmen
rules.description: All warriors in an Outlaws warband may be equipped with only one missile weapon at any time. All warriors must carry a type of bow, but not crossbows, as part of their equipment. So, even if an Outlaw acquires skills that allow him to use additional ballistic weaponry, he cannot do so. The only exception to this is the Cleric who may choose to carry a bow, but is not compelled to do so.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The following Hired Swords are not available to the Outlaws: Bounty Hunter, Wolf-Priest of Ulric, Norse Shaman, Dark Elf Assassin.

lists.name: Outlaws equipment list
lists.note: The following lists are used by Outlaws warbands to pick their weapons:

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any models in the warband within 6" of the Bandit Leader may use her Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Hiring a Cleric
specials.description: Your warband may include up to one Cleric, but he can only be taken instead of either a Champion or a Petty Thief.

specials.name: Disciple of Sigmar
specials.description: The Cleric has devoted his life in the constant service to Sigmar and as such he would start a campaign knowing one of the Prayers of Sigmar. As with a Witch-Hunter’s Warrior Priest, he is also subject to some of the restrictions of being a follower of the Lord Sigmar and may learn neither Sorcery nor Arcane Lore.

rules.title: Bowmen
rules.description: Every warrior may carry only one missile weapon at a time, and must carry a bow of some kind (never a crossbow), even if a skill would let him use other missile weapons. Only the Cleric may go without a bow.

specials.name: Leader
specials.type: Warband - Outlaws of Stirwood Forest, Redux
specials.description: Models of the warband within 6" of the Bandit Leader may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Instead of a Champion or Petty Thief
specials.type: Warband - Outlaws of Stirwood Forest, Redux
specials.description: The warband may take a Cleric only in place of one of its Champions or Petty Thieves.

specials.name: Disciple of Sigmar
specials.type: Warband - Outlaws of Stirwood Forest, Redux
specials.description: The Cleric starts knowing one of the Prayers of Sigmar (rulebook p57). Prayers aren't spells, so he may wear armour. Like a Witch Hunters' Warrior Priest, he may learn neither Sorcery nor Arcane Lore.

rules.title: Swabbies
rules.description:
Pirate warbands can ‘recruit’ new members to join the adventuresome life of a pirate, sometimes willingly but oftentimes more as an alternative to walking the plank! Only humans can be recruited in this manner though – not even the most bloodthirsty pirate would ever trust a Skaven or Beastman, and other races even though friendly to mankind would normally never follow a mere human into battle! The following special rules apply to certain situations in Mordheim game play:

Kidnapped! Enemy human Heroes who after the game rolled up the Captured result (D66 roll of 61) can be ‘offered’ one opportunity to join the pirate crew (usually at the point of a cutlass!). As an alternative to exchanging/ransoming the captured Hero back to their original Warband (or selling him to slavers), the Pirate Captain can instead add the captured enemy to the ship’s crew as follows. Both players roll 2D6, with the Pirate player adding the Captain’s Leadership and the enemy player adding the Leadership of the captured Hero. If either side won that game, it may add +1 to it’s score.

If the Pirate player’s result is higher, the Hero renounces his old ways for the life of the high seas! She or he joins the Crew, either starting a new Crew group or joining an existing one if it has four models or less. There is no extra cost to add him to a group which has accumulated experience points, and any equipment or weapons he had are immediately sold off to buy him the proper weapons and armour to match his new unit in an even swap. His skills and characteristics are changed to those of a starting Crewman, or to match those of his new crewmates if joining an existing group.

Otherwise, the Hero has resisted the siren’s song of the sea, and is forced to become a Swabbie (see Swabbies below). He is stripped of his equipment and weapons; these are handed out as the player desires. He does retain any skills and keeps his original characteristics, but can only be re-armed with the weapons listed in the Swabbie equipment list.

Enemy human Henchmen taken Out of Action during the game and then lost from their original Warband for good (a 1-2 was rolled for them post-game) also have a chance of joining up too! Roll another D6 for each: on a roll of 4+, the Pirates manage to drag them away or otherwise make off with their wounded bodies, and patch them up on the ship. The Pirate player can then test to see if they will join exactly as above, by both players rolling 2D6 and adding it to the Captain’s and the Henchman’s Leadership. This test can only be done if the Pirates win the game, so the Pirate player will always get a +1 to his roll.

Hired Swords and Special Characters are too skilled to be taken off in this manner, and can never be recruited – they have their own agendas to pursue, and will ensure the pirate life is not part of those plans.

Well now matey, have you ever considered pirating as a career? If the Pirates encounter Stragglers (result 44) or Prisoners (result 333) when Searching, there is a chance they may sign up to sail under the Jolly Roger. Either of these options may be used instead of the regular options listed for these situations.

If a Straggler is found, the Captain can try to convince him to join the crew by making a successful Leadership test. If passed, the Straggler joins as a Swabbie (he’s too unhinged even to become a member of the Crew!)

If Prisoners are found, roll a D3 to determine how many are rescued. If the Captain passes a Leadership test (he must make a separate test for each one), the Prisoner eagerly joins his rescuers as a member of the Crew, either starting a new Crew group or joining an existing one if it has four models or less. If he is starting a new Crew group, he will start at the normal characteristics levels for a normal Crew member and at Zero Experience. There is no extra cost to add him to an existing group which has accumulated experience points, and his skills and characteristics match those of his new crewmates. The player must pay though to equip and arm the new Crewman as per his new unit. If the player cannot pay, the prisoner must join as a Swabbie. If the test is failed, the Prisoner isn’t quite so convinced of the worthiness of the sea dogs and is added as a Swabbie.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: Unless noted otherwise, Pirate Warbands have the same access to Hired Swords & any other items as for a regular human Mercenary Warband, and follow all the normal rules for them as well. They must however pay an additional +20 gc in upkeep if they have both Dwarfs and Elves together in the same warband (the ship is only so big, and the confines make them more irritable than usual!).

rules.title: One-off games
rules.description: In one-off games, a Pirate Warband starts with two Swabbies for free.

rules.title: Succession
rules.description: If the Captain is killed, one of the Mates will take over in the same manner as a Champion taking over for a Mercenary warband.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any pirate within 6" of the Captain may use his Leadership characteristic when taking any Leadership tests.

specials.name: Swivel Guns is Dangerous, Matey!
specials.description: Gunners are known to be amongst the bravest of pirates, given their close proximity to blackpowder weapons, but even among themselves they stand in awe of any Gunner who takes a Swivel Gun into battle. Usually they stand in awe quite far away from him – even they can’t be sure when one might blow! If a Pirate Warband includes a Swivel Gun, the Gunner wielding it will always be considered an individual and can never have anyone else with him. Since a Pirate Warband may only have one Swivel Gun, if a Gunner is equipped with one then he must either be a new Gunner, or split from an existing unit. If the latter, he retains all Experience and Skills he had previously.

fighters.name: Boatswain
fighters.fixed_kit: Boatswains start with a Rope & Hook, and may be equipped with weapons and armour chosen from the Pirate Equipment list. Note that they can never sell off or give away their Rope & Hook – a Boatswain would never be without his ropes!

specials.name: Expert Riggers
specials.description: Boatswains are highly trained in using their ropes, as they are the ones who maintain the complex network of rigging throughout the ship. They may re-roll failed Initiative tests Leaping over Gaps, Jumping Down, and performing a Diving Charge, as well as the normal test for Climbing Up or Down that a Rope allows.

specials.name: Not Hired
specials.description: Swabbies are not hired, they follow the special ‘recruitment’ rules above.

specials.name: Never Gain Experience
specials.description: Swabbies generally aren’t interested in proving their worth to the crew, they are interested in survival and hopefully escape! Swabbies never gain experience in games.

specials.name: Rabble
specials.description: Swabbies do not need to be armed all the same. Each may be given different equipment, but only items listed in the Swabbie equipment list. Swabbies can never use magic, or cast spells of any sort, no matter their original background or abilities.

specials.name: ‘Blimey, they got away!’
specials.description: If the Pirate Warband itself Routs, any Swabbies who have already left the table in previous turns are presumed to have made a successful escape, and are never seen from again. Remove them from your warband roster as if they had been killed.

specials.name: ‘Don’t mind them mates, they ain’t true pirates!’
specials.description: The rest of the crew barely notice if any Swabbies run away or go Out of Action – they know they’ll find them later on and give them 30 lashes if they’re lucky! Any Swabbies who are running away or have been taken out of action do not count towards the need to take a Rout test for the warband.

rules.title: Swabbies
rules.description: The warband may capture human Swabbies with the Swabbies rules. One who agrees joins the Deck Hands; one who refuses becomes a Floordog.

rules.title: Swivel Guns are Rare
rules.description: The warband may not start a campaign game with a Swivel Gun on its roster. In a one-off game it may buy one for 2D6 gc on top of its price.

rules.title: Foreign, but Human
rules.description: The warband counts as a Human Pirate warband, as Ostlanders and Averlanders count as Mercenaries.

rules.title: Stranger in a Strange Land
rules.description: In any campaign set in the Old World, Mordheim, Albion, Sylvania and Sartosa among them, roll two dice for the order of deployment and take the lower. A Compass cancels this and gives nothing more. The warband does not suffer it in the Border Town Burning campaign, nor in Lustria, Khemri or the Crusades.

rules.title: Succession
rules.description: If the Disgraced Warlord is killed, one of the Shanghai'ers takes over, as a Champion does in a Mercenary warband.

specials.name: Leader
specials.type: Warband - Pirates of the Cathayan Sea
specials.description: Any pirate within 6" of the Disgraced Warlord may use his Leadership for any Leadership test.

fighters.name: Dragon Monk
fighters.fixed_kit: A Dragon Monk takes no penalty at all for fighting unarmed and gains +1 Attack when he does. He may never wear armour.

specials.name: Art of Silent Death
specials.type: Warband - Pirates of the Cathayan Sea
specials.description: Fighting unarmed in hand-to-hand combat, a Dragon Monk causes a critical hit on a roll to wound of 5 or 6 instead of 6. While he wields a quarterstaff, only his unarmed attacks cause a critical hit on a 5+.

specials.name: Distaste for Poison
specials.type: Warband - Pirates of the Cathayan Sea
specials.description: A Dragon Monk may never use a poison or a venom of any kind.

specials.name: Swivel Guns are Dangerous
specials.type: Warband - Pirates of the Cathayan Sea
specials.description: A Gunner carrying the warband's Swivel Gun always counts as an individual and may never have anyone else with him. As the warband may hold only one Swivel Gun, the Gunner who carries it must either be a new Gunner or be split from an existing group, in which case he keeps the experience and skills he had.

specials.name: Agile (Martial Artist)
specials.type: Warband - Pirates of the Cathayan Sea
specials.description: A Martial Artist always counts as carrying a Rope & Hook. He may also re-roll a failed Initiative test for leaping a gap, jumping down, a diving charge, and the test a rope allows for climbing up or down.

specials.name: Not Hired
specials.type: Warband - Pirates of the Cathayan Sea
specials.description: Floordogs are not hired: they come to the warband by the Swabbies rules.

specials.name: Never Gain Experience
specials.type: Warband - Pirates of the Cathayan Sea
specials.description: A Floordog never gains experience.

specials.name: Rabble
specials.type: Warband - Pirates of the Cathayan Sea
specials.description: Floordogs need not be armed alike. Each may be given different equipment, but only from the Floordog Equipment list. A Floordog may never use magic or cast a spell of any kind, whatever his background.

specials.name: Wo kao, they got away
specials.type: Warband - Pirates of the Cathayan Sea
specials.description: If the warband routs, every Floordog who had already left the table in an earlier turn is taken to have escaped: remove him from the roster as if he had been killed.

specials.name: Don't mind them Lao Xiong, they ain't true pirates
specials.type: Warband - Pirates of the Cathayan Sea
specials.description: A Floordog who is running away or has been taken out of action does not count towards the warband's rout test.

rules.title: Pit Fighter
rules.description: All Pit Fighters have the Pit Fighter skill as described in the Strength Skill List (+1 WS, +1 A when fighting in ruins, buildings and The Pit).

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: Pit Fighters may hire all Hired Swords available except for the Elf Ranger, who feels working with such dirty and brutish individuals would just not do!

rules.title: Weapons & Armour
rules.description:
Unlike other warbands that may chose which weapons and armour to equip their warriors with, Pit Fighters have to chose a specific fighting style which dictates their weapons and armour configuration. This is with the exception of Trollslayers and Ogres that may chose from a limited selection of equipment. The fighting style does not restrict Heroes from using items not on their list if they learn the appropriate skills.

Pit Fighters may chose to change their fighting style at any stage by either swapping with another warrior in the warband or by simply buying a new style (or the separate components). Pit Fighter warbands also differ from other warbands in that a Henchman group may contain a mix of several different fighting styles and does not have to equip all of its warriors in the same manner.

rules.title: Pit Fighter fighting styles
rules.description:
Orc style, 20 gc: Helmet, Dagger, Axe, Shield
Undead style, 35 gc: Helmet, Dagger, Spiked Gauntlet, Sword
Empire style, 45 gc: Helmet, Dagger, Double-handed Weapon, Light armour
Chaos style, 50 gc: Helmet, Dagger, Flail, Shield, Light armour

rules.title: Pursuer fighting styles
rules.description:
Skink style, 25 gc: Helmet, Dagger, Trident or Javelins, Net or Buckler
Witch elf style, 30 gc: Helmet, Dagger, 2 x Sword or Spear & Net

rules.title: Free the Slaves!
rules.description: Pit Fighters hate all slavers. The Pit Fighters will never sell their captured opponents to the slavers.

rules.title: In the Pit!
rules.description: Pit Fighters who capture an opponent may decide to let him fight in the infamous fighting pits of Cutthroat’s Haven (use the rules that appeared earlier in this magazine). The Pit Fighter warband may decide to send in one or more of their own fighters to fight the captive. If the Pit Fighter wins, he gains +2 Experience, the warband gets all the captive’s armour and weapons +50gc. If the Pit Fighter loses, then roll to see whether he is dead or injured as normal (ignore all following results: Robbed, Captured, Hardened, Sold to the Pits, and Survives against the Odds). He will not lose his armour or weapons. The captive will get the 50gc and the +2 Experience when he wins. If the captive wins, the audience decides whether he gains his freedom. Roll a D6; on a 4+ the audience raises their thumbs and he is free. A 1-3 means he remains the Pit Fighters’ captive and may be fielded in the pits after future games.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any models in the Warband within 6" of the King may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Hard to Kill
specials.description: Dwarfs are tough, resilient individuals who can only be taken out of action on a roll of a 6 instead of 5-6 when rolling on the Injury chart. Treat a roll of 1-2 as knocked down, 3-5 as stunned, and 6 as out of action.

specials.name: Hard Head
specials.description: Dwarfs ignores the special rules for maces, clubs, etc. They are not easy to knock out!

specials.name: Grudgebearers
specials.description: Dwarfs hold an ancient grudge against Elves from the days when the two races fought for the supremacy of the Old World. If the Pit Fighters ever hire any kind of Elven Hired Sword, he will leave the Warband immediately, he refuses to fight alongside these pansy Elves!

specials.name: Death Wish
specials.description: Troll Slayers seek an honourable death in combat. They are completely immune to all psychology

specials.name: Evade
specials.description: Pursuers are agile and athletic, well adept at avoiding the heavier Pit Fighters’ charges. When an enemy charges a Pursuer he may choose to try and evade. On a successful Initiative test it is considered a failed charge and the normal rules apply

specials.name: Skills
specials.description: An Ogre Pit Fighter who becomes a Hero as a result of The Lad’s Got Talent may choose from the Combat, Strength and Pit Fighter Special Skills.

specials.name: Slow Witted
specials.description: Although Ogres are capable of earning experience and bettering themselves, they are not the smartest creatures. Ogres only gain advances at half the rate of everyone else (ie, they must accrue twice as much experience as normal to get an advance).

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: Pit Fighters may hire all Hired Swords available except for the Elf Ranger, who feels working with such dirty and brutish individuals would just not do.

rules.title: Pit Fighter
rules.description: All Pit Fighters have the Pit Fighter skill as described in the Strength Skill List except the Pit Fighter Initiates.(Pit Fighter Skill: +1 WS, +1 A when fighting in ruins, buildings and The Pit.)

rules.title: Death of a Leader
rules.description: If the Warrior Priest falls, the Acolyte with the most experience becomes the leader, with every benefit of the Warrior Priest and his title. He gains no prayer at once: at his next advance he may take a prayer from the list instead of rolling, and later advances are as normal. Once promoted he is a Warrior Priest, so the warband may hire another Acolyte.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The warband may hire hired swords as if it were a Witch Hunters warband.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Warrior Priest may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Prayers of Sigmar
specials.description: The Warrior Priest starts with one prayer rolled at random from the Prayers of Sigmar.

specials.name: Zealous
specials.description: The Templar hates every model of a chaotic warband: Skaven, Possessed, Carnival of Chaos, Beastmen, and any warband with a Daemon in it.

specials.name: Instead of a Templar
specials.description: The Huntsman is taken only in place of one of the two Templars.

specials.name: Beastmaster
specials.description: Animals of the warband within 6" of the Huntsman may use his Leadership. A hostile beast must pass a Leadership test to charge him.

fighters.name: Hound
fighters.fixed_kit: None. A Hound never uses weapons or armour and suffers no penalty for it.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Hounds are animals and gain no experience.

specials.name: Devoted
specials.description: A Hound within 12" of the Warrior Priest may re-roll a failed Leadership test.

rules.title: Swabbies
rules.description: The warband's Swabbies are human, and are captured rather than hired, under the Sartosa campaign rules.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The warband hires Hired Swords and buys other items as a human Mercenary warband does. A warband holding both Dwarfs and Elves pays 20 gold crowns more in upkeep.

rules.title: Swivel Guns are Rare, Matey!
rules.description: Unlike other Pirate warbands, the Sartosans may start with a Swivel Gun, bought as normal. In a one-off game they start with two free Swabbies.

rules.title: Succession
rules.description: If the Captain is killed, one of the Mates takes his place, as a Champion does in a Mercenary warband.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any pirate within 6" of the Captain may use his Leadership for any Leadership test.

specials.name: Swivel Guns is Dangerous, Matey!
specials.description: A Gunner carrying the Swivel Gun always counts as an individual and may never be joined by anyone else. Since the warband may hold only one Swivel Gun, the Gunner carrying it is either newly hired or split off from his group, keeping the experience and skills he had.

fighters.name: Boatswain
fighters.fixed_kit: A Rope & Hook, which he may never sell or give away.

specials.name: Expert Riggers
specials.description: A Boatswain may re-roll a failed Initiative test for leaping over a gap, jumping down or making a diving charge, and the test for climbing up or down with a rope.

specials.name: Not Hired
specials.description: Swabbies are not hired: they are captured, under the Sartosa campaign rules.

specials.name: Never Gain Experience
specials.description: Swabbies never gain experience.

specials.name: Rabble
specials.description: Swabbies need not be armed alike: each may carry different equipment, but only from the Swabbie Equipment list. A Swabbie may never use magic or cast a spell.

specials.name: 'Blimey, they got away!'
specials.description: If the warband routs, any Swabbie who has already left the table in an earlier turn escapes for good: remove him from the roster as if he had been killed.

specials.name: 'Don't mind them mates, they ain't true pirates!'
specials.description: Swabbies who are running away or have been taken out of action do not count towards the warband's rout test.

rules.title: Animosity
rules.description:
At the start of your turn roll a D6 for each Henchman who is an Orc or a Goblin, leaving out any model already engaged in close combat. On a 1 he has taken offence: roll another D6 and read the result below.

D6 | Result
1 | If a friendly Orc or Goblin subject to Animosity, or a Hired Sword, is within charge reach he charges the nearest of them and fights one round of close combat. At the end of that round the two models move 1" apart and no longer count as being in close combat, unless one of them rolls this result again. If none is within charge reach and he carries a missile weapon, he instead shoots at the nearest friendly Orc or Goblin subject to Animosity, or the nearest Hired Sword. If neither applies, treat the roll as 2-5. In any case he may take no other action this turn, though he may defend himself in close combat.
2-5 | He spends the turn hurling insults at the nearest friendly Orc or Goblin. He may do nothing else this turn, though he may defend himself in close combat.
6 | He must move as fast as he can towards the nearest enemy model, charging into close combat if he can. With no enemy model in sight he may make a normal move at once. This move is in addition to his move in the Movement phase, so he may move twice in the turn, and if it takes him within charge reach of an enemy model he must charge during his regular movement.

rules.title: Forest Goblins
rules.description: The warband may never hold more Forest Goblins than Orcs.

rules.title: Shops
rules.description: Savage Orcs may visit the Orc Camp and the Orc Black Market.

specials.name: No Shield
specials.description: A Savage Orc Shaman may take magic war paint, but may never take a shield.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of a Black Orc may use his Leadership when taking a Leadership test.

specials.name: Bossy
specials.description: Any Orc or Goblin within 6" of a Black Orc does not roll for Animosity.

specials.name: Animosity
specials.description: A Savage Orc Scarboy is subject to Animosity.

specials.name: Animosity
specials.description: A Savage Orc Scarboy is subject to Animosity.

specials.name: Animosity
specials.description: A Savage Orc Scarboy is subject to Animosity.

specials.name: Animosity (Forest Goblin)
specials.description: A Forest Goblin is subject to Animosity. He will not charge an Orc because of Animosity, but he will still shoot at one.

specials.name: Not Orcs
specials.description: When testing whether the warband must take a Rout test, each Forest Goblin taken out of action counts as half a model.

specials.name: Natives
specials.description: A Forest Goblin suffers no movement penalty in woods.

specials.name: Weedy Grots
specials.description: A Forest Goblin gains experience, but must re-roll any "Lad's Got Talent" result.

rules.title: Animosity
rules.description: Savage Orcs are subject to animosity, as Orcs are.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The warband may hire the Black Orc Bodyguard, and Snerik.

rules.title: Pet
rules.description: One Savage Orc Hero may have a single pet: a War Boar, a Giant Wolf or a Giant Spider. The pet is his own. Only he may ride the War Boar, and nobody rides a Wolf or a Spider, goblins included; he may buy a second War Boar to ride. The pet counts as a piece of equipment, not as a member of the warband, for the share of treasure and for the warband's size, and it runs off at once if the Hero dies. A warband with Giant Wolves may hold no Giant Spiders, and one with Giant Spiders no Giant Wolves.

lists.name: Savage Orc Equipment List
lists.note: Heroes and Henchmen buy from the same list.

lines.note: , Savage Orcs and Gobbo Boyz only
, any Orc warband but no Goblin

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any member of the warband within 6" of the Boss may use his Leadership for a Leadership test.

specials.name: No Armour
specials.description: The Wierdo may wear no armour, but may take anything else from the list.

specials.name: Get out dere!
specials.description:
To send a Spotta ahead, roll a D6 for him at the start of the game, after every model on both sides has been deployed, the Spottaz included. Subtract 1 from the roll if the Boss is within 6" of him.

D6 | Result
1-2 | The Spotta sneaks forward and may be placed anywhere on the table, at least 12" from any enemy model.
3-4 | The Spotta may be moved up to D6+6" from where he stands.
5-6 | The Spotta refuses to leave the others; if the Boss is within 6", he starts the game knocked down.

specials.name: Animosity
specials.description: Brutes are subject to animosity.

specials.name: Animosity
specials.description: Brutes are subject to animosity.

specials.name: No Missiles
specials.description: A Nutta may take anything from the list except a missile weapon.

specials.name: Animosity
specials.description: Brutes are subject to animosity.

specials.name: Animosity
specials.description: Brutes are subject to animosity.

specials.name: Ain't Orcz
specials.description: Each Gobbo Boy taken out of action counts as half a model when working out whether the warband must take a Rout test. A warband of 5 Orcs and 10 Gobbo Boyz, 15 models, tests only once 4 models have fallen: 4 Orcs, 8 Gobbo Boyz, or any mix that comes to 4.

specials.name: Useless Gitz
specials.description: Gobbo Boyz gain no experience.

rules.title: Sundering
rules.description: Every Elf of the warband hates Dark Elves.

rules.title: Excellent Sight
rules.description: Every Elf of the warband spots hidden enemies from twice his Initiative in inches.

rules.title: Distaste for Poison
rules.description: No warrior of the warband may use poison of any kind.

rules.title: Tolerant
rules.description: Unless his rules say otherwise, the warband may hire any hired sword who isn't a Dark Elf, a Skaven or a follower of Chaos, but never an Assassin.

rules.title: Magicians
rules.description: A hired Elf Mage may be kept after each battle for 25 gc upkeep.

rules.title: Unforgiving
rules.description: In multiplayer games the warband may never ally with Dark Elves, followers of Chaos or Skaven.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Wayfinder may take Leadership tests on his Leadership.

specials.name: Navigator
specials.description: Once the Wayfinder captains a vessel of his own he is a Shipmaster, who turns the tide in battles at sea: once a battle, while he is within 6" of the warband's boat, you may re-roll one dice result.

specials.name: Bestial
specials.description: The Feast-Master can never be the warband's leader.

specials.name: Talismanic Tattoos
specials.description: The Feast-Master has a special 6+ save that Strength, spells and magical abilities can't modify.

specials.name: Shadow Dances of Loec
specials.description:
Instead of a new skill, the Feast-Master may learn a Wardancer Dance:

Dance | While he performs it
Whirling Death | +1 to his Injury rolls.
Storm of Blades | +1 Attack.
The Shadows Coil | A special 4+ save that Strength, spells and magic weapons can't modify.
Woven Mist | 1 Attack fewer, but he always strikes first; against a foe who also strikes first, attacks go in Initiative order.

In each round of close combat he fights he must perform one Dance he knows if he can, never the same one in two turns running of the same combat.

specials.name: Seeker
specials.description: When you roll on the Exploration chart, the Lookout lets you change one dice by -1 or +1.

specials.name: Songster
specials.description: Any friendly model within 6" of a Minstrel may re-roll a failed Leadership test, rout tests included, at +1 Leadership.

specials.name: Deathdancer
specials.description: A Minstrel promoted to Hero may learn a Wardancer Dance instead of a new skill (the Feast-Master's Shadow Dances of Loec), and then must dance in close combat as the Feast-Master does.

specials.name: Loner
specials.description: Wildkin are immune to All Alone tests and can never be the warband's leader.

specials.name: Animal Charmer
specials.description: A Wildkin controls up to five animals while they stay within 6" of him. An animal not within 6" of him in the Movement phase moves D6" in a random direction; if that takes it into contact with a model, friend or foe, it attacks as if charging.

name: Shadow Warriors
source: Town Cryer #10, revised in Mordheim Annual 2002

rules.title: Hate Dark Elves
rules.description: All warriors in a Shadow Warrior Warband (excluding any Hired Swords) have an unyielding hatred for Dark Elves.

rules.title: Excellent Sight
rules.description: Elves have eyesight unmatched by mere humans. All the Elves in a Shadow Warrior Warband can spot Hidden enemies from twice as far away as other warriors (i.e. twice their Initiative in inches).

rules.title: Distaste for Poison
rules.description: The use of poisons and various drugs is a Dark Elf specialty. As such, it is frowned upon by Shadow Warriors, even more so than by other High Elves. Warriors in a Shadow Warrior Warband may not use poisons of any type.

rules.title: Unforgiving
rules.description: In addition to their hatred of their corrupt kin, the folk of Nagarythe have a long history of struggle against the forces of Chaos. In multiplayer games, a Shadow Warrior warband may never forge an alliance with any Warband of a Chaotic nature (Possessed, Skaven, Beastmen, Dark Elves, etc.).

rules.title: Tolerant
rules.description: Due to their outsider status with their own people, the Elves of Nagarythe have learned to stifle their distaste for ‘lesser races’, and have even been known to work alongside them from time to time. A Shadow Warrior Warband may hire any Hired Sword that is not of a Chaotic or evil bent (so no Skaven, Possessed, Beastmen, Dark Elves, Undead, etc.). They also shun the company of anyone specialising in the use of poison (so no Assassins).

lists.name: Shadow Warrior equipment lists
lists.note: The following lists are used by Shadow Warrior warbands to pick their weapons:

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Shadow Master may use his Leadership characteristic when taking any Leadership tests.

rules.title: Aquatic Mutants
rules.description: A Hero may start the campaign with one of these mutations, paying its price: Blackblood, Great Claw, Tentacle, Prehensile Tail, Beak, Electrical Touch, Mer-creature, Suckers or Eye Stalks (Hideous).

rules.title: Seafaring
rules.description: Warriors of the warband have +2 Strength when they row a boat.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Buccaneer may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Swashbuckler
specials.description: At the end of any close combat phase in which he is still in base contact with an enemy, the Buccaneer may take a Leadership test. If he passes, he may make a normal move away (not a run or a charge) and the enemy strikes no blows at him; if he fails, he stays in the combat and fights as normal in the next turn.

specials.name: Prayers
specials.description: The Mutant-Priest may use the Prayers of Manann (the Miracle Workers chapter). Instead of a new skill, after an advance roll of a double, he may receive a Mark of Manann.

specials.name: Bite Attack
specials.description: The Mutant-Priest has a bite attack at his own Strength, with no penalty for not using a weapon. It always strikes last, whoever charged and whatever weapon is used, even after double-handed weapons.

specials.name: Blessed Child
specials.description: A Foundling may re-roll any advance roll; the re-roll stands.

specials.name: Mer-creature (Fishmen)
specials.description: Fishmen are aquatic: they can be submerged in water without harm, treat impassable obstacles such as deep rivers, lakes or open sea as difficult terrain, and ignore the penalties for slow-moving rivers and ponds.

specials.name: Swamp Striders
specials.description: Swampers move through swamp and marshland terrain with no penalty.

specials.name: Marsh Born
specials.description: Swampers re-roll failed Initiative tests when crossing marshland or fighting on slippery jetties.

specials.name: Herb Lore
specials.description: At the start of the recovery phase, a Swamper may tend a model in base contact with him, himself included: on a 4+ it regains 1 wound. He may not move in a turn he does this.

rules.title: Assignments
rules.description:
After the game any Hero who was not taken out of action may carry out a client's assignment instead of exploring. He adds no dice to the Exploration chart and may not search for rare items. Roll a D6 instead.

D6 | Result
1 | He fails and misses the next game while he evades his pursuers.
2-5 | He succeeds and gains 2D6 gold crowns and 1 experience point.
6 | He surpasses the client's requirements and gains 3D6 gold crowns and D3 experience points.

rules.title: Sworn Brotherhood
rules.description: To hire a new Hero during a campaign the warband's leader must first pass a Leadership test. If he fails, no new Heroes may be hired after that game. This does not apply when the warband is raised.

rules.title: The silence
rules.description: No warband member or Hired Sword may ever use a blackpowder weapon or an animal.

rules.title: Underground contacts
rules.description: Each Hero may have one underground contact. Instead of searching for rare items he may use his contact, paying the bribe its rules give.

rules.title: Modus Operandi
rules.description: Every Hero may choose one modus operandi when he is hired, and the choice can never be changed. A Hero may hold only one, and must have the weapons, armour and equipment it needs when it is bought; its price covers that basic set, which may be replaced later with no penalty. A Hero with none may take one instead of a skill on an advance. A second Hero may take a modus operandi only once each of them is held by someone, so two Executors need a Sniper and a Lurker first. The Silent Master may not take the sniper. Only a Hero with the sniper may buy the Crossbow or the Long bow from the Brotherhood list.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Silent Master may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Toxic trades
specials.description: If the Poisoner does not search for rare items he may make a single dose of Black Lotus. It must be used in the next battle and may not be sold or traded to another warband.

specials.name: Loudmouths
specials.description: A Thug never becomes a Hero: re-roll every That Lad's Got Talent result.

special.name: Sniper
special.description:
Equipment: a crossbow or long bow, a sword, and a rope and hook.

Sniper: while hidden, he may shoot and stay hidden. If his target is not taken out of action at once, the target tests against its Initiative to spot him; a passed test means he has been spotted and is no longer hidden.

Distant fighter: he gains +1 Ballistic Skill and suffers -1 Weapon Skill, and may not take skills from the Combat list.

special.name: Executor
special.description:
Equipment: an axe and a sword or a double-handed weapon, and light armour.

Crushing attack: he gains +1 Initiative and +1 to hit on the turn he charges. Enemy warriors attacking him in return also gain +1 to hit for that turn.

Close quarters: he may not take skills from the Shooting list.

special.name: Lurker
special.description:
Equipment: a blowpipe or long daggers, and throwing knives.

Stealthed advance: he may hide even after running in the Movement phase.

Lightly armed: he may never use armour.

lists.name: Sisters Of Sigmar Equipment
lists.note: The following lists are used by Sisters of Sigmar warbands to pick their equipment.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warband member within 6" of the Sigmarite Matriarch may use her Leadership characteristic when taking any Leadership tests.

specials.name: Prayers of Sigmar
specials.description: The Sigmarite Matriarch is a servant of Sigmar and may use the Prayers of Sigmar as detailed in the Magic section and the Sigmarite Matriarchs start with one prayer generated at random. In addition the Sigmarite Matriarchs may learn a new Prayer instead of a new skill.

specials.name: No Armour
specials.description: They never wear armour.

specials.name: Blessed Sight
specials.description: An Augur can re-roll any failed characteristic tests (climbing, resisting spells or any other reason), and any rolls to hit in close combat or shooting. You must accept the second result. In addition, an Augur can use her Blessed Sight to help the Sisterhood when they are searching the city for wyrdstone. If the Augur is not put out of action in the battle, you may roll two dice for her in the exploration phase and pick either dice as the result.

lists.name: Skaven Hero Equipment List
lists.note: The following lists are used by the Skaven to pick their equipment.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Assassin Adept may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Magic User
specials.description: The Eshin Sorcerer has the ability to use magic and casts spells like any other magicians, and the Eshin Sorcerer starts with one spells generated at random from the Magic of the Horned Rat. In addition the Eshin Sorcerer may learn a new Spell instead of a new skill.

specials.name: Weapons/Armour
specials.description: None. Giant Rats never use any armour or weapons.

specials.name: Pack Size
specials.description: You can recruit as many Giant Rats as you wish.

specials.name: Experience
specials.description: Giant Rats are animals and do not gain experience.

fighters.name: Rat Ogre
fighters.fixed_kit: Jaws, claws and brute force! Rat Ogres can never use weapons or armour.

specials.name: Stupidity (Rat Ogre)
specials.description: A Rat Ogre is subject to stupidity unless a Skaven Hero is within 6" of it.

specials.name: Experience (Rat Ogre)
specials.description: Rat Ogres do not gain experience.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any model in the warband within 6" of the Claw Leader may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Tactical Genius
specials.description: The Clan Mors player adds +1 to his dice roll to see who sets up first.

specials.name: Experience
specials.description: Skavenslaves gain no experience.

specials.name: All Races
specials.description: A Skavenslave may be of any race, their fellow Skaven included. The profile above is the weakened state of all of them.

specials.name: Slavers
specials.description: A captured enemy warrior may be added to a Skavenslave group. He takes the profile above and must be equipped as the rest of the group is. Anything he carried when he was captured may be kept or sold by the warband.

fighters.name: Rat Ogre
fighters.fixed_kit: None. A Rat Ogre fights with jaws, claws and brute force, and can never use weapons or armour.

specials.name: Stupidity (Rat Ogre)
specials.description: A Rat Ogre is subject to stupidity unless a Skaven Hero is within 6" of it.

specials.name: Experience
specials.description: Skavenslaves gain no experience.

fighters.name: Wolf Rat
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Wolf Rats neither need nor use weapons or armour.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Wolf Rats are animals and gain no experience.

rules.title: Goading
rules.description:
At the very start of the Clan Moulder turn, before any model moves, the Packmaster and each Apprentice may each try to goad one beast model, or one henchman group of beasts (Giant Rats, Wolf Rats or Rat Ogres), of their own warband within 6" of him as the turn begins. A group can be goaded only if at least half its members are within 6".

Roll 2D6 as for casting a spell: the goad works on a score equal to or above the beast's Difficulty, which is 6 for a Giant Rat, 8 for a Wolf Rat and 10 for a Rat Ogre. When it works, roll a D6 on the table below; on a double 6 pick the result instead of rolling.

When it fails, the beast or group must take a Stupidity test at once. If that test is failed with a double 1 the beasts turn on the goader: move them into base contact with him and resolve one attack against him from each beast he targeted. They return to the Moulder player's control at the start of his next turn.

D6 | Result
1-2 | Yelp: the beast or group must run in the Movement phase, at up to triple its Movement instead of double, even if enemy models are within 8" at the start of the move.
3-4 | Growl: if an enemy is in its line of sight the beast or group must charge it (the Moulder player picks among several), at triple its Movement instead of double. The usual charge rules apply, but the charge can't be intercepted.
5-6 | Roar!: until the start of the next Moulder turn the beast or group is subject to frenzy and hates every model of the opposing warband.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Packmaster may take Leadership tests on his Leadership.

specials.name: Master Handler
specials.description: The Packmaster may goad (see Goading). He starts any one-off game or campaign with the Ride Wolf Rat skill and one more Beast Handling skill, for Giant Rats or for Wolf Rats.

specials.name: Poke 'em in the Squidgy Bits
specials.description: When he goads, the Packmaster gets the benefits of both a Beastwhip and a Thingcatcher if he carries both.

specials.name: Novice Handler
specials.description: An Apprentice may goad (see Goading), but in a goad he takes the benefit of a Beastwhip or of a Thingcatcher, not both.

specials.name: Heir to Power
specials.description: If the Packmaster is slain, one of the Apprentices must succeed him as Leader and counts as a Packmaster in every way from then on; a new Apprentice may be hired in his place. If the Packmaster and every Apprentice die at once, or the warband has no Apprentice when the Packmaster dies, the warband disbands.

specials.name: Experience (Rat Ogre)

specials.name: It's Alive!
specials.description: When hired, each Rat Ogre must buy one mutation from the Possessed's list in the rulebook, at its listed price.

specials.name: Hard to Handle
specials.description: Rat Ogres are hired one at a time and never form a henchman group, even when you hire more than one.

specials.name: Spellcaster

specials.name: Stupidity (Rat Ogre)

specials.name: Experience (Rat Ogre)
specials.description: Rat Ogres do not gain experience.

specials.name: Leader

specials.name: Doomed
specials.description: If a Skaven Slave rolls "The lad's got talent", the leader has him executed rather than let him rise: take him off the roster, whether or not the warband holds its full quota of heroes.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Plague Priest may use his Leadership instead of their own.

fighters.name: Plague Rat
fighters.fixed_kit: None. A Plague Rat fights with teeth and claws.

specials.name: Plague Infested
specials.description: Every attack a Plague Rat makes counts as coated with black lotus.

specials.name: Animal

specials.description: Giant rats may raise the warband's numbers to 20 models.

specials.name: Experience
