rules.title: Skryre Special Equipment
rules.description: The warband may hold jezzails, warpfire throwers, warplock pistols and poison wind globes only while it has at least one Warlock Apprentice; with no Apprentice none of that equipment may be included. The Warlock Engineer is the exception: he may always buy it for his own use.

rules.title: Slaves
rules.description: The warband may hold any number of Slaves, up to half the warband.

rules.title: Shops
rules.description: Clan Skryre warbands may visit the Skaven Armoury, the Clan Skryre Armoury and the Warlock's Inner Sanctum.

specials.name: Leader
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Athel Loren)
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Warlock Engineer may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Trainees
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Athel Loren)
specials.description: A Warlock Apprentice begins with no spells. When he rolls a new skill as an experience advance he may take a randomly determined spell instead of a skill.

specials.name: Inexperienced
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Athel Loren)
specials.description: Every spell a Warlock Apprentice casts counts as +1 difficulty.

specials.name: The Lad's Got Talent
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Athel Loren)
specials.description: When an Initiate group rolls "Lad's Got Talent", the promoted Initiate must take spells as one of his two skill lists, and the rules for Warlock Apprentices apply to him from then on.

specials.name: Slave's Kit
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Athel Loren)
specials.description: A Slave may carry a shield, but may never wear a helmet or light armour.

specials.name: Expected to Die
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Athel Loren)
specials.description: When testing whether the warband must take a Rout test, each Slave taken out of action counts as half a model.

specials.name: Doomed
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Athel Loren)
specials.description: A Slave who rolls "Lad's Got Talent" is removed from the roster, whether or not the warband holds its full number of Heroes, and you roll for an advance again if his group has other members.

specials.name: Leader
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Karak Azgal)
specials.description: Any model in the warband within 6" of the Master Engineer may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Master Engineer
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Karak Azgal)
specials.description: The Master Engineer may re-roll any fumble with a blackpowder or wyrdstone-powered weapon he carries. The second result stands.

specials.name: Experience
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Karak Azgal)
specials.description: Skavenslaves gain no experience.

specials.name: All Races
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Karak Azgal)
specials.description: A Skavenslave may be of any race, their fellow Skaven included. The profile above is the weakened state of all of them.

specials.name: Slavers
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Karak Azgal)
specials.description: A captured enemy warrior may be added to a Skavenslave group. He takes the profile above and must be equipped as the rest of the group is. Anything he carried when he was captured may be kept or sold by the warband.

name: Skaven of Clan Skryre (Relics of the Crusades)

specials.name: Leader
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Relics of the Crusades)
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Warlock Engineer may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Slave Driver
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Relics of the Crusades)
specials.description: Skaven Slaves within 3" of the Skaven Overseer may use his Leadership. If he carries a scourge, the range is 6".

specials.name: Slave Master
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Relics of the Crusades)
specials.description: Skaven Slaves ignore the Easy come, easy go rule in a battle the Skaven Overseer was not taken out of action in.

fighters.name: Skaven Slave
fighters.fixed_kit: A single dagger, and no other equipment.

specials.name: Life is cheap
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Relics of the Crusades)
specials.description: A member of the warband may shoot into a close combat that holds only enemies and Skaven Slaves. Randomise the hits.

specials.name: Easy come, easy go
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Relics of the Crusades)
specials.description: After rolling for injuries, roll a D3 and remove that many Skaven Slaves from the warband.

specials.name: Numerous
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Relics of the Crusades)
specials.description: Skaven Slaves may take the warband up to 20 models: with 15 other Skaven on the roster, up to 5 Skaven Slaves may be added.

specials.name: Worthless
specials.type: Warband - Skaven of Clan Skryre (Relics of the Crusades)
specials.description: A Skaven Slave taken out of action counts as half a model towards the warband's rout test. A warband of 5 Skaven and 10 Skaven Slaves tests when 4 models have fallen: 4 Skaven, 8 Skaven Slaves, or any mix worth 4.

fighters.name: Giant Rat
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Giant Rats never carry weapons or armour.

rules.title: Slave trade
rules.description: The warband counts as gaining one extra piece of treasure after every battle, for the slaves it sells who do not fight.

rules.title: Lad's got the talent
rules.description: When a slave gains the Lad's Got the Talent advance, he takes a Leadership test. Passed, he is freed: he keeps his profile, becomes a Caravan Guard, may become the warband's leader, and loses every special rule of being a slave. Failed, he is taken off the warband list and becomes a new Eunuch in a henchmen group of his own. Roll advances for any slave left in the group as normal.

rules.title: Room for slaves
rules.description: The warband may hold 20 warriors while hiring its heroes and henchmen gives at most 12, so the rest are slaves it buys.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Slave Merchant may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Slave Driver
specials.description: A slave within 3" of the Overseer may use his Leadership. If he carries a scourge, the range is 6".

specials.name: Broken Spirit
specials.description: A Eunuch automatically passes any Leadership test he has to take while the Slave Merchant is not out of action. A Eunuch may never become the warband's leader.

specials.name: Slow Witted
specials.description: An Ogre gains advances at half the rate of everyone else.

fighters.name: Hound
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Hounds never carry weapons or armour.

specials.name: Keen Scent
specials.description: While the warband holds a Hound, its slaves ignore the I'm outta here rule.

rules.title: Hard to Kill
rules.description: A Dwarf is taken out of action only on a 6 on the Injury chart: 1-2 is knocked down, 3-5 stunned, 6 out of action.

rules.title: Hard Head
rules.description: A Dwarf ignores the special rules for maces, clubs and the like.

rules.title: Grudgebearers
rules.description: The warband may never include an Elven Hired Sword or Dramatis Persona of any kind.

rules.title: See You in Davie Jones!
rules.description: If the warband routs voluntarily, it receives half the exploration dice, rounding up.

rules.title: Deathwish
rules.description: Unless a rule says otherwise, every member of the warband is immune to all psychology, frenzy and stupidity included, and never tests for fighting alone.

rules.title: Not just any ol' Toy!
rules.description: A Slayer may never use armour of any kind, and may use no magic except magic weapons.

rules.title: Up Close
rules.description: A Slayer may use only thrown missile weapons and pistols of any kind. Only the Gunners and the Master Gunner may learn Shooting skills, and only they may use thrown weapons and gunpowder weapons; they may use no other missile weapon.

rules.title: Swabbies
rules.description: The warband captures Swabbies, under the Sartosa campaign rules. A willing captive joins the Landlubbers; an unwilling one becomes a Thaggi.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Slayer Captain may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Expert Weaponsmith
specials.description: Every Pistol in the warband, of any kind, has its range increased by 3", and every Blunderbuss, of any kind, by 6". The increase holds only while the Master Gunner is in the warband, and only in a battle he was deployed in.

specials.name: Skittish
specials.description: Gunners do not have the Death Wish skill and suffer psychology as normal. When a Gunner gains That Lad's Got Talent, he must learn Death Wish instead of rolling on the Hero advance table, even if Special is not one of his two skill lists.

specials.name: Skittish
specials.description: Gunners do not have the Death Wish skill and suffer psychology as normal. When a Gunner gains That Lad's Got Talent, he must learn Death Wish instead of rolling on the Hero advance table, even if Special is not one of his two skill lists.

specials.name: Not Hired
specials.description: Thaggi are not hired: they are given to the warband, under the Sartosa campaign rules.

specials.name: Never Gain Experience
specials.description: Thaggi never gain experience.

specials.name: Rabble
specials.description: Thaggi need not be armed alike: each may carry different equipment, but only from the Thaggi Equipment list. A Thaggi may never use magic or cast a spell.

specials.name: 'Kruk, they got away!'
specials.description: If the warband routs, any Thaggi who has already left the table in an earlier turn escapes for good: remove him from the roster as if he had been killed.

specials.name: 'Don't mind them mates, they ain't true dwarves!'
specials.description: Thaggi who are running away or have been taken out of action do not count towards the warband's rout test.

name: Snotlings
source: Luke ‘Ram Rock Ed First/Auretious Taak’ Roberts and Dave ‘Styrofoamking’ Seidman-Joria

rules.title: Dodgy
rules.description: Every Snotling has a 6+ save against hits, as the Fey Quickness skill gives. A Hero who gains Dodge or Step Aside combines it into a 4+ dodge or step aside save.

rules.title: Small Target
rules.description: Ranged attacks are at -1 to hit a Snotling.

rules.title: Small Hands
rules.description: Snotlings and the Bullied Goblin may never use long bows, elf bows, handguns, long rifles or blunderbusses, even when an advance would allow it. Shoota Teams are the exception.

rules.title: Not-So-Tough Gits
rules.description: A Snotling's injury roll is knocked down on a 1, stunned on a 2-3 and out of action on a 4-6. A Snotling henchman taken out of action dies on a 1-3 instead of 1-2, and a Snotling Hero (not the Bullied Goblin) rolls twice on the Heroes Serious Injury table.

rules.title: Weakness in Numbers
rules.description: The warband's rating is halved, rounding up (117 becomes 59). For income and trading the warband counts as half its size, rounding up, from 3 to 15.

rules.title: Scavengers!
rules.description: The warband rolls one extra exploration die, even when all its Heroes were taken out of action.

rules.title: That (Git)'s Got Talent!
rules.description: A Snotling henchman who gains That Lad's Got Talent learns Mob Rule and The Rigors of Leadership.

rules.title: Too Unruly
rules.description: The warband may hire no hired swords or dramatis personae but Snotling ones and those that name the warband.

rules.title: Promoted Henchmen
rules.description: A promoted henchman may never choose Strength or Academic skills.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Bullied Goblin may use his Leadership when taking Leadership tests.

specials.name: Not A Snotling
specials.description: The Bullied Goblin isn't a Snotling: Dodgy, Small Target and Not-So-Tough Gits don't apply to him. His rating is still halved (Weakness in Numbers), and he may still use a Pebble.

specials.name: Mob Rule
specials.description: The Hero gains +1 Leadership for every 2 Snotlings within 6" of him, to 10 at most. The bonus counts for the Leader rule.

specials.name: The Rigors of Leadership
specials.description: The Hero gains +2 experience for surviving a battle.

specials.name: Mob Rule
specials.description: The Hero gains +1 Leadership for every 2 Snotlings within 6" of him, to 10 at most. The bonus counts for the Leader rule.

specials.name: The Rigors of Leadership
specials.description: The Hero gains +2 experience for surviving a battle.

specials.name: Mob Rule
specials.description: The Hero gains +1 Leadership for every 2 Snotlings within 6" of him, to 10 at most. The bonus counts for the Leader rule.

specials.name: The Rigors of Leadership
specials.description: The Hero gains +2 experience for surviving a battle.

specials.name: Scout
specials.description: The Snotling Scout is set up after the opposing warband, anywhere on the table out of its sight and more than 8" from every enemy model. If both sides have infiltrators, each rolls a D6 and the lowest sets up first.

specials.name: He's No Threat!
specials.description: A Snotling Scout may always run, even with enemies within 8" at the start of the turn.

specials.name: Mob Rule
specials.description: The Hero gains +1 Leadership for every 2 Snotlings within 6" of him, to 10 at most. The bonus counts for the Leader rule.

specials.name: The Rigors of Leadership
specials.description: The Hero gains +2 experience for surviving a battle.

specials.name: 'Eadache!
specials.description: Each time the Shaman tries to cast a spell, whether it works or not, roll a D6: on a 1-2 he and every model in base contact with him take a S5 magical hit. With a familiar not yet used this turn he may re-roll it, keeping the second result. No roll when he only rolls to keep a spell going.

specials.name: One Big Gun
specials.description: A Shoota Team may buy only one missile weapon other than pebbles and slingshots (not a crossbow and a blunderbuss). No more than 2 Shoota Teams may have blunderbusses, and a pistol is never bought as a brace.

specials.name: Teamwork
specials.description: A Shoota Team is two or more Snotlings but counts as one model.

specials.name: Cumbersome
specials.description: A Shoota Team with a missile weapon other than a pebble or slingshot can never run, only charge.

specials.name: Recoil
specials.description: When a Shoota Team fires a missile weapon other than a pebble or slingshot, it is knocked back D6" at once. Hitting solid terrain, it takes a S2 hit; hitting another model, both take a S2 hit. Firing a pistol in combat, it moves the D6" directly away from its opponent and leaves the combat, with no free attack against it. Knocked off a building's top, it tests for falling as normal.

specials.name: Teamwork (Snotling Mob)
specials.description: A Snotling Mob is many Snotlings but counts as one model.

specials.name: Not So Small, Surprisingly Tough
specials.description: Small Target and Not-So-Tough Gits don't apply to a Snotling Mob: shooting at it has no -1 to hit, it rolls for injury on the normal table, and it dies only on a 1-2. It keeps Dodgy.

specials.name: Mass Stupidity
specials.description: A Snotling Mob can never gain That Lad's Got Talent: re-roll it until another advance comes up.

specials.name: Mob Mentality
specials.description: When a Snotling Mob starts a turn within 2" of another Snotling Mob, both are Immune to Psychology for the rest of that turn, an opponent's turn included.

fighters.name: Snotling Wheelo
fighters.fixed_kit: The crew have a dagger and 1 pebble. A 40mm base.

specials.name: Movement
specials.description: Walking, the Wheelo moves D6", rolled each turn, only straight forwards or backwards; it may pivot up to 90° on the spot at the start of the turn, before rolling. It stops when it hits any terrain but open ground or a building's wall (it may climb, at random: half way up a wall, it falls as normal). Running or charging, it moves 2D6" instead, and a charge that falls short isn't halved. Moving into a model, it deals Impact Hits; into an enemy, that counts as a charge. Each time a running or charging Wheelo enters a different piece of terrain other than open ground (rubble, barricades, houses), it takes a S5 hit at once; if it survives it may finish its move.

specials.name: Impact Hits
specials.description: A model the Wheelo moves into takes D3 S4 hits, before any blows, as a crossbow pistol's shot is worked out; only in the first round of combat and only in a turn the Wheelo charged. A model that charges the Wheelo takes none. A friendly model it rolls into takes them too. They stay S4 whatever the crew's Strength. Charging two models, each takes D3-1 hits (1 at least, one roll for both); charging three or more, each takes 1.

specials.name: Combat
specials.description: The profile is the crew's, and they fight in each hand-to-hand combat phase, charged or charging (charged, without Impact Hits). They never attack a friendly model the Wheelo rolls into. Rolling into an enemy that causes fear, the Wheelo still charges and deals Impact Hits, but the crew must pass a Leadership test or hit only on 6s.

specials.name: Tough Machine
specials.description: Not-So-Tough Gits, Small Target and Dodgy don't apply to the Wheelo. Taken out of action, it rolls a D6 instead of the Injury table: 1, destroyed and struck off the roster; 2, misses the next D3 games; 3-6, fights the next battle as normal.

specials.name: Upgrades
specials.description: The Wheelo is a henchman but rolls its advances on the Heroes' Advance table, as a hired sword does. It never gains That Lad's Got Talent, may raise each characteristic only once, and ignores the Snotling maximums. A Skill advance is from the Combat, Strength or Speed lists.

specials.name: Special Skill Modifications
specials.description: Weapons Training fits one weapon to the Wheelo: an axe gives its Impact Hits -1 to the armour save; a club gives them Concussion; a spear deals one Impact Hit to a model that charges it, before attacks; a morning star makes its first round of Impact Hits each game S5. Sprint lets it run or charge 3D6" instead of 2D6". Mighty Blow gives the crew +1 to wound in combat, not its Impact Hits.

specials.name: Teeny Hands
specials.description: Runts use missile weapons as normal, but only one one-handed weapon at a time (a second gives no extra attack), and no armour of any kind. A Runt who gains That Lad's Got Talent loses Teeny Hands.

specials.name: Smallest of the Small
specials.description: Missile attacks are at a further -1 to hit a Runt (-2 in all); in combat he is hit as normal. A Runt taken out of action dies on an injury roll of 1-4 instead of 1-3.

specials.name: Experience
specials.description: Runts gain experience as normal. An enemy Hero or henchman group that takes a Runt out of action rolls a D6 after the battle, and gains 1 experience only on a 5+.

specials.name: Swarm Size
specials.description: A group of Runts may hold any number of them.

rules.title: Keep it secret, keep it safe!
rules.description: The warband may never hire a hired sword or dramatis persona with the Wizard ability, except the High Elf Mage. Otherwise it hires hired swords as a Human Mercenary warband does.

rules.title: The Vagaries of Magic
rules.description:
When a wizard of the warband rolls a natural 2 (two 1s) to cast a spell, roll 2D6 on the Magical Failure table:

2D6 | Result
2 | Aaarrgh!: he mutates into a Spawn of Chaos. Remove him from the roster.
3 | Gglbddlh: he is stupid. After the battle roll a D6: on a 2+ it ends.
4 | Magical Shutdown: he can cast no spells for the rest of the battle.
5-6 | Uh-oh!: the spell is cast on the wizard himself. Any choice it needs (Flight of Zimmeran's, say) is made by the player to his player's left.
7 | Pooh, nothing at all!: the spell fails, with no other effect.
8-9 | Magical Explosion: he is thrown D6" in a random direction and lands knocked down.
10-11 | Magical Jam: he can't cast a spell in his next shooting phase; he may use missile weapons as normal.
12 | Wait, what's that?: he mutates, then the change ends. Choose a free mutation for him from the Possessed's mutations (Rulebook p76).

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Magus may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Don't look at me!
specials.description: A Companion may never become the leader, and no other model may use his Leadership for a test, including Rout tests once the leader is out of action.

specials.name: Body Guard
specials.description: While a Companion is within 2" of a wizard and not in hand-to-hand combat, he takes all missile fire aimed at the wizard and intercepts any charge at him. He moves at once to do it, even out of sequence or further than he could normally move in a turn, but only along a path he could take (not from another floor of a building).

specials.name: Respect your betters
specials.description: A Mage may never have more spells than the leader. If he does, he at once fights the leader in a Wizard's Duel, another player playing the leader, and the loser leaves the warband.

specials.name: Here, hold this
specials.description: Untrained may carry special items, such as holy relics or lucky charms.

specials.name: Harnessed
specials.description: An Untrained who rolls The Lad's Got Talent at once gains the Wizard skill. He may give up his extra advance to roll a spell at random, or roll for it as a Hero's advance.

specials.name: Prove that Talent!
specials.description: A Grunt who rolls The Lad's Got Talent may become a mundane Hero, or an Untrained instead. So a Grunt who rolls it twice may become a wizard.

rules.title: Dead Leader
rules.description: If the Vampire is killed he cannot be replaced for that battle: every undead creature of the warband crumbles and is lost with its equipment. Pick a new leader from among the Heroes as the rulebook says. After one game a new Vampire may be bought, who becomes the leader, and the acting leader returns to his former place.

rules.title: Bats or Fell Bats
rules.description: The warband may hold up to 5 Bats or up to 2 Fell Bats, never both kinds at once.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: Besides any who name the warband themselves, the warband may hire the Strigani Seer, and a Necromancer only while it has no Vampire.

rules.title: Strigoi Vampire Abilities
rules.description: The Vampire may take an ability in place of his search for rare equipment. The prices below are for his first; the second and every later one cost double. Each ability may be taken only once unless it says otherwise.

fighters.name: Vampire
fighters.fixed_kit: None. A Strigoi Vampire uses no weapons or equipment.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any model in the warband within 6" of the Vampire may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Bestial
specials.description: The Vampire has a 6+ ward save against every attack.

fighters.name: Charnel Guard
fighters.fixed_kit: None, apart from the few bones a Charnel Guard uses as a primitive weapon.

specials.name: Cunning
specials.description: Unlike an ordinary Ghoul, a Charnel Guard may learn the Weapons Training or Weapons Expert skill and use any weapon.

specials.name: Living
specials.description: The Strigany are living humans, and none of the Undead rules apply to them.

fighters.name: Ghoul
fighters.fixed_kit: None, apart from the few bones a Ghoul uses as a primitive weapon.

specials.name: No Brain
specials.description: Skeletons gain no experience.

specials.name: Hand-to-hand only
specials.description: A Skeleton may take hand-to-hand weapons and armour from the list, but no missile weapon.

fighters.name: Bat
fighters.fixed_kit: None.

specials.name: Living (Bat)
specials.description: Bats are living beings, and none of the Undead rules apply to them.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Bats are animals and gain no experience.

specials.name: Flyers
specials.description: A Bat ignores terrain when it moves and may charge any model it can see, whatever its height and whoever would intercept.

specials.name: Squishy
specials.description: A wounded Bat uses this Injury chart: 1-2 knocked down, 3 stunned, 4-6 out of action.

fighters.name: Fell Bat
fighters.fixed_kit: None.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Bats are animals and gain no experience.

specials.name: Flyers
specials.description: A Bat ignores terrain when it moves and may charge any model it can see, whatever its height and whoever would intercept.

special.name: Curse Of The Undead
special.description: If the Vampire goes out of action, after the battle he heals all of his wounds on a D6 roll of 5+, and then does not roll on the serious injury table.

special.name: Infinite Hatred
special.description: The Vampire may re-roll his failed to-hit rolls in the first turn of each combat. Each dice may be re-rolled only once.

special.name: Quick Blood
special.description: The Vampire's ward save improves to 5+.

special.name: Blood Lust
special.description: The Vampire is subject to frenzy.

special.name: Master Strike
special.description: The Vampire causes a critical hit on a 5 or 6.

special.name: Dark Acolyte
special.description: The Vampire gains +1 on his difficulty roll to cast a spell.

special.name: Bat Wings
special.description: The Vampire may fly up to 12" in the movement phase, ignoring terrain and climbing.

special.name: Revulsion
special.description: Anyone taking a fear test because of the Vampire does so at -1 Leadership.

special.name: Infected Wound
special.description: The Vampire's attacks are poisoned, with the effect of Black Lotus. It may not be combined with Corpse Liquor.

special.name: Blood Kiss
special.description: The Vampire may steal a wound from an enemy he stuns or takes out of action in combat. This may take him above his starting Wounds, and lasts only for that battle.

special.name: Iron Sinews
special.description: The Vampire gains +1 Strength, which may take him beyond his racial maximum.

special.name: Hunter
special.description: The Vampire may spot hidden models at up to twice his Initiative in inches.

rules.title: The Only Undead
rules.description: The warband doesn't disband if the Strigoi Vampire dies, as he is its only Undead model. It hires hired swords as an Undead warband does.

fighters.name: Strigoi Vampire
fighters.fixed_kit: None. The Strigoi Vampire fights with tooth and claw and suffers no penalty for being unarmed.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Strigoi Vampire may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Kindred Hatred (Strigoi Vampire)
specials.description: The Strigoi Vampire hates vampires of every other bloodline.

specials.name: Seeker
specials.description: A Seer who fought in the battle and wasn't taken out of action may change one exploration die by +1 or -1.

specials.name: Child of Darkness
specials.description: Domnu are immune to Sylvania's Spooky special rule.

specials.name: Gypsy Ward
specials.description: A Domnu has a special 5+ save against magical attacks.

fighters.name: Ghoul
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Ghouls carry only a few bones as crude weapons.

fighters.name: Giant Bat
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Giant Bats fight with their jaws.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Giant Bats are animals and gain no experience.

specials.name: Flying
specials.description: Giant Bats fly: they never climb or leap gaps, even when their move ends over open air.

specials.name: Sonic
specials.description: A Giant Bat needs no line of sight to charge.

rules.title: Slow witted
rules.description: A Brood member gains half the experience another model would gain.

rules.title: Always hungry
rules.description: Each Hero counts as two models when the warband sells moonstones.

rules.title: Brood Mentality
rules.description: Every Brood member is subject to stupidity. When one takes a Stupidity test he adds 1 to his Leadership for each warband member within 6". The warband never hires Hired Swords. A Baneworm neither gains nor suffers from this rule.

rules.title: Hoard
rules.description: The warband never sells a rare item, even one no Brood member can use, but it may trade stored items for captured brood members. It suffers -2 on every rarity roll.

rules.title: Regenerate
rules.description: When a Brood member rolls for serious injuries after being taken out of action, treat any result of 16-35 as a full recovery. A Henchman taken out of action during a game survives on a 2+. A Brood member whose last wound was caused by fire does not regenerate after the game. A Baneworm neither gains nor suffers from this rule.

rules.title: Aquatic
rules.description: A Brood member may move through water terrain with no penalty and counts as being in cover while he is in the water.

rules.title: Accelerated evolution
rules.description:
Each time a Brood Hero rolls for an advance he may also consume any number of moonstones, roll a D6 and add the number of moonstones spent to the result.

D6 | Result
1-4 | Nothing happens.
5-6 | He may choose a single lesser Mutation.
7-8 | He may choose a single lesser or greater Mutation.
9+ | He may choose any single Mutation.

Lesser Mutations: Blackblood, Daemon Soul, Mer-creature, Suckers, Tentacle. Greater Mutations: Great Claw, Leech maw, Poisonous fangs, Spines, Spit venom. Sublime Mutations: Acidic stream, Extra Arm, Regeneration, Scaly skin, Shark bite.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Broodmother may use her Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Nestlings
specials.description: If a Newborn is taken out of action by an enemy warrior in close combat, every Brood Hero who can see him hates that model until the end of the game. A Hero must always try to intercept a charge at a Newborn.

specials.name: Too little
specials.description: A Newborn never becomes a Hero: re-roll every That Lad's Got Talent result.

fighters.name: Baneworm
fighters.fixed_kit: A maw and mandibles. A Baneworm never uses weapons or armour.

specials.name: Lurker
specials.description: A Baneworm that was hidden in the previous turn may make a diving charge even when he does not charge from above.

specials.name: Animal
specials.description: A Baneworm gains no experience and may not climb.

rules.title: Foolish Nobleness
rules.description: Even if all non-animal member of the warband are Human, the distorted and perverted power of the dark gods bent the morale and psyche of these men beyond any imaginable level, even for the most tolerant of mercenary. For this reason, the Cursed Cavalcade is treated as an Evil warband, and, similarly to the Cult of the Possessed, for all game effects purpose (such as, for example, for the effect 333 - Prisoners, on the exploration chart). They cannot hire any Hired Sword or Dramatis Personae, other than the Crow Master and anyone that specifically says otherwise.

rules.title: Capture!
rules.description: If a Hero takes Out of Action an enemy human Henchmen model with a Misericordia, and you have less than 5 Captured Thrall in you warband, roll a die: on a 5+ the model is captured. Enemy Heroes can only be Captured as a result of a roll of “61 - Captured!” on the Serious Injuries Table. It’s not possible to Capture more than 2 model per game. If you already captured 2 henchmen, or already have 5 Captured Thrall in your warband, reroll any result of “61- Captured!” for the heroes.

rules.title: The Throne of Worms
rules.description:
The most horrible end for an enemy of the Cavalcade is not death but capture! Captured models are brought down to the Throne of Worms and abandoned to the judgment of this abomination. Only a few survive this madness but they emerge lost forever!

For each enemy captured, instead of rolling on the Serious Injury Table after the battle, roll 1d6:

1-2 The warrior is swallowed up forever by the Throne of Worms. Remove the warrior from the original warband’s roster.
3-5 The warrior completely loses his mind and is submitted to the power of the Throne. Remove the warrior from the original warband’s roster and You gain a Captured Thrall for your warband.
6 The warrior is sacrificed with a ritual to the Throne. Remove the warrior from the original warband’s roster and a random Hero in your warband gains 1 XP.

Note: this replaces the Captured! standard rules on the Serious Injuries Table for Heroes.

lists.name: Thralls Equipment List
lists.note: This list is for Thralls only.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior of the Cavalcade Warband within 6" of the Aristocrat may use his Leadership value when taking Leadership tests.

specials.name: Magical Adept
specials.description: When hiring a Twisted Scholar, you may pay 10 additional GC to upgrade it to a Wizard. If you do this then the twisted scholar uses Lesser Magic and knows 1 spell chosen randomly.

specials.name: Story Teller
specials.description: When hiring a Twisted Scholar, if you did not upgrade it to a Wizard, you may pay 10 additional GC to make it a Chronicler. A Chronicler has in-depth knowledge of the city of Mordheim and may reroll an extra dice during Exploration phase and may decide which of the two dice to keep.

specials.name: Danse Macabre
specials.description:
The Piper plays the Danse Macabre in combat. During the shooting phase the Cursed Piper can direct the cursed melody of is flute against one enemy model he can see within 6” from the Piper. The enemy model must take a Ld test.

If failed, the warrior is cursed by the Danse Macabre loses control of his body and forced to dance under the Piper’s will. The Piper can move the enemy model in any direction he wishes also out of close combat or force him to fall from height.

At the beginning of the enemy’s turn, in the recovery phase the warrior will have to pass a Ld test or will continue to be under the Pipers’ control and cannot shoot, charge or cast spells. If engaged in close combat the model cannot attack (it is too busy dancing!).

Only one enemy warrior at time can be controlled by the Danse Macabre. If the Piper targets another warrior the previous one is immediately free from the curse.

specials.name: Extra servitors, worthless, but still precious
specials.description: Captured Thralls do not count toward the maximum number of models allowed in your warband, effectively increasing the maximum capacity from 13 to 18. You cannot dismiss any Captured Thrall you own.

specials.name: Not really clever
specials.description: Captured Thralls cannot earn experience points, and therefore cannot gain any advancement.

specials.name: Maddened With Pain
specials.description: As soon as the Great Bear suffers a single wound it gains an additional attack.

specials.name: Animal
specials.description: Great Bears are animals and thus do not gain experience.

specials.name: Charge
specials.description: When charging their enemies the Wild Beasts gain +1 Attack on the first turn of close combat.

specials.name: Animal
specials.description: Great Bears are animals and thus do not gain experience.

specials.name: Cymbals
specials.description: when hiring a Fighting Ape, you may give her a pair of cymbals at 15 gc, which it frenziedly beats together to the forbidding tune of Danse Macabre. Any enemy model within 6" will be so disturbed by the sound that they suffer a penalty of -1 to BS and Ld.

specials.name: Agile (Fighting Ape)
specials.description: The Fighting Apes are fantastically agile and nimble, putting even the greatest acrobat or Skaven Assassin to shame. The Fighting Ape has the Scale Sheer Surfaces Skill, Acrobat Skill, and Dodge Skill. In addition, the Fighting Ape can make a diving charge from up to 10" high.

specials.name: Animal (Fighting Ape)
specials.description: Fighitng Apes are animals and thus do not gain experience, but can still climb and enter buildings as normal.

rules.title: Eaters of Flesh
rules.description: Make a note of any enemy model taken out of action by a warrior who has the Eaters of Flesh rule. A hero deducts 1 from his serious injury roll. A henchman is removed from his warband on a D6 of 1-3 instead of 1-2.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any friendly warrior within 6" of the Revenant may use his Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Eaters of Flesh
specials.description: When the Revenant takes a living enemy out of action and is in base contact with no enemy model, he takes a Leadership test. Failed, he starts eating the body and may do nothing for D3 turns. He takes his turns as normal once those turns are up, or as soon as he is hit by an attack.

specials.name: Eaters of Flesh
specials.description: When the Revenant takes a living enemy out of action and is in base contact with no enemy model, he takes a Leadership test. Failed, he starts eating the body and may do nothing for D3 turns. He takes his turns as normal once those turns are up, or as soon as he is hit by an attack.

fighters.name: Ghoul
fighters.fixed_kit: None while he is a henchman. A Ghoul promoted to a hero picks weapons and armour from the Fallen Equipment list.

fighters.name: Sgull
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Sgulls never carry weapons or armour.

specials.name: Flyers
specials.description: A Sgull ignores all terrain and may move at any angle.

fighters.name: Wild Dog
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Wild Dogs never carry weapons or armour.

rules.title: They're Just Kids
rules.description: No member of the warband may be Fearsome; roll again if Fearsome comes up. The Innocents are not evil and may ally with no evil warband, hired sword or dramatis persona, Chaos, Skaven and Undead among them.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Siblings may use their Leadership instead of his own.

specials.name: Close Knit
specials.description: The Siblings share one base and count as a single model. Their +1 Wound and +1 Attack for it are already in the profile.

specials.name: Irreplaceable
specials.description: The Siblings may only be recruited when the warband is created.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: A Stray Dog gains no experience and uses no equipment.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: A Stray Dog gains no experience and uses no equipment.

rules.title: Leaders
rules.description: The warband has no standing leader. At the start of each battle the hero with the highest Leadership takes the role and has the Leader skill for that battle; where no hero clearly has it, the hero with the most experience leads.

rules.title: Traps
rules.description: Write down which buildings are rigged: one building for each hero or henchmen group with the Trap Master skill. The first model to enter a rigged building must pass an Initiative test or take one Strength 3 hit.

specials.name: Mob Mentality
specials.description: For every other member of the warband within 3", the Baron gains +1 Leadership, to a maximum of +3.

specials.name: Advisor
specials.description: One hero within 6" of the Elder may re-roll one dice each turn.

specials.name: Trap Masters
specials.description: Greycoats may set traps, as the warband's Traps rule describes.

specials.name: Brutes
specials.description: Mummers may never rise to power: re-roll any Lad's Got Talent result they roll for experience.

lists.name: Restless Dead Equipment List
lists.note: The following lists are used by Restless Dead warbands to pick their equipment.

specials.name: Eternal
specials.description: A Liche can choose to ignore any result on the hero's Serious Injury chart except Killed by taking a permanent -1 on their starting Wound profile. Obviously, a Liche with 1 Wound remaining on their starting profile does not have this option. A Liche that gets a Killed result instead takes a permanent –D3 Wounds on their starting profile. If this takes their starting Wound total to 0 or less, the Liche is Killed as normal.

specials.name: Feed Upon Magic
specials.description: A Liche can perform spells that, with the consumption of D3 Treasures, can give the Liche a permanent +1 Wound on their starting profile. This can only be used in between battles and cannot be used if the Liche searches for rare items or was put out of action in the previous battle. If the warband does not have enough Treasures to complete the spell, then the Treasures are consumed anyway and the Liche does not gain the Wound.

specials.name: Warrior Wizard
specials.description: The Liche may wear armour and cast spells. Indeed, it is often the clothing and armour alone that gives the Liche substance and form!

specials.name: Advancement
specials.description: If a Liche gets an advance roll of +1 Wound, they may instead pick a new skill from their available lists.

specials.name: Apprentices
specials.description: Necromancers may only ever know spells known by their Liche masters. Even if they did know spells the Liche didn’t, they wouldn’t dare use them for fear of their master’s response for their arrogance! If the Liche is ever killed, the Necromancer can continue to learn magic spells as a normal wizard, ignoring the Apprentice rule.

specials.name: Gofer
specials.description: As an Apprentice, the Necromancer spends much of their time running errands for their Liche masters and over the years get exceptionally good at it. When a Necromancer searches for rare items, they roll 3D6 and pick the two highest.

specials.name: Wight Blades
specials.description: Grave Guards carry weapons laden with evil magic. All close combat ‘to hit’ rolls of a 6 will automatically wound. You may roll ‘to wound’ as normal to determine if it is a ‘critical hit’, but even a failed ‘to wound’ roll will still cause a wound if a 6 was rolled first ‘to hit’.

specials.name: No deal
specials.description: Grave Guards may not search for rare items.

fighters.name: Zombie
fighters.fixed_kit: Zombies may not carry any weapons or wear armour and do not suffer any penalties for this.

specials.name: No Brain
specials.description: Zombies never gain experience.

specials.name: No Brain
specials.description: Zombies never gain experience.

specials.name: Experience
specials.description: Wights may gain experience, however Wights promoted to become Heroes by rolling The lad's got talent will be unable to search for rare items in the same way as Grave Guards. They must choose the Combat and Strength skill lists if promoted. Wights also gain Wight Blades if they become Heroes.

fighters.name: Scarecrow
fighters.fixed_kit: The scarecrow carries no equipment and suffers no penalties for this.

specials.name: No Brain
specials.description: Zombies never gain experience.

specials.name: No Substance
specials.description: The scarecrow is incredibly difficult to take down with shooting as there are few vital parts to hit. The scarecrow counts as having a T6 against all shooting and magical missiles, likewise, a scarecrow is immune to critical hits caused by shooting. The exception to this rule is missile weapons or spells that are fire based which deal damage as normal.

specials.name: Flammable
specials.description: The scarecrow is primarily ratty cloth, straw and preserved body parts so as a result they burn very easily. Scarecrows count as being flammable. In addition, a scarecrow will be 'caught fire' on the roll of a 3+ as opposed to the normal 4+.

specials.name: Construct
specials.description: The scarecrow is an undead construct and may re-roll any rolls on the injury table except for wounds caused by fire.

specials.name: Animated Construct
specials.description:
Powerful constructs such as scarecrows require much more concentration from their summoners than normal skeletons or zombies to remain animated. The scarecrow is controlled by either the Liche or the Necromancer (note down on the warband roster which), but each may only control one at a time, so only a warband with both a Liche and a Necromancer may ever take two Scarecrows. If the Liche or the Necromancer is for some reason unable to participate in a battle, their Scarecrow will also be unable to participate.

Whenever the scarecrow's controller loses a wound he must pass an unmodified Leadership test or the magical bond is broken and the scarecrow is immediately taken out of action.

rules.title: Hard Head
rules.description: Chaos Dwarfs and Bull Centaurs ignore the special rules for maces, clubs, etc. They are not easy to knock out!

rules.title: Armour
rules.description: Chaos Dwarfs and Bull Centaurs never suffer movement penalties for wearing armour.

rules.title: Hard to Kill
rules.description: Chaos Dwarfs and Bull Centaurs are tough, resilient individuals who can only be taken out of action on a roll of 6 instead of 5-6 when rolling on the Injury chart. Treat a roll of 1-2 as knocked down, 3-5 as stunned, and 6 as out of action.

rules.title: Slavers
rules.description:
One of the main objectives of the Chaos Dwarfs of Mordheim is to get more slaves for their sacrifices and for their tasks. Consequently, the Chaos Dwarfs will never free any slave they capture.

Pick one: Sacrifice them or put them to work. If you sacrifice them, the apprentice sorcerer will get +1 to Experience for each slave sacrificed. If put to work, you force them to help them in their quest for the witchstone; at the end of the game, gain an additional +1 wyrdstone for each working slave; then make a 1D6 roll: On a result of 2 to 6, the captive dies due to overwork, disease, the effects of long exposure to the sorcerer’s stone, or for any other similar reason, and the Chaos Dwarf band may keep the captive’s equipment. On a result of 1, the captive manages to escape, returns to his band with his equipment intact and, in addition, gains an experience bonus of 1D3 (if he is a henchman, simply add 1 to his total).

rules.title: Uncommon
rules.description: Chaos Dwarfs are quite rare in Old World settlements. For this reason, when they make rolls for the acquisition of new recruits in their bands, they have to spend 1.5 times (rounding up) the amount of experience they normally spend for veterancy. Remember that this is not the case for Hobgoblins, a race far more common than that of Chaos Dwarfs. For example, a group of Chaos Dwarf recruits armed with blunderbusses with 4 experience points would require at least 6 experience points to acquire one recruit, 12 to recruit two and so on.

rules.title: Indentured Servants
rules.description: A Chaos Dwarf warband must start with at least 4 Hobgoblins; if it drops below 4 Hobgoblins, you cannot recruit other members until the number of Hobgoblins is increased to four or more.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: A Chaos Dwarf warband may hire the following Hired Swords: Ogre Bodyguard, Pit Fighter, Warlock, Imperial Assassin, and Hobgoblin Scout. They may hire any Hired Sword described as “all may hire,” or allowed by Orc warbands and Chaos warbands. They may never hire Elves of any sort!

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6“ of the Apprentice Sorcerer may use his Leadership when taking Ld tests.

specials.name: Rituals of Chaos
specials.description: Chaos Dwarf spellcasters are wizards and can learn a random spell from the Chaos Dwarf spell list.

specials.name: Skinny
specials.description: Hobgoblins are naturally cowardly creatures that are forced to fight by their Chaos Dwarf masters. As a result, they take damage easily and at the slightest opportunity try to escape from their captors. When making serious injury rolls, a result of 1-3 indicates that they abandon the band.

specials.name: Nobody cares about them
specials.description: Hobgoblins count as half the number of troops if the band has to make a rout check. For example, in a band made of 12 miniatures, if 2 Hobgoblin miniatures and 1 Chaos Dwarf miniature are out of action, the total would be two miniatures out of action (1/2 + 1/2 +1 =2). Also, Hobgoblins cannot be heroes, just reroll the “Lad's got talent” roll.

rules.title: Expert Scroungers
rules.description: The warband may re-roll any one die in the exploration phase and must accept the second result. It may do this whether or not a hero is able to search.

rules.title: Fight Masters' Training
rules.description: A Protagonist and a Sidekick each get +1 Weapon Skill from the Fight Masters' training, now and whenever one is hired later. The bonus is already in their profiles.

rules.title: Townsfolk and Soldiers
rules.description: The troupe may hold any number of Townsfolk and any number of Soldiers, but never more Soldiers than Townsfolk.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any thespian within 6" of the Narrator may use his Leadership for a Leadership test.

specials.name: Expert Swordsman
specials.description: A Fight Master may re-roll any failed roll to hit when he charges. This holds only while he fights with a normal sword or a rapier, not with a double-handed sword or any other weapon.

specials.name: Mob
specials.description: Townsfolk are bought in groups of 2 to 5 and stay within 3" of one another. While two or more of a group are left they are immune to fear.

rules.title: Miragliano
rules.description:
Therefore Miraglean Heroes have a +1 to hit when using crossbows only.

Marksmen get a +1 to hit with any missile weapon they use.

All Miragleans have a deep-seated hatred toward Skaven. This dates back to the red pox outbreak of 1812 when three quarters of the population of the city perished. When fighting Skaven a Miraglean warband will be affected by the rules for hatred towards them. Hired swords are not affected by the Hatred rule.

Hired Swords: Miragleans warband cannot have Skaven Hired Swords.

rules.title: Remas
rules.description:
To represent this, the Remasen player is allowed to re-roll any rout test one time and must abide by the second roll. This only applies when fighting Dark Elves.

Remasen officers are steadfast individuals whose years of training have afforded them excellent leadership. The leadership value of a Remasen captain, champion and young blood are always one point higher regardless of whom they are fighting.

Hired Swords: Remasens warband cannot have Dark Elf Hired Swords.

rules.title: Trantio
rules.description: To represent this a Trantio war band will always start a one-off match with an extra 100 GC and in a Lustrian campaign they will start with an extra 20% GC added to their total.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Captain may use his Leadership characteristic when taking Leadership tests.

specials.name: Cloak & Dagger
specials.description: Duellists are adept at fighting using their billowing cloaks to swirl at an enemy distracting him and warding off blows. The Duellist counts as using a buckler in close combat.

rules.title: Cause Fear
rules.description: All Undead warriors cause Fear.

rules.title: Immune to Psychology
rules.description: All Undead warriors are immune to psychology and never leave combat.

rules.title: No pain
rules.description: All Undead warriors treat a Stunned result as Knocked Down.

rules.title: May not run
rules.description: No Undead warrior may run, but may charge as normal.

rules.title: Immune to poison
rules.description: No Undead warrior is affected by poison.

rules.title: No Brain
rules.description:
Skeletons are not alive, thus they never gain experience.

Note: Tomb Lords don't actually learn new skills, rather they remember the skills they knew when they were alive. Liche Priests and Acolyes are also undead but the have retained a form of living mind and are capable of learning from their experiences.

rules.title: Flammable
rules.description: The Tomb Lord is as dry as tinder and wrapped in bandages soaked in highly flammable resins and preservatives. A hit from a fire-based attack will cause double the normal number of wounds on it.

rules.title: Do not Drink
rules.description: Undead models do not need food and water. However any living animals that accompany the Mummies follow the water rules as normal.

rules.title: Home Ground
rules.description: The Tomb Guardians live in the Necropolises and have no trouble locating the hidden tombs in search of weapons and armour to help them defend their homes. A Tomb Guardian warband always roll one extra dice in the Exploration phase.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: The Tomb Lord is the warband's Leader and follows all the rules for Leaders.

specials.name: Undead
specials.description: The Tomb Lord is undead and follows all rules for the Undead.

specials.name: Undead
specials.description: The Tomb Lord is undead and follows all rules for the Undead.

specials.name: Undead
specials.description: The Tomb Lord is undead and follows all rules for the Undead.

specials.name: Undead (Skeleton Warrior)
specials.description: Skeletons are undead and follow all rules for the Undead.

specials.name: Undead (Tomb Guardian)
specials.description: The Tomb Guards are undead and follow all rules for the Undead.

fighters.name: Tomb Scorpion
fighters.fixed_kit: Scorpions don't use weapons or armour.

specials.name: Living
specials.description: Scorpions are living beings and are affected by Psychology as normal. However as they are small desert creatures they do not need water.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Scorpions are animals and do not gain experience points.

specials.name: Scorpions sting*
specials.description: Scorpions attack using the poisonous sting in their tails. This attack is worked out exactly as if the scorpion was attacking with Black Lotus.

rules.title: Pride in horses
rules.description: A Turjuk leader who owns neither a Riding Horse nor an Arabian Steed has his Leadership reduced by 1.

rules.title: A slave may lead
rules.description: A slave, or the son of a slave, may become the warband's leader.

lists.name: Townsmen Equipment List
lists.note: This list is for Townsmen only.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Emir may use his Leadership for a Leadership test.

specials.name: Field of Scholarship
specials.description:
When the Scholar joins the warband, choose the field he has studied.

Cartography: add or subtract 1 from the D6 when exploring.

Physiology: after all serious injuries have been worked out, one hero may re-roll his result.

Poetry: the warband's leader adds +1 to his Leadership for his first Leadership test of a scenario if the warband won its last battle. For one turn of a scenario, every friendly model within 6" has +1 Weapon Skill and +1 Attack.

Theology: the Scholar serves The One and learns Holy skills.

The Occult: the Scholar is a wizard and casts Lesser Magic.

lists.name: Undead Equipment
lists.note: The following lists are used by Undead warbands to pick their equipment.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any models in the warband within 6" of the Vampire may use his Leadership instead of their own.

fighters.name: Ghouls
fighters.fixed_kit: Ghouls never carry any equipment, apart from a few bones which they use as primitive weapons.

fighters.name: Dire wolves
fighters.fixed_kit: None.

specials.name: Charge
specials.description: Dire Wolves are slavering creatures that overpower their opponents when they charge. Dire Wolves fight with 2 attacks instead of 1 during the turn they charge.

specials.name: Unliving
specials.description: Dire Wolves do not gain experience. You can’t teach an old dog new tricks!

fighters.name: Zombies
fighters.fixed_kit: Zombies may not have any weapons or armour and suffer no penalties for this.

specials.name: No Brain
specials.description: Zombies never gain experience. They do not learn from their mistakes. What did you expect?

rules.title: An Alliance of Inconvenience
rules.description: The warband has two leaders: only Skaven may use the Slum Lord's Leadership, and only Goblins the Goblin Bully's. The warband tests for rout as normal (25% out of action), but takes two rout tests, one for each leader; if one fails, every warrior of his race routs with him. The Warpstone Troll belongs to both sides and routs only when both have.

rules.title: Who'z da Boss!
rules.description:
After a game the warband won, instead of the leader's +1 experience, roll a D6:

D6 | Result
1 | Neither: they were too busy fighting each other to learn anything.
2-3 | Cunning but Brutal!: the Goblin Bully gains it.
4-5 | Sneaky but Stabby!: the Slum Lord gains it.
6 | A rare moment of comradery: both gain +1 experience.

rules.title: Warpstone for Breakfast
rules.description: A Hero may start the campaign with one of these mutations, a leader with two, paying each one's price: Poisonous Bite, Extra Arm, Hulking Brute, Regeneration, Suckers, Elastic Arms, Vestigial Twin or Cloud of Flies. On an advance roll of a double, a warrior may buy one instead.

rules.title: Factional Jealousy
rules.description: A warrior of one race never intercepts a charge meant for a warrior of the other.

rules.title: Glory Hogz
rules.description: Once a battle, if one side has routed, roll 2D6 at the start of your turn: on a double, the routed side rejoins the battle at a random table edge. Warriors taken out of action before that rout don't return, so the returning side is already taking rout tests.

rules.title: Power Grab
rules.description: If one race has more warriors than the other at the start of a game, its warriors have +1 Leadership and the other's -1.

rules.title: Plenty More Where That Came From
rules.description: If one of the two leaders dies, another Hero of his race takes command, with the dead leader's title and special rules (Goblin Bully or Slum Lord), so a new Hero of the new leader's old type may be bought.

rules.title: Jealousy
rules.description: If one leader takes an Academic skill, the other's next skill must be an Academic skill too.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors of his own race within 6" of him may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: One Upmanship
specials.description: The Goblin Bully re-rolls every to-hit roll in a combat the Slum Lord fights in too.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors of his own race within 6" of him may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Sneaky Snark
specials.description: When the Goblin Bully takes an enemy out of action in a combat the Slum Lord fights in too, roll a D6: on a 4+ the Slum Lord stole the kill, and gains its experience.

specials.name: Disgusting
specials.description: A Stinky Git is not affected by poison attacks, and shrugs off any disease on a 4+, tested when he first catches it.

specials.name: Tunnel Rat
specials.description: A Slave Champion may re-roll any characteristic test in a scenario set in the sewers or anywhere else underground.

specials.name: Largely Insignificant
specials.description: Boglars count towards the warband's number of warriors, but not for rout tests: neither for the warband's size nor as warriors lost.

specials.name: Bicker
specials.description: At the start of each turn, roll a D6 for each Boglar within 2" of another and not in close combat: on a 1 he bickers with the other, and does nothing else that turn.

specials.name: Regeneration (Boglar)
specials.description: Whenever an enemy inflicts a wound on a Boglar, roll a D6: on a 5+ the wound is ignored. Not against wounds from fire or fire magic.

fighters.name: Sewer Squig
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Squigs never use or need weapons or armour.

specials.name: Movement
specials.description: A Sewer Squig moves 2D6-1" each turn on land. In water it swims 2D6" each movement phase, which water's penalties don't reduce; it isn't aquatic.

fighters.name: Giant Rat
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Giant Rats never use armour or weapons.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Giant Rats are animals and gain no experience.

fighters.name: Warpstone Troll
fighters.fixed_kit: None. A Warpstone Troll needs no weapons to fight.

specials.name: Regeneration (Warpstone Troll)
specials.description: Whenever an enemy inflicts a wound on a Warpstone Troll, roll a D6: on a 4+ the wound is ignored. Not against wounds from fire or fire magic.

specials.name: Mutates
specials.description: A Warpstone Troll wounded 3 or more times in a game, but not taken out of action, rolls on the Random Mutation chart.

specials.name: Vomit Attack
specials.description: Instead of its normal attacks, a Warpstone Troll may make one vomit attack on an enemy in hand-to-hand combat: it hits automatically at Strength 5 and ignores armour saves.

upgrades.note: A Hero may start the campaign with one, a leader two, and may buy one on an advance's double.
