rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The warband may hire hired swords as if it were a Human Mercenary warband.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Vampire Hunter may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Stake the Vampire!
specials.description: The Vampire Hunter hates Vampires. He must always move towards a Vampire he can see, unless he can shoot, when he may choose.

specials.name: Stake the Vampire!
specials.description: The Vampire Hunter hates Vampires. He must always move towards a Vampire he can see, unless he can shoot, when he may choose.

specials.name: Dagger and Scythe
specials.description: The Priest of Morr may carry only a dagger and a scythe as weapons, and may never wear armour.

specials.name: Loner
specials.description: The Priest of Morr never takes All Alone tests.

specials.name: Funerary Rites
specials.description: The Priest of Morr is not a wizard, but starts with one Funerary Rite rolled at random.

fighters.name: Wolfhound
fighters.fixed_kit: None. A Wolfhound never uses or needs weapons or armour.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Wolfhounds are animals and gain no experience.

specials.name: Fanatical
specials.description: Pilgrims automatically pass every Leadership-based test they take. A Pilgrim may never become the leader.

specials.name: Blunt
specials.description: Pilgrims use no bladed or ranged weapons, only maces, hammers and staffs, and the silver-tip stake.

rules.title: Swabbies
rules.description: The warband's Swabbies are human, and are captured rather than hired, under the Sartosa campaign rules.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: The warband hires Hired Swords and buys other items as a human Mercenary warband does. A warband holding both Dwarfs and Elves pays 20 gold crowns more in upkeep.

rules.title: Swivel Guns are Rare, Matey!
rules.description: The warband may not start a campaign game with a Swivel Gun on its roster. In a one-off game it may buy one for 2D6 gold crowns more.

rules.title: Master Gunners
rules.description: A Gunner may fire and reload a Handgun in the same turn, as the Hunter skill allows, with Handguns only.

rules.title: Succession
rules.description: If the Captain is killed, one of the Mates takes his place, as a Champion does in a Mercenary warband.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any pirate within 6" of the Captain may use his Leadership for any Leadership test.

specials.name: Swivel Guns is Dangerous, Matey!
specials.description: A Gunner carrying the Swivel Gun always counts as an individual and may never be joined by anyone else. Since the warband may hold only one Swivel Gun, the Gunner carrying it is either newly hired or split off from his group, keeping the experience and skills he had.

fighters.name: Boatswain
fighters.fixed_kit: A Rope & Hook, which he may never sell or give away.

specials.name: Expert Riggers
specials.description: A Boatswain may re-roll a failed Initiative test for leaping over a gap, jumping down or making a diving charge, and the test for climbing up or down with a rope.

specials.name: Not Hired
specials.description: Swabbies are not hired: they are captured, under the Sartosa campaign rules.

specials.name: Never Gain Experience
specials.description: Swabbies never gain experience.

specials.name: Rabble
specials.description: Swabbies need not be armed alike: each may carry different equipment, but only from the Swabbie Equipment list. A Swabbie may never use magic or cast a spell.

specials.name: 'Blimey, they got away!'
specials.description: If the warband routs, any Swabbie who has already left the table in an earlier turn escapes for good: remove him from the roster as if he had been killed.

specials.name: 'Don't mind them mates, they ain't true pirates!'
specials.description: Swabbies who are running away or have been taken out of action do not count towards the warband's rout test.

rules.title: Constabulary
rules.description: The patrol represents one constabulary, chosen with its Watch Captain: the City Watch, the River Watch or the Marsh Watch.

rules.title: Black Caps
rules.description: A City Watch patrol may requisition one Watch Carriage with two horses before every battle.

rules.title: Secretariat
rules.description: A River Watch patrol may commandeer a River Boat before the start of every battle.

rules.title: Fenland Striders
rules.description: A Marsh Watch patrol's Heroes and Officers re-roll failed Initiative tests when fighting on causeways, jetties and gangplanks, or crossing a marsh.

rules.title: Jurisdiction
rules.description: An enemy warrior taken out of action in close combat by the patrol is placed under arrest when the Injury chart roll is a natural 6, unless the patrol routed: instead of rolling on the Serious Injury chart, he goes quietly. The equipment of an arrested warrior can't be kept by his warband unless it was impounded under the campaign's objectives, and confiscated items can't be sold or traded.

rules.title: Interrogation
rules.description: Instead of searching for a rare item after a battle, the patrol's leader may interrogate a Hero held under arrest: on a passed Leadership test the patrol gains 1 Campaign Point and the Hero's warband loses 1. Each suspect may be interrogated once.

rules.title: Fanatical
rules.description: A Hero of the Watch who reaches 30 experience becomes a Knight of Purity, and automatically passes every Leadership-based test.

rules.title: Whistling
rules.description: In the recovery phase the patrol may blow its whistles: D3+1 Watch Officers arrive D3 turns later, in a recovery phase, unless the game has ended, and once they arrive the patrol may whistle again. They carry clubs, are deployed within 6" of a random table edge after compulsory moves and charges, and don't count for rout tests.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Watch Captain may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Falconer
specials.description: A Sergeant has the animal handling skill Falconer, so he may use a hunting bird.

specials.name: Scryer
specials.description: The Sleuth may re-roll any roll in close combat; the second result stands. If she wasn't put out of action in the battle, roll two dice for her in the exploration phase and pick either as the result.

specials.name: Hypnotist
specials.description: At the start of the combat phase, the Sleuth may try to entrance one living warrior in base contact who isn't immune to psychology: he must pass a Leadership test or be entranced. An entranced warrior may not attack in close combat, and counts as knocked down when he is attacked. The trance ends when he or the Sleuth is attacked, or when she ends it.

specials.name: Immune to Disease
specials.description: Sewer Jacks are not affected by any disease.

specials.name: Tunnel Rat
specials.description: A Sewer Jack may re-roll any characteristic test in a scenario set in the sewers or anywhere else underground.

rules.title: Excellent Senses
rules.description: A werewolf detects a hidden enemy from twice as far away as other warriors, so twice his Initiative in inches.

rules.title: Secretive
rules.description: The warband may never include a hired sword or dramatis persona who is not of werewolf blood.

rules.title: Regenerate
rules.description: Whenever an enemy wounds a werewolf, roll a D6: on a 4 or more the wound is ignored. A wound caused by fire, including fire magic, by silver or by wolfsbane may not be regenerated.

rules.title: Human Appearance
rules.description: Out of combat a werewolf may look human or wolflike, so for any post-game event, an exploration roll among them, the warband counts as a human warband.

rules.title: Claws and Teeth
rules.description: In battle form a werewolf with no weapon does not count as unarmed, and his claws count as an additional weapon for the extra attack.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any model in the warband within 6" of the Beornwulf may use his Leadership instead of its own.

specials.name: Infectious Bite
specials.description: If a human model is taken out of action by the Beornwulf and survives, he must take a Toughness test at the start of every post-game sequence after the one he was bitten in. For each test he fails he gains +1 Strength, and the moment his Strength reaches 6 he becomes a werewolf and leaves his warband. One dose of wolfsbane makes him pass the next test automatically; two taken at once cure him.

specials.name: Human enough
specials.description: A Weremaeg is in human shape and counts as a human.

specials.name: New Path
specials.description: If a Weremaeg rolls That Lad's Got Talent you may send him off to learn a trade instead of making him a hero. Pay the hire fee of any human hired sword and roll a D6: he is away for that many games, and comes back as that hired sword, under every hired sword rule, upkeep included. He no longer counts as part of the warband except as a hired sword does, and you keep whatever equipment he carried.

specials.name: Animal
specials.description: A Wulfmaeg is in wolf shape and counts as an animal, a wolf, but still earns experience and advances as normal. He fights with claws and teeth and may never carry a weapon, nor armour that needs a hand such as a shield; his armour costs twice as much. A Wulfmaeg hero may carry only equipment with no active use, a lucky charm or a holy relic and the like, where no decision is needed about when to use it.

lists.name: Witch Hunter Equipment
lists.note: The following lists are used by Witch Hunter warbands to pick their equipment.

lists.name: Flagellant Equipment List
lists.note: This list is for Flagellants only.

lists.name: Zealot Equipment List
lists.note: This list is for Zealots only.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Witch Hunter Captain may use his Leadership value when taking Leadership tests.

specials.name: Prayers
specials.description: The Warrior-Priest is a servant of Sigmar and may use the Prayers of Sigmar as detailed in the Magic section and the Warrior-Priest start with one prayer generated at random. In addition the Warrior-Priest may learn a new Prayer instead of a new skill.

specials.name: Fanatical
specials.description: Flagellants are convinced that the end of the world is nigh, and nothing in this world holds any terror for them. Flagellants automatically pass all Leadership-based tests they are required to take. A Flagellant may never become a warband leader.

fighters.name: War hounds
fighters.fixed_kit: Jaws and brutality! War hounds never use or need weapons and armour.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: War hounds are animals and thus do not gain experience.

rules.title: No Metal
rules.description: A Wood Elf may never use a crossbow or a blackpowder weapon.

rules.title: Honourable
rules.description: A Wood Elf may never use drugs or poisons.

rules.title: Native
rules.description: A Wood Elf suffers no movement penalty in woods.

rules.title: Shops
rules.description: Wood Elf Scouts may visit the Wood Elf Village, the Pine Glade and the Yew Glade.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Waywatcher may use his Leadership when taking a Leadership test.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Protector of the Hunt may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Sniper
specials.description: An Elder Scout may shoot while hiding. After the shot roll a D6: on a 5 or more nobody saw where the arrow came from.

specials.name: Camouflage
specials.description: While an Elder Scout is hidden, each enemy model must pass a further Initiative test to spot him.

specials.name: Crossfire
specials.description: If more than one Scout henchman shoots at the same target, they have +1 on the injury roll.

fighters.name: Ivy Ferret
fighters.fixed_kit: None. An Ivy Ferret may carry no weapons or armour.

specials.name: Keeper
specials.description: An Ivy Ferret stays beside its keeper, any Hero of the warband, and moves with him.

specials.name: Running About
specials.description: Nobody may attack an Ivy Ferret directly. For each hit on its keeper roll a D6: on a 6 the Ivy Ferret is hit instead. Once it has been hit and survived it hides for the rest of that combat, and may neither be hit nor attack again.

specials.name: Spirit
specials.description: An Ivy Ferret is a woodland spirit and gains no experience.

specials.name: Poison Teeth
specials.description: An Ivy Ferret's bite counts as coated with black lotus. It may attack in each round its keeper may attack.

rules.title: Hate Dark Elves
rules.description: Every warrior of the warband, hired swords excepted, hates Dark Elves.

rules.title: Excellent Sight
rules.description: Every Elf of the warband spots hidden enemies from twice his Initiative in inches.

rules.title: Unforgiving
rules.description: In multiplayer games the warband may never ally with a warband of a chaotic nature (Possessed, Skaven, Beastmen, Dark Elves and the like).

rules.title: Tolerant
rules.description: The warband may hire any hired sword who isn't chaotic or evil (no Skaven, Possessed, Beastmen, Dark Elves, Undead and the like).

specials.name: Leader
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves of Athel Loren
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Hunt Master may use his Leadership when taking Leadership tests.

specials.name: Sniper
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves of Athel Loren
specials.description: A Waywatcher may shoot while hidden. After he shoots roll a D6: on a 5+ he stays hidden.

specials.name: Camouflage
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves of Athel Loren
specials.description: While a Waywatcher is hidden, every enemy model must pass an extra Initiative test to spot him.

specials.name: Crossfire
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves of Athel Loren
specials.description: When more than one Deepwood Scout shoots at the same target, they have +1 to their injury rolls.

rules.title: Forest Walk
rules.description: Wood elves move through forest and woodland terrain with no penalty.

rules.title: Excellent Sight
rules.description: A wood elf spots a hidden enemy from twice as far away as other warriors, so twice his Initiative in inches.

rules.title: Subtle Nature
rules.description: A wood elf will never use a blackpowder weapon, and will never wear heavy armour of any kind except ithilmar.

rules.title: Clandestine
rules.description: The warband will never hire a hired sword or dramatis persona who is not an elf.

rules.title: Long Lived
rules.description: The first time any wood elf henchman rolls That Lad's Got Talent, re-roll the dice and take the second result, even if it is That Lad's Got Talent again. Any later result of That Lad's Got Talent counts as normal; only the first rolled for each henchmen group is re-rolled.

specials.name: Leader
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves, The Asrai Way-farers
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Way-Warden may use his Leadership for a Leadership test.

specials.name: Beast Empathy
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves, The Asrai Way-farers
specials.description: While the warband holds a Wild Hunter it may buy 0-3 of each beast companion its lists allow. A beast bought this way may use the Wild Hunter's Leadership for a test while it is within 6" of him.

fighters.name: Pathfinder
fighters.fixed_kit: A Pathfinder must always carry a missile weapon.

specials.name: Natural Stealth
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves, The Asrai Way-farers
specials.description: While a Pathfinder is hiding, enemy models suffer -1 to their Initiative for working out whether they detect him.

specials.name: No Missiles or Armour
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves, The Asrai Way-farers
specials.description: A Wardancer may use neither a missile weapon nor armour.

specials.name: Talismanic Tattoos
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves, The Asrai Way-farers
specials.description: A Wardancer has a 6+ armour save that is never modified, and ignores a spell that targets or affects him on a D6 roll of 6.

specials.name: Nimble Fighters
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves, The Asrai Way-farers
specials.description: A Wardancer may always try to parry, whatever weapon he uses. Fighting with a sword he may re-roll a failed parry, as though he carried a buckler and a sword; two swords give him nothing more.

specials.name: Animal
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves, The Asrai Way-farers
specials.description: A Wolfhound is an animal and gains no experience.

specials.name: Beast Companion
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves, The Asrai Way-farers
specials.description: A Wolfhound may only be included while the warband holds a Wild Hunter.

specials.name: Pack Sense
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves, The Asrai Way-farers
specials.description: While one or more wolves are in base contact with the same opponent as the Wild Hunter, a Wolfhound gains +1 to hit that opponent. The bonus does not stack when more than one wolf is in base contact.

specials.name: Animal
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves, The Asrai Way-farers
specials.description: A Wolfhound is an animal and gains no experience.

specials.name: Beast Companion
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves, The Asrai Way-farers
specials.description: A Wolfhound may only be included while the warband holds a Wild Hunter.

specials.name: Pounce
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves, The Asrai Way-farers
specials.description: If a Hunting Cat charges an opponent and hits with both attacks, whether or not it wounds, the target must pass a Strength test or be knocked down. It has no effect on a large target.

specials.name: Barkskin
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves, The Asrai Way-farers
specials.description: A Wood Spirit has a 4+ armour save.

specials.name: Vulnerable to Fire
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves, The Asrai Way-farers
specials.description: A Wood Spirit takes double wounds from a fire attack.

specials.name: Elemental
specials.type: Warband - Wood Elves, The Asrai Way-farers
specials.description: A Wood Spirit gains experience at half rate and may never become a hero.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Warriors within 6" of the Chief may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specials.name: Expert Shot
specials.description: A Bowman ignores cover penalties when he shoots a bow or a long bow.

specials.name: Set Traps
specials.description: A Trapper may set a trap in a turn he does nothing else, and not in one in which he recovered from being knocked down: place a marker touching him. A model, friend or foe, that moves within 2" of the marker rolls a D6, and on a 3+ triggers the trap and takes a Strength 4 hit; the Trapper never triggers his own. If the hit doesn't wound or the trap isn't triggered, the model may finish its move; a model knocked down or stunned is placed 2" from the marker. The marker is removed either way.

fighters.name: Hunting Hound
fighters.fixed_kit: None. Hunting Hounds use no weapons or equipment.

specials.name: Animal
specials.description: Hunting Hounds are animals and gain no experience.

specials.name: Dog Handler
specials.description: A warband may buy no more Hunting Hounds than it has Trappers. While it has more Hounds than Trappers, the spare Hounds may not fight; they may be kept until the Trappers are replaced, and still count towards the warband size for trading and for the maximum.
